name: Bio-UV 2017: Photo(chemo)therapy in skin diseases
description: In this study, the molecular mechanisms of action of photo(chemo)therapy in skin diseases are investigated. The diseases include psoriasis, cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, other lymphoproliferative disorders of the skin, eczema, lichen planus, rurigo/pruritus, polymorphic light eruption, mastocytosis, graft-versus-host disease, vitiligo and other photo(chemo)therapy-responsive diseases. Twenty patients are being enrolled per diagnosis group.

name: BioPersMed Cohort: cardiovascular and metabolic diseases
description: This cohort comprises a huge number of samples and data collected since 2010 and is still ongoing. The aim is to detect biomarkers of patients at risk for cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. The BioPersMed cohort includes the areas: endocrinology & metabolism and cardiology. In the focus of this cohort: e.g. diabetes, fatty liver disease, osteoporosis, cardiovascular diseases. name: Gestational diabetes mellitus cohort / Obstetrics diabetes mellitus cohort
description: The aim of this study was to collect blood samples from pregnant women diagnosed with diabetes receiving obstetric care at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the University Hospital Graz. Gestational diabetes is a condition in which a woman without diabetes develops high blood sugar levels during pregnancy. GMD accounts for approx. 90% cases of diabetes mellitus in pregnancy, while preexisting type 2 diabetes accounts for less than 10% of such cases. This retrospective cohort (5 years of collection - from 2015 until 2019) may be used to address various research questions in the field of obstetrics and diabetes research.

name: HBO Post-Covid: ongoing Covid-19, long Covid-19, hyperbaric oxygen
description: Opportunistic and exploratory pilot study in patients with ongoing or long Covid-19, respectively. Hypothesis: Breaching of chronic inflammatory reaction by cyclic hyperbaric oxygenation (HBO) using 10 sessions (one each working day) at 2,2 ata at a duration of 75 minutes is possible. Besides measurements of oxygen saturation, tissue oxygen tension, spirometry, blood pressure and heart rate, neurological status and subjective assessment by questionnaire and VAS-scale laboratory parameters will be assessed before and after the treatment cycle as well as after 3 months. Samples will be collected from 100 patients at 3 visits (2400 aliquots).

name: Intermittent Fasting Cohort Study: alternate day fasting, intermittent fasting, healthy subjects
description: Intermittent fasting is a dietary regimen by alternating fasting and “feeding” cycles. In addition to caloric restriction only, intermittent fasting seems to activate cell autophagy which potentially increases cellular stress resistance and removes accumulated molecules that are potentially toxic. This cohort study with embedded pilot randomized control-trial investigates the effects of repeating fasting periods in healthy subjects on human physiology, aging process and molecular-cellular processes in humans. We will be able to study long term effects (subjects, who already practise ADF for a defined time period) and short term effects (subjects randomized to the ADF group) of this nutritional intervention.

name: KIWI Collection: fertility treatment, reproductive medicine, in vitro fertilisation

The aim of the study is to establish a database of infertile couples to facilitate scientific approaches to improve the success of fertility treatments.

name: Probiotic dietary Intervention in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome – A Randomized Controlled Trial (ProPCO-RCT): PCOS, probiotics, metformin, RCT, testosterone
description: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a condition characterized by increased male sex hormones, irregular menstrual cycles, infertility, obesity, diabetes and other symptoms and complications. It is usually treated with lifestyle changes, hormonal contraceptives ("the pill") or with metformin, an antidiabetic drug.We want to assess the possibility of treating PCOS with probiotics, as gut bacteria are known to affect hormonal and metabolic functions. For that purpose, we designed this 6-month intervention trial, in which 60 women per group ingest either a probiotic, a placebo or metformin. In the end hormones, sugar metabolism and other PCOS criteria are evaluated.

name: 9853/9854/9856 - ME/CFS Biobank Austria
description: The purpose of the biobank collection “ME/CFS Biobank Austria” is to establish the first Austrian biobank for samples from Myalgic Encephalomyelitis / Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients. A particular focus of our biobank is to collect samples in a way that makes them inter-nationally comparable, in order to harmonize the Austrian ME/CFS Biobank with ME/CFS biobanks in other European countries (currently the United Kingdom, Neth-erlands, Germany). This is of particular importance, as technical differences in sample collection and storage often result in non-comparable or non-reproducible results. By aligning with other European ME/CFS biobanks, we can not only counter this problem but also accelerate international research in the field, ultimately improving patient care. The collected samples will be made available for research projects aimed pri-marily at investigating the cause of ME/CFS, identifying disease-specific markers for reliable diagnosis, and developing therapies. Future research projects may also in-volve the extraction and analysis of genetic material (DNA, RNA) from the collected samples for scientific purposes.

name: LEAD
description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is an important cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide and has a tremendous impact on the individual patient, the healthcare system, and the general public. Contrary to other chronic diseases, the natural history of COPD, commonly described as the natural decline of lung function, has not been investigated sufficiently. Understanding normal lung development and ageing, both in health and disease, and in men and women, is considered a research priority in current respiratory medicine and is essential to properly interpret results of eventual therapeutic interventions. , Therefore, we intend to asses a) the age-related natural decline in lung functions in the general population, b) the prevalence of COPD and the development of major respiratory symptoms in this disease, c) the prevalence of the most important COPD comorbidities (eg. cardiovascular, metabolic and cognitive dysfunction) and d) the association between the natural decline of lung function and socioeconomic status, individual long term exposure to air pollution and other toxic inhalants and comorbidities. , To our knowledge this health examination survey will be the first investigation in Austria providing information about the most prevalent respiratory disease worldwide, its comorbidities and underlying causal factors in a longitudinal approach.

name: Fructose and NAFLD
description: Fructose overconsumption is linked to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and impaired lipid and glucose metabolism which is also associated with increased risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD). Since bile acids (BA) are critical regulators of lipid and energy metabolism, we aimed to explore whether dietary fructose challenge (FC, 150g/day for 4 weeks) may impact on lipid and glucose dysbalance by changing BA metabolism. Further, we aimed to assess the impact of the high oral fructose challenge on hepatic lipid metabolism reflected by total hepatic lipid content (HLC), fatty acid saturation and phosphorous metabolites (PM, indicating hepatic energy metabolism), and glucose homeostasis. Moreover, we aimed to explore the role of LPA as potential biomarker predicting hepatic sensibility to fructose induced (lipo)toxicity. Finally, in animal models fructose overconsumption leads to chronic metabolic low-grade inflammation and was also linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD) as well as development of type-II-Diabetes (T2DM). Until now, the impact of fructose overconsumption is often studied in overweight, T2DM or NAFLD patients, but is not as well described in healthy subjects. To test our hypothesis that fructose overconsumption may impact on the gut-liver axis by increasing intestinal permeability, bacterial translocation, and consecutively metabolic inflammation as important mechanisms in the pathogenesis of NAFLD, CVD and T2DM, we examined the impact of a high oral fructose challenge on intestinal permeability and inflammation.

name: Biobank Antwerpen
description: Biobank Antwerpen is an academic university hospital integrated biobank. Historically this biobank originated from Biobank@UZA which was a tumourbank. Nowadays, it's a collaboration between the University Hospital of Antwerp (UZA) and the University of Antwerp (UAntwerpen). Biobank Antwerpen is also the partner for many other research institutions and companies working with human body material. It contains a broad sample collection, harbouring samples of all active research domains at the university and the hospital. Examples are samples from oncology, pediatrics, immunology, microbiology, neurology etc. Biobank Antwerpen provides samples for all kind of research projects, both academic as (non)-commercial.

name: Geneva Memory Center Biobank
description:
This biobank includes all biological material collected at the Geneva Memory Center at HUG for research on biomarkers and treatment options related to Alzheimer’s disease and other dementia-associated pathologies.
Specifically, it includes samples from the following studies:

1) gMAD: Examines how gut bacteria (microbiota or formerly gut flora), saliva, and blood elements are associated with tau protein and beta-amyloid in the brain.

2) COSCODE: Aims to predict the progression of diseases such as Alzheimer’s by comparing clinical characteristics of patients with Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD), healthy volunteers, and those with diagnosed cognitive disorders.

3) HISTEPPA: Investigates the role of probiotics on biomarkers associated with Alzheimer’s disease.

4) MIPINO: Explores how intestinal bacteria (microbiota) are associated with the progression of idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus.

5) ECL-EPAD and EPAD-LCS: Examines factors involved in the development of dementia caused by Alzheimer’s disease.

name: SAPALDIA cohort study
description:
The SAPALDIA cohort is a population-based multi-center study in eight geographic areas representing the range of environmental, meteorological and socio-demographic conditions in Switzerland. It was initiated in 1991 (SAPALDIA 1) with a follow-up assessment in 2002 (SAPALDIA 2) and 2010 (SAPALDIA3). This study has specifically been designed to investigate longitudinally lung function, respiratory and cardiovascular health; to study and identify the associations of these health indicators with individual long term exposure to air pollution, other toxic inhalants, life style and molecular factors.
At the first follow-up (SAPALDIA2), the disease focus expanded to cardiovascular and metabolic health. To investigate biologic mechanisms and strengthen causal inference via systematic prospective, collection of population-based blood samples started and the SAPALDIA biobank was established (follow-up 1 in 2002). There have been a second (SAPALDIA3 in 2009), a third (SAPALDIA4 in 2017) and a fourth follow-up (SAPALDIA5 in 2021) inviting the same participants for additional data collection including detailed questionnaires, clinical examination and health measures. Repeated blood samples (SAPALDIA2 to SAPALDIA4) were processed and stored and complemented with saliva, urine and stool samples (SAPALDIA4). No blood samples were collected at SAPALDIA5.

name: Liquid Biobank Bern
description:
The Liquid Biobank Bern (LBB) consists of an institutional collection of patients from the Inselspital, Bern University Hospital. Blood samples (Plasma, Serum, DNA) of patients of the Inselspital including the clinical patient data are collected and stored for the future use of research projects.

A high sample quality suitable for omics analysis is achieved by fast track (~1h from needle to freeze), an highly automated and standardized processing, and storage in fully automated robotic stores (at -80°C and N2) by the state-of-the-art infrastructure of the Inselspital, operated by the Center for Laboratory Medicine. The samples are tightly tracked by their barcodes and each time-point (from blood draw to storage) is set by robots/scanners to grant a high data quality.  

The samples are collected specifically for this biobank (no leftover material) to achieve this controlled, standardized fast track processing. This hospital cohort was initiated by the Inselspital to facilitate biomedical research by supplying samples of high quality. The goal is to improve prediction, prevention, diagnosis and therapy in human medicine. With the collected samples and data, underlying mechanisms of diseases can be researched.

name: CELSPAC: TNG (The Next Generation)
description: The Next Generation Study (TNG) is an ongoing population-based longitudinal birth cohort study designed to investigate the determinants of metabolic, immune and developmental disorders in childhood. Complex data on participants' internal and external exposomes and biosamples suitable for multi-omics approaches are collected to study disease aetiology holistically. TNG is a collaborative project between Masaryk University and the University Hospital in Brno, Czech Republic, which was launched with the aim of following 4,000 mother-child pairs. At baseline (26-40 weeks of pregnancy), eligible and consenting women complete a series of self-administered questionnaires assessing their health, psychosocial factors, lifestyle, including diet, and environment. Trained nurses take the women's medical history. They also collect venous blood and urine samples. Cord blood is taken immediately after birth. On the second day after delivery, the nurses take buccal swabs from the mothers and newborns. In addition, a sample of meconium and a dry blood spot are collected from the newborns. All biological samples are aliquoted and stored in the CELSPAC biobank. Finally, details of pregnancy, delivery and birth are transcribed from the medical records. Parent-reported online questionnaires assessing the child's psychomotor development are emailed to the mothers at 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 12, 18, 19, 24, 36, 37, 48, and 60 months. In the future, the TNG dataset will be enriched with data from paediatricians' records and national health registers.

name: PROSECO (Prospective Seroconversion Coronavirus Study) - Phase 1
description: The Prospective Seroconversion Coronavirus Study (PROSECO) provided key data from the highly affected Central European region and contributed to the epidemiological and serological characterisation of SARS-CoV-2 infection. All 30,054 study participants were recruited between October 2020 and March 2021, covering the epidemic peak (November 2020, January and March 2021) of the second COVID-19 epidemic wave. The PROSECO study followed the dynamics of seroconversion of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies in the immunologically naive and unvaccinated population during the COVID-19 pandemic. Study participants were reassessed in the second (April 2021 - September 2021) and third (October 2021 - March 2022) phases to study the post-infection/post-vaccination dynamics of seroconversion in/after a period of massive vaccination. Phase 1 includes COVID-19 epidemic data and samples from the unvaccinated Czech population, collected November 2020-March 2021.

name: FREEZE Comprehensive study on carotid artery plaques using MRI and blood biomarkers
description:
We prospectively recruite patients with asymptomatic 20-80% internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis or patients with symptomatic ICA stenosis <50% and at least one cardiovascular risk factor. We perform multimodal MRI including 4D flow MRI to assess plaque composition, geometry and local hemodynamics. In addition, we measure biomarkers of lipid metabolism and inflammation in blood and perform CHIP analysis. Follow-up will take part 2 years later and we aim to identify predictors of plaque progression and cerebrovascular events.
Head of the collection is Prof. Dr. Andreas Harloff, PI

name: Collection GAIN Freiburg
description:
The German Multi-Organ Autoimmunity Network (GAIN) is an association of physicians and scientists from the universities of Freiburg, Hanover, Munich and Kiel with the aim of researching multi-organ autoimmune diseases. Multi-organ autoimmune diseases are among the very rare diseases and are often caused by monogenic mutations in certain immunoregulatory genes. The GAIN project aims to investigate the pathophysiology and identify new genetic causes. It will also establish a patient registry and a biobank for multi-organ autoimmune diseases. The samples and data collected will be made available to internal and external scientific projects. The analysis of the collected patient samples should provide insights into the function and interaction of the affected genes with the immune system. This is of particular interest to the scientific community, as it may also be applicable to more common diseases of the immune system. By understanding the underlying molecular pathogenic mechanisms, it is hoped to be able to restore the balance of the immune system and thus improve patient care in the long term. An accompanying clinical trial (ABACHAI) for patients with CTLA4 deficiency, who receive a personalised therapy tailored to their mutation, is already leading the way.

description: The German Chronic Kidney Disease (GCKD) study represents a prospective observational national cohort study of patients with CKD in Germany. Central storage of high quality biomaterials is a central component of the study concept to allow establishing associations between biomarkers, patient characteristics and outcomes. The GCKD Study has established a network that combines a central coordinating center in Erlangen with nine regional centers at collaborating academic institutions (Aachen, Berlin, Erlangen, Freiburg, Hannover, Heidelberg, Jena, München and Würzburg). The GCKD-Study is governed by a Steering Committee which is formed by representatives of the coordinating center, each regional center and cooperating institutes. Six members from the Steering Committee have been elected to the Executive Publication Committee to review proposed publications according to the publication policy and to an Ancillary Studies Committee to channel and harmonize ancillary study proposals according to the ancillary studies policy. The GCKD Steering committee must take all decisions about biomaterial utilization. Members of the study consortium can request biomaterials; application forms and processes for evaluation are in place. Biomaterials have already been shared with sites in Germany, Switzerland and the US

NEOCYST is a multicenter, interdisciplinary network of clinicians and scientists exploring early onset cystic kidney diseases. Hereditary cystic kidney diseases are among the most important causes of chronic renal failure in childhood.
The goals of NEOCYSTare to increase the knowledge on the epidemiology, the phenotypical spectrum, the underlying genetic and pathophysiological mechanisms as well as the individual prognosis of early onset cystic kidney diseases and thereby to improve the clinical management and counselling of affected patients.

NEOCYST ist ein multidisziplinäres, multizentrisches Netzwerk zur Erforschung zystischer Nierenerkrankungen des Kindesalters. Es handelt sich um einen Verbund aus Klinikern, Genetikern und Wissenschaftlern, die gemeinsam das Ziel verfolgen, die Betreuung, die Therapie sowie die Lebensqualität von Patienten mit zystischen Nierenerkrankungen zu verbessern.
Erbliche zystische Nierenerkrankungen repräsentieren eine der häufigsten Ursachen eines chronischen Nierenversagens im Kindesalter. Gleichzeitig zählen sie zur Gruppe der „Seltenen Erkrankungen“, so dass nur wenige hundert Patienten in Deutschland betroffen sind. Alle zystischen Nierenerkrankungen zeichnen sich durch ein hohes Maß an phänotypischer wie genetischer Variabilität aus. Zudem erschweren erhebliche Krankheitsüberschneidungen eine frühzeitige Diagnose sowie eine individuelle Beratung betroffener Patienten und deren Familien.

name: Biomarkers for Motoneuron and neurodegenerative diseases (BIO-MNDEG)
description: Motoneuron diseases (MND) are rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disorder that presents with the variable deterioration of the corticospinal tract, brainstem, and spinal anterior horn neurons. MND has increasingly come to be recognized as a “syndrome,” with markedly heterogenous progression rates and pathological courses, despite the existence of clinically well-defined phenotypes; the clinical and pathological overlap with frontotemporal dementia has also rendered the “single system, single disorder” hypothesis tenuous. Advances in modern genetics have led to the identification of over 10 genes linked to the familial form of the disease (fMND); however, the vast majority of cases are sporadic (~90%), with as yet poorly understood etiology. Crucially, there exists no disease-modifying treatment or “cure” for MND, nor any definitive diagnostic test. There is, therefore, an intense need to establish biomarkers that assist with diagnoses, prognostic stratification, and disease activity; of particular value would be biomarkers that are sensitive to the substantial variation in progression rates and can consequently be used to inform therapeutic choices. Knowledge of an individual patient's course at the time of diagnosis would facilitate effective care planning and resource targeting. Given the complexity and heterogeneity of MND, it is unlikely that a single biomarker will be able to accomplish all of the objectives listed above. It is far more plausible that a “multimodal panel” of biomarkers with varying kinetics and specificities for different parts of the disease process will possess clinical utility. Therefore, this repository aims to build a panel of numerous bio-tissues that capture the range of pathogenic processes at play in MND and related neurodegenerative disorders.

name: Systems Medicine of Community Acquired Pneumonia (CAPSyS)
description:
CAPSyS is a sub-study of the PROGRESS study of the Pneumonia Research Network on Genetic Resistance and Susceptibility for the Evolution of Severe Sepsis. The CAPSyS add-on protocol expands the observational, longitudinal case-cohort study PROGRESS by adding sample collection from the upper and lower airways and assessments addressing barrier function in the lung. The CAPSyS protocol is activated in selected study centers and applied to ventilated patients on ICU. Activation of the CAPSyS protocol can commence up to seven days after hospitalization for CAP. Patient's progress is followed in much detail for up to six days after protocol activation. Further data are collected until discharge from the hospital. Patients are followed up on at days 28, 180, and 360. 
Baseline assessment comprises sociodemographic, anamnestic, family history, and live style information. Pneumonia risk stratification scores Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) and CURB-65 are determined upon enrolment. At enrollment and for up to six subsequent study days routine laboratory data, clinical observations, and information on therapy are documented. The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS) status, and organ dysfunction are documented for the same time frame. Starting with enrollment, up to six consecutive sets of biomaterials are collected comprising serum, plasma, and materials for extraction of RNA. Blood for extraction of DNA is collected once. Airway materials (nasal and throat swabs, tracheal secretion, bronchoalveolar lavage) are obtained at protocol activation and tracheal secretion again five days after. Follow up comprises vital status, housing situation, recurrence of pneumonia, and a quality of life questionnaire.
CAPSyS addresses the airway and lung compartment in patients enrolled into the PROGRESS study. The aim is to better understand the lung microbiome and barrier function in CAP patients in regard to patient heterogeneity regarding outcome in the hospital and the development of novel treatment concepts.

name: Hydrocortisone for Prevention of Septic Shock (HYPRESS)
description:
Severe sepsis is a disease with a high mortality. Development of shock is a most serious complication and increases the risk of death considerably. Application of low dose hydrocortisone is currently recommended only in patients after severe septic shock has been established. Hydrocortisone therapy has a hemodynamic stabilizing effect and may reverse shock, however, the preventive application has not been investigated in a larger study. The study investigates whether low dose hydrocortisone prevents the development of shock in patients with severe sepsis. It is postulated that shock prevention may also affect morbidity and mortality.
HYPRESS is a placebo-controlled, randomised, double-blind study to investigate the efficacy and safety of low dose hydrocortisone to prevent the development of septic shock in patients with severe sepsis.

name: Conversion of alpha linolenic acid (KoALA)
description: The KoALA study focuses on the impact of variations in the background diet as a confounding factor. The intake of linoleic acid (LA, C18:2 n-6) has been suggested to diminish the metabolism of α-linolenic acid (ALA, C18:3 n-3) to eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA, C20:5 n-3) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 22:6 n-3. In this context, NuCo Study III will be conducted to evaluate the influence of the background diet, in particular the impact of the simultaneous intake of LA on the conversion of ALA into their long-chain (LC) metabolites, the incorporation of n-3 LC-PUFA in human tissues and their metabolism into eicosanoids and docosanoids. Further, the influence of a regular intake of milk fat, in particular from free-grazing ruminants, on n-3 PUFA metabolism will be investigated, because short- and middle-chain fatty acids as well as the branched-chain fatty acids in milk fat may influence the conversion of ALA into n-3 LC-PUFA (hypothesis). Thus, validated nutrition concepts for increasing n-3 LC-PUFA status from plant sources will be developed.

name: Comparison of Two Antibiotic Regimen (Meropenem Versus Meropenem+Moxifloxacin)in the Treatment of Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock (MAXSEP)
description:
Severe sepsis and septic shock are diseases of infectious origin with a high risk of death. Antibiotic therapy is mandatory but it is unknown whether one antibiotic alone is sufficient for initial therapy. The purpose of this study is to compare a therapy with meropenem alone or the combination of meropenem plus moxifloxacin in the treatment of severe sepsis/ septic shock. Patients randomly receive one of the two treatments for at least 7 days but not longer than 14 days.
MAXSEP is a prospective, randomized, open, multicentre study about the effect of an empirical antibiotic monotherapy with meropenem (Meronem®) versus a combination therapy with moxifloxacin (Avalox®) on organ dysfunction in patients with severe sepsis and septic shock.

description:
Severe sepsis and septic shock are diseases of infectious origin with a high risk of death. The purpose of this study is to determine whether the intravenous application of selenium (given as sodium-selenite) can reduce mortality in patients with severe sepsis or septic shock. Additionally, it is investigated, whether the measurement of procalcitonin - a marker of infection - can be used to guide anti-infectious measures in this disease.

name: Therapeutic drug monitoring-based dose optimisation of piperacillin/tazobactam to improve outcome in patients with sepsis (TARGET)
description: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection with hospital mortality in excess of 40% despite modern supportive care. Along with insufficient and delayed empirical antimicrobial therapy, inappropriate antimicrobial exposure has been identified to negatively affect patient outcomes. Using therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) guided antimicrobial therapy with dosing tailored to the altered pharmacokinetics of the individual patient in combination with continuous infusion may be an appropriate strategy to overcome the problems of under- and overdosing of beta-lactam antibiotics. This current trial will address the question whether a TDM-based treatment approach in patients with sepsis and continuous infusion of piperacillin/tazobactam will result in a greater resolution of organ dysfunction and hence better clinical outcome compared to dosing according to manufacturers’ recommendations.

name: Leibniz-IZW Wildlife Cell and Tissue Cryobank
description:
The Leibniz-IZW Wildlife Cell and Tissue Cryobank is a non-for-profit repository, which collects, processes, stores, and, upon request, also shares viable animal cellular material for genetic rescue, conservation efforts and (stem) cell-based research. 

1) Tissue – for cell culture, genetic studies and basic research
The cryobank contains tissue samples from more than 500 species (approximately 600 taxa), which can be used for the establishment of cell cultures as well as for genetic, physiological, and evolutionary research. In addition, the collection includes approximately 10,000 tissue samples from naked mole-rats originating from both wild populations and the Leibniz-IZW breeding colony.

2) Fibroblast cultures – for generating iPSC
The responsible department establishes and maintains fibroblast cell lines from approximately 350 taxa representing all major vertebrate groups (mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, amphibia). These include numerous threatened species, as well as species that are extinct in the wild, such as the northern white rhinoceros. The collection provides the foundation for generating induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and will be strategically expanded to include key conservation species such as rhinoceroses, elephants, and wolves.

3) Gametes, Embryos, ESC
Since the 1990s, the cryobank group has collected and maintained cryopreserved sperm samples from approximately 100 species. The value of such genetic resource banks has been demonstrated through their successful application in artificial insemination and in vitro fertilization programs for elephants and rhinoceroses.

name: LIFE-Adult-Study Basis Leipzig
description:
The aim of the LIFE Adult Study is to obtain meaningful health data from a broad cross-section of the population, recording the health status and (early) pathological changes of the test subjects. This is a prerequisite for clarifying the heterogeneity of diseases and finding new approaches for early diagnosis and prevention.

The focus is on civilisation diseases such as cardiovascular diseases, metabolic diseases, depression, cognition and brain function, sleep disorders and vigilance regulation, degenerative retinal diseases and allergies.

The LIFE Adult Study is designed as a prospective, longitudinal, population-based cohort study. After extensive preparation and a pilot phase with 400 subjects, the cross-sectional baseline survey was conducted between August 2011 and November 2014 among 10,000 randomly selected adult citizens of Leipzig, Germany, aged 20-79 years.

Each participant was asked to provide a blood and urine sample. A comprehensive immediate laboratory programme was implemented so that around 70 laboratory parameters were available for almost all study participants. In addition, biospecimens (plasma, serum, lymphocytes for DNA, RNA and urine) from more than 9,900 participants were stored at -80 °C and -150 °C respectively.

Each participant underwent an examination programme lasting approximately 5 to 6 hours. In addition, more than 3,000 people from selected age groups underwent a 4-hour EEG programme and more than 2,500 people underwent an MRI programme of the same length.

The examination programme consisted of physical and instrumental examinations, interviews, self-administered questionnaires and psychometric tests.

name: LIFE-CHILD-Study Leipzig
description: LIFE Child is a prospective population-based cohort study in the greater Leipzig area to investigate the molecular causes of environmental and lifestyle-related diseases in childhood and adolescence. To this end, we examine and interview pregnant women from the 24th week of pregnancy and their children in the 3rd, 6th and 12th month of life. We invite children from the age of one and their parents to attend our annual study day. Due to the breadth of recruitment, this study has both a longitudinal and a cross-sectional design. This allows for a variety of evaluation options. The aim of the study is to use the information obtained to determine the multifactorial causes of lifestyle diseases, to identify their risk factors and to understand the mechanisms involved, in order to effectively prevent the development or manifestation of these diseases in the future.

name: LIFE_LONG-COVID-Studie
description:
In order to be able to better treat patients with post-COVID symptoms in the future or, in the best case, to prevent complications, Leipzig University Medicine is researching the after-effects of a SARS-CoV-2 infection. To this end, the Adult Outpatient Clinic of the Research Centre for Civilisation Diseases LIFE at the University of Leipzig is working closely with the Post-COVID University Outpatient Clinic at Leipzig University Hospital and the Network of General Practitioner Teaching Practices at Leipzig University Hospital. The aim of the project is to address the urgent need for clinical characterisation of the post-COVID course in order to develop appropriate diagnostic procedures for the prevention and treatment of post-COVID complications.

To this end, 400 patients who have survived SARS-CoV-2 infection will be systematically examined and interviewed several times according to clinical and epidemiological standards. The programme includes extensive standardised interviews, physical and instrumental examinations. The cohort consists of subjects from the LIFE-ADULT study who already have health data from the period before their COVID illness, patients from the post-COVID university outpatient clinic and patients from the general practitioners' teaching practices at the university medical centre. It is also planned to interview comparison subjects from the LIFE Adult study who do not have SARS-CoV2 disease.  This will make it possible to characterise patients with an initial examination from the past and to map severe disease progression. This approach clearly distinguishes the research project from similar studies.

This provides an important basis for future national and international research projects.

name: UGMLC Giessen Biobank main collection
description:
Next to a large collection of liquid biospecimen (BAL-fluid, EDTA-blood, plasma and serum) from >1000 patients in the field of DPLD (mainly lung fibrosis, sarcoidosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis), PH, ARDS/ALI and pneumonia, the biobank provides a large collection of tissue from explanted lungs and isolated cells. 
Within the last 10 years >900 explanted lungs (fibrosis ~330, PH ~120, COPD ~150, Donors ~170, other entities ~130) have been worked up according to standardized protocols. 
We collect fresh frozen and FFPE lung tissue, pieces of arteries, veins and bronchi, isolate cells (interstitial fibroblasts, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells, adventitial fibroblasts) and generate precision cut lung slices (PCLS). The Biobank-team develops further protocols for isolation of other cell types (vascular endothelial and lung epithelial cells). 
In addition, a collection of biopsied tissue from lung cancer patients has recently been established (tumor, and tumor-free tissue from >110 lungs)

The UGLMC-Gießen Biobank also hosts the biobank of the European IPF registry/European ILD registry (eurIPFreg/eurILDreg) that was funded in frame of the European IPF network (FP7) in 2008 and enrolled >1000 patients with IIPs (idiopathic interstitial pneumonia) so far. The eurIPFreg biomaterial collection comprises the following specimens: BAL, serum, plamsa, EDTA-blood, PAXgene-blood, exhaled breath condensates, electric nose samples, and tissue from transbronchial biopsies or explanted lungs.

description: [NCT04396899] The DZHK BioVAT-HF trial will test the hypothesis that cardiomyocyte implantation via engineered heart muscle (EHM), the proposed investigational medicinal product (IMP; designated "Biological Ventricular Assist Tissue" or BioVAT), results in sustainable remuscularization and biological enhancement of myocardial performance in the failing heart. name: Analyse von zellfreier Tumor DNA bei Patienten mit Plattenepithelkarzinomen des Kopf-Hals Bereichs
description: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the sixth most common cancer worldwide, with approximately 140,000 new cases per year in Europe. The prognosis of locally advanced HNSCC is limited despite intensive multimodal therapy, with disease-free survival <60% at 3 years and 5-year overall survival rates for unresectable tumours of approximately 20%. Response to therapy is assessed solely by imaging. A molecular biomarker to measure disease burden and/or response control is not available. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), which can be detected in the blood plasma of cancer patients, is a non-invasive tumour-specific biomarker that is currently the subject of intensive research. Circulating tumour DNA consists of small DNA fragments that are shed by tumour cells and can be detected in a patient's blood or other body fluids.

description: Heart muscle tissue cannot repair itself after damage. In both adults and children, heart muscle weakness is a common disease that is difficult to treat. At the Institute of Pharmacology and Toxicology, we construct replacement heart muscles from stem cells for individualised heart repair in cases of heart muscle weakness and test them for therapeutic suitability. Artificial tissue systems, such as heart muscle, skeletal muscle, neural networks and liver tissue, are being developed and used at our Institute to better predict adverse drug effects prior to first clinical application, thereby significantly improving overall drug safety.

name: Prehabilitation "Karl-Heinz" with a Focus on Cardiac and Cognitive Functions prior to Interventions on the Heart: an Analysis of the State of Health
description:
[DRKS00030526] The evidence for the effectiveness of phase II rehabilitation for patients after cardiovascular interventions and operations is sufficient. Especially elderly and multimorbid patients seem to benefit most from follow-up rehabilitation. The primary rehabilitation goals of this patient group are to restore and secure participation in everyday life and to avoid the need for long-term care.
Until now, patients have only had the option of rehabilitation after cardiac intervention. In order to achieve the above-mentioned goals in the best possible way, prehabilitation before elective intervention is becoming more and more important. The basic idea of prehabilitation is to improve physical and mental performance in advance of a planned intervention through multi-modal preoperative interventions in order to achieve the highest possible level of functional capacity and recovery afterwards.
Current reviews show that not only rehabilitation, but especially preparation for cardiac intervention in the context of prehabilitation can improve the perioperative outcome and alleviate negative effects. Participation in prehabilitation before elective cardiac procedures was associated with a pre- and postoperative increase in functional capacity as measured by 6-minute walk distance, reduced extubation time, lower risk of postoperative pulmonary complications and reduced hospital length of stay.
Other randomized controlled trials of cardiac prehabilitation show positive effects in terms of delirium rate, quality of life, length of stay in intensive care unit, and improved compliance with postoperative rehabilitation with good safety.
Pre- and perioperative psychological interventions in cardiac interventions additionally led to a reduction in length of stay and an increase in self-efficacy.
The innovative concept of prehabilitation was developed to increase patients' functioning in the perioperative period, reduce postoperative morbidity and improve recovery. This study serves to evaluate the concept.

name: Pre-surgery Optimization of Patient’s Expectations to improve Outcome in Heart Surgery
description: [DRKS00016793] The aim of the PSY-HEART II study is to examine whether a preoperative psychological intervention targeting patients' expectations (EXPECT) is capable of improving long-term outcome after coronary artery bypass graft surgery with or without heart valve replacement compared to Standard of Care (SOC) and an attention control intervention. In a 3-arm multi-center randomized, controlled, prospective trial (RCT) N=567 patients scheduled for heart surgery will be randomized to either a psychological preoperative intervention to optimize expectations (EXPECT); or a psychological control intervention focusing on emotional support and general advice, but not on expectations (SUPPORT); or to standard medical care/standard of care /SOC) only. Patients will be randomized with a fixed unbalanced ratio of 3:3:1 (EXPECT:SUPPORT:SOC) to compare EXPECT to SOC and EXPECT to SUPPORT. Both psychological interventions consist of 2 in-person sessions (à 50 min) and 2 phone consultations (à 20 min) during the week prior to surgery, and one booster session post-surgery (around 6 weeks later). The 4 assessment will take place at baseline (approx. 10 days before surgery), preoperative assessment (-1 day before surgery), approx. 4-6 after surgery and 6 months after surgery. Primary endpoint of the study will be patients’ disability scores 6 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes will be patients’ expectations, subjective illness beliefs, quality of life, anxiety and depression, physical activity, cardiac anxiety, optimism, pain, beliefs about medicine, rehospitalization, adverse events, left ventricular ejection fraction, treatment satisfaction, manipulation check, expected working ability and blood samples (e.g., catecholamines, cortisol, IL-6, IL-10, CRP). A multi-center trial with a large sample size is needed to generalize the results (and to review the promising results of PsyHeart I) and its implications for health care systems, and to better understand the pathways of action and implications for different clinical outcomes.

name: DZHK Effect of Anti-Fibrotic Therapy on Regression of Myocardial Fibrosis after Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) in Aortic Stenosis Patients with High Fibrotic Burden
description: [NCT05230901; EudraCT: 2019-004244-29] The aim of the study is to evaluate the effect of antifibrotic therapy on regression of myocardial fibrosis after TAVI in patients with baseline high fibrotic burden. Therefore, patients will be treated with Spironolactone in addition to standard of care, Spioronolactone + Dihydralazine in addition to standard of care or according to standard of care alone without any study medication. First, differences between patients in the control arm and patients randomized to anti-fibrotic therapy will be analyzed. The second analysis will determine, whether dihydralazine medication in addition to spironolactone is able to increase a potential antifibrotic effect. Myocardial fibrosis will be assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) before TAVI and 1 year after. Quantification of potentially irreversible replacement fibrosis will be carried out by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), and quantification of the potentially reversible diffuse interstitial fibrosis will be performed by measurement of the extracellular volume fraction (ECV), thereby deriving matrix volume and cell volume.

description:
Multicenter prospective collection of deep-frozen tissue and blood samples of adult patients with glioma. 
From 2004 to 2012, the German Cancer Aid funded the German Glioma Network (GGN), a nationwide alliance of university hospitals and reference centers specializing in neuro-oncology, neuroradiology, neuropathology, molecular diagnostics, and biometry. A major achievement was the establishment of one of the world’s largest integrated brain tumor databases and biobanks, linking centrally stored tumor tissue with detailed clinical data and molecular genetic analyses. name: BiDirect-Studie („Establishing the links between subclinical arteriosclerosis and depression“)
description:
BiDirect integrates three cohorts into one study design to prospectively investigate the relationship between subclinical atherosclerosis and depression. The cohorts were comprehensively analysed four times during the study period 2010-2021 using identical methods and examination procedures. Cohort 1 recruited patients who had been hospitalised for a depressive episode in psychiatric clinics. Cohort 2 included patients from cardiac rehabilitation centres approximately 3 months after acute coronary syndrome. Cohort 3 was randomly selected and invited from the residents' registration office of the city of Münster and serves as a population control for the two patient cohorts. A total of 2259 subjects were included in the study, with an initial age range of 35-65 years in all three cohorts.

The comprehensive examinations included a medical interview, clinical-apparative diagnostics (including anthropometry + BIA, IMT, arterial flow velocities), detailed depression diagnostics and neuropsychological tests, various scales of quality of life, sleep, life situation and emotional function, as well as a 3T MRI of the brain. 
Biomaterials (serum, plasma) were collected at all examination times. Numerous biomarkers were measured, in some cases repeatedly (at different follow-ups), and a GWAS dataset, epigenetics, RNA sequencing and telomere length were analysed.

name: Prospective Cardiovascular Münster-Study II
description:
Recruitment and examination of employees in > 50 medium and large companies and public authorities in NRW, including 9302 men (mean age 43.1 years) and 8010 women (41.6 years) as part of a screening programme for cardiovascular disease. Voluntary participation took place during working hours by agreement with the employer, and the examination was carried out in a specially equipped bus at or outside the company premises or at the premises of the local occupational health service. The baseline interview and examination took place in 2000-2007 and lasted only about 30 minutes. A follow-up examination of the part of the participants with genotyping (N = 9,484) was carried out by postal questionnaire in 2021.
The baseline examination included sociodemographics, medication use, questionnaires on angina pectoris, PAD, medical diagnoses (lifetime prevalence) for hypertension, gout, rheumatism, bronchitis, myocardial infarction, stroke, kidney disease, family history of the above diseases, cardiovascular risk factors, and female contraceptive use.
Many laboratory parameters have already been determined. The biospecimens will also be made available as a 'control cohort'.

During the transfer of the health data and/or biological material, adata release form will be signed. description: The Control Sample Collection provides biological samples from pediatric donors and patients with mild conditions—encompassing a range of sexes and ages—obtained during minor, routine medical interventions or as surplus material from clinical care processes. name: CRC Eye Tracking Dataset
description: In digital pathology, advancements by the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are enabled, which are based on well-defined clinical data collected via decisions of medical experts. In this forward-looking process, the question of how exactly these experts make their decisions remains open. Which areas in the image are examined by a pathologist while making medical assessments. For a deeper understanding of this process, we collected a dataset of Eye-Tracking and navigation coordinates, classification assessments and confidence-assessments by pathologists. The dataset is based on a cohort of digital scanned histopathological slides (WSIs) of confirmed colorectal cancer cases (CRC). Our dataset consists of extensive annotations (mucosa and submucosa) from 533 WSIs and 6361 annotated gland images (dysplastic and non-dysplastic). Furthermore, Eye-Tracking data, classification decisions and confidence assessments from 12 pathologists, while they assessed the gland images, as well as 90 Eye-Tracking recordings, collected during the diagnostic process for 14 different WSIs. Together with the detailed-medical information of the CRC-cohort our dataset closes the gap between full-case medical data and the observation behavior of the treating medical experts in digital pathology.

name: The John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre Biobank
description: The John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre (JWMDRC) is dedicated to translational research in genetic neuromuscular diseases, aiming to improve health outcomes for individuals living with these conditions. Its work focuses on identifying novel disease-causing genes and exploring the molecular and cellular mechanisms that drive muscle degeneration and weakness in affected patients. Central to this effort is the Biobank - the centre’s specialised biorepository, which houses a collection of well-characterised, high-quality biospecimens donated by individuals with genetic neuromuscular conditions. Since its establishment in 2008, the Biobank has amassed over 21,000 anonymised specimens and has supported more than 250 academic and industry researchers globally, distributing over 20,000 vials to accelerate discovery and therapeutic development. It is represented by Professor Volker Straub - Director of the John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre at Newcastle University.

name: Auria EDTA blood samples
description: The EDTA collection is the largest blood sample based cohort of Auria Biobank. The objective is to take a 10 ml EDTA blood sample from every patient who has given their consent to Auria Biobank. Whole blood, plasma, buffy coat or DNA are available from these samples. Along with the current collection procedure, the sample is centrifuged, after which the plasma is divided into two units of 475 Âµl and the whole blood into two units of 400 Âµl. The samples are stored at a temperature of -80Â°C. Some of the whole blood samples that are collected due to the given biobank consent, are selected for DNA extraction. Hence the DNA is extracted from fresh blood and DNA concentration and purity of the samples are measured. DNA can also be extracted from deep-frozen blood samples. The samples are stored at a temperature of -80Â°C.

name: ATBC, Lung Cancer Prevention Study
description: The ATBC study conducted between1984-1993 in Finland had nearly 29 000 middle-aged male participants. Available research material contains GWAS data currently from > 9000 participants and extensive amount of self-reported data, dietary information, physical and laboratory measurements. Samples include DNA (~17 000), and limited amount of serum. The Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene (ATBC) Lung Cancer Prevention Study was a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial testing whether alpha-tocopherol and/or beta-carotene supplements can reduce the incidence of lung cancer and other cancers. The participants received daily active supplements or placebo capsules for 5 to 8 years (median 6.1 years). All participants were smokers. The study was conducted in collaboration with the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) and the U.S. National Cancer Institute (NCI) and itis still one of the largest lung cancer chemoprevention trials worldwide.

name: Botnia Study
description: The Botnia Study aims at characterizing the genetic and environmental factors predisposing to diabetes and its complications. It is one of the largest diabetes family studies in the world, initiated in 1990 on the western coast of Finland in the Gulf of Bothnia. A total of 15,200 participants are part of the Botnia study hosted by THL Biobank. For these individuals, DNA (and for a subset serum and plasma) samples, as well as physical and laboratory measurements, lifestyle and disease history information related to diabetes have been collected.  Two main substudies fit under the umbrella of the Botnia Study: (1) The Botnia Family Study, which includes individuals diagnosed with diabetes and unaffected family members; and (2) The Prevalence, Prediction and Prevention of Diabetes (PPP) Study, which recruited random individuals aged 18 to 75 years old from Western Finland. Genome-wide SNP data (array genotypes and imputed GWAS) are available for a total of 14,400 individuals.

name: Corogene Study
description: Corogene study includes over 5000 patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and other related heart diseases, such as heart failure and aortic valve disease. All patients (aged 65.6 ±11.1 years) had been assigned for coronary angiogram at the Helsinki University Central hospital during 2006 to March 2008, when they also participated in the study. DNA and GWAS data are available from THL Biobank for almost all participants. The data include physiological measurements, basic lipid and CRP values as well as information on smoking. The objective of the study was to understand risk factors affecting the development and degree of heart diseases. Research was conducted by Helsinki University Hospital (HUS) in collaboration with University of Helsinki and National Institute for Health and Welfare (THL).

name: FinHealth 2017 Study
description: A health and well-being survey study that involved 6650 randomly selected donors from the adult Finnish population. The data include GWAS and NMR metabolomics data, physical and laboratory measurements as well as extensive amount of self-reported data on lifestyle and health. High-quality DNA, plasma and serum samples collected by the well-defined protocol are also available. The new format of the survey conducted in 2017 combined the two major populations health monitoring surveys of the Finnish Institute for health and Welfare (THL), the Health 2000/2011 and FINRISK surveys, to produce up-to-date information on the health, health behavior, functioning and well-being of adults living in Finland in 2017.

name: Fin-HIT Study
description: The Finnish Health in Teens Study (Fin-HIT) is a follow-up study from childhood to early adulthood that focuses on the causal relationships between genetic and various lifestyle factors that affect weight and health. Material currently available for biobank research contains > 3000 DNA samples extracted from the saliva samples of 9-12 y old children and their parents as well as selected data on diet, physical activity, body image, sleep and screen time. The follow-up study has been done in three phases; the baseline study in 2011-2014, first follow-up in 2015-2016 and second follow-up in 2020 as the donors entered adulthood. More samples and data will gradually be transferred to THL Biobank when released from the use of the original study. The ongoing study is conducted by the Folkhälsan Research Center, Helsinki, Finland.

name: Finnish IPF Study
description: The Finnish IPF cohort includes patients with confirmed diagnosis of idiopatic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a progressive lung disease. Currently, DNA and GWAS data from over 300 patients, as well as serum and PBMCs from the subset of patients are available for biobank research via THL Biobank. The Finnish IPF study is a national clinical trial of IPF patients launched at the Helsinki University Central Hospital in 2012. The aim of the ongoing study is to study and monitor the prognosis and course of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in a standardized manner, and to investigate the incidence of the disease in Finland. The participants were originally identified from the hospital registers by ICD-10 diagnosis code J84.1 1 (other interstitial pulmonary diseases with fibrosis) and J84.9 (interstitial pulmonary disease). All included patients meet the ATS/ERS statement´s diagnostic criteria for IPF (Raghu et al, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2011;183:788–824).

name: The National FINRISK Study
description: The National FINRISK Study has been conducted every 5 years during 1972-2012, to assess the risk factors of chronic diseases (e.g. CVD, diabetes, obesity, cancer) and health behavior in the working age population.  THL Biobank hosts samples and data from approx. 35000 participants, from survey years 1992-2012.  Data and samples were collected for this cross-sectional population survey at a baseline visit. The data includes background information on socioeconomic status, medical history, smoking, diet, physical activity, as well as information from the health examination, such as blood pressure, height and weight. A large spectrum of laboratory measurements from serum and plasma samples is available, including NMR metabolomics. Available genomics data include GWAS (array and imputed genotypes, N>31,000), whole exome sequences (N>12,000), and whole genome sequences (N>5000). FINRISK 2007 includes two follow-up studies: DILGOM 2007 and DILGOM 2014, focused on metabolic diseases.

name: THL Psychiatric Family Collections
description: Research cohort includes patients diagnosed with bipolar spectrum disorders (BPD), schizophrenia (SZ) or schizoaffective disorder (FSZ) and their family members. The data consist of a wide range of phenotypes, neurocognitive tests as well as GWAS from almost 4000 participants and WES data from 385 sample donors. DNA and B-lymphocyte cell lines (subset) are also available. The BPD family collection include 180 families with patients who were born between 1940 and 1969, had onset of disease before the age of 30, and had two or more hospital admissions due to BPD. The schizophrenia collection consists of 734 families with one or more family member diagnosed with SZ or FSZ. In this collection, patients were born between 1940 and 1976. THL Biobank has restricted the sample and data use of Psychiatric Family Collections to concern only research of psychiatric disorders.

name: FUSION Study
description: The FUSION (Finland-United States Investigation of NIDDM Genetics) study was launched in 1994 to investigate the genetic basis of type 2 diabetes and diabetes-related traits, including glucose, insulin, and lipid levels, and obesity. The research cohort consists of two main phases, FUSION1 and FUSION 2 (includes D2D study), and one sub-study FUSBIOPS. The FUSION collection in THL Biobank contains DNA samples and data from almost 15 000 Finnish participants, thus providing an ideal basis for genetic studies. In addition, fibroblasts and skin biopsies are available from a subset. FUSION data that will be gradually available through the biobank includes information about physical measurements and lifestyle, self-reported information about diseases and medication, as well as biological measurements from the samples. GWAS data is expected to become available by 2025.

name: GeneRISK Study
description: The GeneRISK Study is a prospective observational study with focus on determining genetic risk factors of cardiovascular diseases and utilization of genetic and traditional risk factor information in disease prevention. Baseline samples were collected in 2015-2018, and the follow-up is still ongoing. High-quality DNA, plasma and serum samples are available from THL Biobank to over 7300 sample donors aged 45-64 years. From the baseline THL Biobank can also provide extensive health and lifestyle data collected through health examinations, interviews and questionnaires and genome-wide SNP data (GWAS). The main goal of the GeneRISK Study is to communicate risk personal risk information directly to the study participants and monitor the effect in possible disease outcomes.

name: Health 2000 and 2011 Surveys
description: A comprehensive 10-year follow-up survey of the Finnish population containing total of 8600 sample donors recruited in 2000 and 2011. The research material available in biobank consists of extensive health data, large-scale omics data (GWAS, WES, WGS, telomeres, NMR metabolomics), and high-quality DNA, serum, and plasma samples. Almost 8000 donors participated in the population survey in 2000 (of those, 1000 individuals also participated in Mini-Finland survey 20 years earlier during 1978-1980). In 2011, an extensive 10-year follow-up data and samples were collected from 4200 previous participants and approximately 800 new donors. The available longitudinal data consists of health examination, cognitive test results, interview and questionnaire data, physical and laboratory measurements, and NMR metabolomics data. Longitudinal samples of serum, plasma and DNA were collected by a well-defined protocol and are available in THL Biobank for research projects.

name: Helsinki Heart Study
description: Samples and data of 4000 middle-aged men (40 to 55 y), collected as part of the five-year clinical trial to test whether the cholesterol-lowering drug Gemfibrozil could reduce the risk of coronary heart disease. All participants had primary dyslipidemia but no previous major illness or coronary heart disease. DNA and GWAS data are available from more than 3500 participants. Data also contains physical and laboratory measurements and questionnaire data on health and lifestyle. The randomized, double-blinded and placebo-controlled trial was conducted during 1981-1990 by KTL, a predecessor to Finnish Institute of Health and Welfare (THL). Due to current high age of the donors, an extensive amount of longitudinal register data can be combined with the research material by the separate permission of the national registry authority, Findata.

name: Mini-Finland Survey (Finnish Mobile Clinic)
description: Mini-Finland Study's purpose was to create the foundations for a national health monitoring system in Finland. The aim was to conduct versatile and reliable research about population health, need for treatment, and functional capacity. Focus areas included common chronic diseases, i.e. diseases of the circulatory, respiratory and musculoskeletal systems as well as mental disorders. The study was conducted in 40 areas across the country, targeting a sample of 8 000 Finns aged 30 years and over, and it was third main phase of Finnish Mobile Clinic Health Examination Survey. Even in the 2000's the Mini-Finland Study can still be considered a pioneer in Europe in terms of the development of health monitoring systems.

name: Migraine Study
description: One of the largest family collections of migraine research consisting of almost 10 000 participants. The genetic data in THL Biobank includes GWAS data from over 8400 sample donors, WES data from 490 donors and WGS data from more than 600 donors. The DNA samples of the study have been collected since 1992 as part of research collaboration between Helsinki University and Helsinki University Central Hospital. The study includes sample donors diagnosed with migraine and their family-members and aims to detect variation in genes associated with migraine, headache-related symptoms and chronic disease risk factors. The research is still ongoing and new study participants are recruited.

name: Finnish SUPER Study
description: The SUPER Study cohort is a collection of over 9000 Finnish patients diagnosed with psychotic illnesses with ICD-10 diagnostic codes F20-F29, F30.2, F31.2, F31.5, F32.3 and F33.3. The currently available research material in the biobank includes GWAS genomic data (>9000), diagnostic information, medication data and basic information (height, weight, smoking). High-quality DNA, plasma and serum are available from all participants. The Finnish SUPER study is a part of the international Stanley Global Neuropsychiatric Genomics Initiative and was collected during 2015-2018 in Finland. The objective of the still ongoing study is to obtain information on the genetic and biological background of psychotic disorders and promote development of therapeutic interventions. PBMC samples and an extensive amount of data collected by health examinations, interviews and questionnaires will also be gradually available in THL Biobank when released from the original study of the University of Helsinki.

name: THL Diabetes Studies
description: THL Diabetes cohort is a combination of several diabetes studies conducted in Finland between 1986 and 2013. The cohort consists of samples and data (including GWAS from > 10 000 participants) from more than 13 500 young donors with type 1 diabetes and from their family members. The material includes DNA (and GWAS data) from most of the donors and plasma/serum and mononuclear cells from the subsets.

description: The Twin study is a large research collection of data and samples from Finnish twins. Biological samples have been collected between 1994 and 2017 in the several sub-studies that recruited participants from the base cohort. The data collected in the sub-studies include physiological measurements, laboratory measurements and other omics data that will also made gradually available through THL Biobank.

name: Finnish Maternity Cohort
description: The Finnish Maternity Cohort (FMC) is a unique, accessible biobank collection for epidemiological, biomarker, and surveillance studies. It contains over 2 million serum samples (2,059,000) from 993 000 pregnant women at first trimester. The population-based cohort is collected nationwide and covers over 90% of women in Finland who have been pregnant between 1983-2016. The samples were collected at local maternity care units for routine screening for congenital infections and the remaining samples (1-3 mL) were stored at -25°C for scientific research. For women with multiple pregnancies, serial prediagnostic samples are available. Moreover, there are approximately 100,000 pairs of mothers and daughters, who both have donated sera to the FMC for scientific research. Personal identification codes enable linkage with the nationwide, population-based health registries (such as Finnish Cancer Registry and Medical Birth Register) and establish a unique study base for longitudinal studies.

name: FCBT Blood Samples Collection
description: The blood sample collection includes EDTA whole blood, EDTA plasma and serum samples. Blood samples have been collected from 2016 to 2025 from about 53,000 different individuals.Of the EDTA whole blood samples, some are assorted for DNA extraction. DNA is extracted from a frozen sample and there are currently extracted DNA samples from about 37,000 individuals. From extracted DNA samples there exists a storage tube (volume 270-320 µl), whose DNA concentration may vary. In addition, there are 1-3 normalized aliquot tubes (50 µg/µl) with volumes ranging from 80 to 500 µl. Some of the EDTA whole blood samples (N=13000) have been preserved as whole blood, with volume ranging 800-2700 µl. Serum and plasma samples have been collected using the cold chain, i.e. stored and processed at +4 °C from collection to storage. All samples are first stored at -75 °C and long-term storage occurs in liquid nitrogen tanks (-196 °C).

name: FCBT Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples Collection
description: The Cerebrospinal fluid (CFS) collection includes CSF samples collected during diagnostics and serum samples (matching serums) taken at the same sampling time. In the collection, there are currently CSF samples from  over 600 different individuals and  matched serum samples from  1 500 different individuals. CFS samples accumulate in the biobank from about 15 individuals and serum samples from about 35 individuals per month. After sampling, the samples are frozen and stored at -75 °C. In the biobank, samples are thawed and centrifuged at + 4 °C, and the supernatant are divided into aliquots (volume 200-450 µl). The aliquots are re-frozen and stored at -75 °C. The sample collection was initiated in September 2021 and is still ongoing.

name: FCBT Fresh Frozen Tissue Samples Collection
description: High-quality collection of fresh frozen tissue samples of different types of cancer, preserved by instant freezing fresh in isopentane and then under controlled conditions at -75 °C. The cold ischemia time of samples is routinely monitored and representativeness of the samples is verified by the pathologist. The four most represented disease groups are: Urological cancer, breast cancer, gastrological cancer, gynecological cancer. CtDNA samples (N=2 800) are plasma samples collected from cancer patients during the collection of fresh frozen tissue samples. ctDNA samples have been collected before surgery, with the somatic mutations and epigenetic changes characteristic of the cancer still remaining in the patient's blood. In addition to plasma, buffycoat and red blood cell fraction are segregated from the samples.

name: FCBT FFPE Tissue Samples Collection
description: The sample collection contains a large number of histological samples collected at Tampere University Hospital since 1963.The collection contains tumor samples taken or removed in connection with tumor diagnostics and cancer. In addition, the sample material exhibits various precancerous changes, inflammatory changes, reactive changes, and tissue samples belonging to normal variation. Histological specimens have mainly been treated with formalin and cast in paraffin (FFPE). The collection includes FFPE tissue samples from more than 400,000 individuals, forming a collection of more than 3.4 million diagnostic tissue samples. Of the samples, c. 8% (N=270,000) are cancer samples. FFPE samples are stored in a dry environment at room temperature in compliance with the diagnostics requirements of Fimlab Laboratories Pathology Unit.

name: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966
description: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 (NFBC1966) is a prospective birth cohort initiated in the 1960s to examine risk factors involved in pre-term birth and intrauterine growth retardation, and the consequences on subsequent morbidity.
