name: BAVL25 Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell biobank for immunology research
description:
PBMC collection occurs in many different studies which all have been previously approved by the METC (or the RvB in some rare cases). This biobank application covers for the generation of one large PBMC biobank based on all these studies. The current list of studies (which may be expanded over time):

N03LAM, N10TIL, M14TIL, N11RFA, N12INT, M11TCR, N12LON, N14ITO, N14IMR, M12PCA, N14OPC, M14PRT, N14MPN, N15TON, N14HPV, N12LAR, M11CIR, N15HTC, N15TCH, N15IMP, N19RNA, N17DTI, M16COW

Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) can be isolated from the blood and consist of many different types of immune cells. After PBMC isolation the immune cells can be studied; e.g. the ratio of different immune cell subsets, or the expression of certain surface molecules on these cells, or the specificity of the cells (in the case of T-cells) can be determined. These analyses are often performed using flowcytometry.
Many different intervention clinical trials study the response of immune cells to treatment over time by taking regular blood samples. In addition, there are a number of trials which are not designed to test the effect of a (drug) intervention, but purely to follow the immune responses. In these trials, blood is also taken from the patient for PBMC isolation, but no further interventions are performed.
In all cases peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) are isolated from the blood of patients. These cells contain the most important immune cells that can be studied. These PBMCs are then frozen and can be used for subsequent research. 
The proposed PBMC biobank will consist of all these PBMC isolations resulting from separate studies. It is important to work with one biobank code, instead of a separate biobank code for each independent trial in which PBMCs are isolated, because over time patients are often included in multiple studies; using one biobank code for PBMCs ensures that it is easy to trace all PBMC samples of the patient over time and not just the samples of when the patient was in study x or y (eg patients can be included in a drug intervention study and at the same time be included in the N03LAM general material sampling study or a patient can fail in one study and then be included in the next study). In some cases there is a sample taken from the patient at the end of study x, which can nicely be used as a pre-treatment sample for study y. Using separate biobank codes for separate studies it will be much more difficult to find this out.

name: BAVL26 Wholeblood biobank for immunology research
description:
Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) can be isolated from the blood and consist of many different types of immune cells. After PBMC isolation the immune cells can be studied; e.g. the ratio of different immune cell subsets, or the expression of certain surface molecules on these cells, or the specificity of the cells (in the case of T-cells) can be determined. 
In parallel to PBMC isolation, 2 x 0.5 ml wholeblood is isolated from each sample as well. The wholeblood can be used for DNA isolation, for example to determine the HLA-subtype of the patient (a parameter often needed for immunological analyses). By isolating DNA from the wholeblood, PBMCs can be ‘saved’ for the actual immunological assays. This biobank application applies for biobanking of the wholeblood. The biobanking of the PBMCs is arranged in a separate application.
Many different intervention clinical trials study the response of immune cells to treatment over time by taking regular blood samples. In addition, there are a number of trials which are not designed to test the effect of a (drug) intervention, but purely to follow the immune responses. In these trials, blood is also taken from the patient for PBMC/wholeblood isolation, but no further interventions are performed.
In all cases peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) are isolated from the blood of patients and thus wholeblood is also isolated from the same samples (as part of the lab protocol). 
The proposed wholeblood immunology biobank will consist of all these wholeblood isolations resulting from separate studies. It is important to work with one biobank code, instead of a separate biobank code for each independent trial in which PBMCs and thus wholeblood is isolated, because over time patients are often included in multiple studies; using one biobank code ensures that it is easy to trace all wholeblood samples of the patient over time and not just the samples of when the patient was in study x or y (eg patients can be included in a drug intervention study and at the same time be included in the N03LAM general material sampling study or a patient can fail in one study and then be included in the next study). Using separate biobank codes for separate studies it will be much more difficult to find this out.

name: BAVL27 Tumor digest and PDX biobank for immunology research
description:
Tumor material can be enzymatically digested to single cell suspensions which can then be frozen if needed. These single cell suspensions can be used for different things: e.g. growing of tumor cell lines, isolation of immune cells such as T-cells, or analysis of the quantity and quality of the different immune cells present in the tumor. Alternatively, tumor material can be frozen in very small PDX fragments, which at a later timepoint could be transplanted in mice to grow tumor samples so that e.g. immune responses to the tumor can be tested.
Many different intervention clinical trials study the response of immune cells in the tumor to treatment by analyzing tumor biopsies or leftover tumor material. In addition, there are a number of trials which are not designed to test the effect of a (drug) intervention, but purely to follow the immune responses in the tumor itself. In all cases, tumor biopsies or leftover tumor tissue is taken from the patient for digestion to single cell suspension or freezing of PDX fragments.
The proposed tumor digest/PDX immunology biobank will consist of all these tumor single cell digestion products or PDX fragments resulting from separate studies. It is important to work with one biobank code, instead of a separate biobank code for each independent trial in which tumor material is isolated for digestion or PDX, because over time patients are often included in multiple studies; using one biobank code ensures that it is easy to trace all samples of the patient over time and not just the samples of when the patient was in study x or y (eg patients can be included in a drug intervention study and at the same time be included in the N03LAM general material sampling study or a patient can fail in one study and then be included in the next study). In some cases there is a sample taken from the patient at the end of study x, which can nicely be used as a pre-treatment sample for study y. Using separate biobank codes for separate studies it will be much more difficult to find this out.

name: BAVL30 Drug Rediscovery Protocol (DRUP)
description:
This is a prospective, non-randomized clinical trial that aims to describe the efficacy and toxicity of commercially available, targeted anticancer drugs prescribed for treatment of patients with advanced cancer with a potentially actionable variant as revealed by a genomic or protein expression test. The study also aims to simplify patient access to approved targeted therapies that are contributed to the program by collaborating pharmaceutical companies and to perform next generation sequencing on tumor biopsies for biomarker analyses. 
Eligible patients have an advanced solid tumor, multiple myeloma or B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma for which standard treatment options are no longer available and acceptable performance status and organ function. A genomic or protein expression test must have been performed on the tumor and the results must identify at least one potentially actionable molecular variant as defined in the protocol. Results from the molecular profiling test will be used to determine an appropriate drug(s) from among those available in the protocol. The choice of drug will be supported by a list of potential profiles, a molecular tumor board, a knowledge library and by study coordinators for review and approval of the match. The protocol-specified treatment will be administered to the patient once any drug-specific eligibility criteria are confirmed and a fresh pretreatment biopsy is performed for future genetic studies.  All patients who receive treatment with a drug available in the protocol will be followed for standard efficacy outcomes including tumor response, progression-free and overall survival as well as duration of treatment. In addition, treatment related toxicity will be evaluated.
The pre-treatment fresh frozen tumor biopsy specimen will be submitted to the Hartwig Medical Foundation, the Centre for Personalized Treatment’s core sequencing facility for Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS). Thereafter we would like to store any remaining body material (blood + biopsy) in a central Biobank, to facilitate potential future research projects.

name: BAVL36 Translational Gastrointestinal Oncology – tissue
description: This biobank will collect colorectal adenoma and carcinoma tissue samples that are crucial for conducting the research of the Translational Gastrointestinal Oncology group, which includes mechanisms of disease as well as biomarkers for predicting disease outcome. One of the most crucial steps in the pathogenesis of colorectal cancer is the progression from adenoma to carcinoma. However, only a minority of adenomas progress to cancer and so far, solid instruments to predict which adenomas are at high risk of progressing to carcinoma are lacking. On the other hand, In established cancers, it is difficult to predict which will recur after treatment and which will respond to therapy. To answer these questions we want to identify molecular markers for early detection as well as for risk of recurrence and response to therapy. name: BAVL42 Prospective evaluation of Human Epididymal protein 4 (HE4) as predictor of malignancy in patients with a ovarian mass, HE4 Prediction
description: Correct characterization of an ovarian mass is important for the referral of patients with a high risk of malignancy, to a specialized oncologic center. Currently, the Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI), with a cut-off value of 200, is used in the Netherlands to select patients with a high risk of ovarian cancer. However, the sensitivity and specificity of the RMI score are not optimal. Currently, 40% of the referred patients have benign disease in the final pathology. This incorrect characterization of the ovarian mass causes an increase in health care costs and may lead to anxiety in the patient because of the referral to an oncologic center. Serum biomarker Human Epididymal protein 4 (HE4) is increased in patients with epithelial ovarian cancer and to a lesser extent in patients with a benign ovarian mass. Multiple retrospective studies have shown that mainly the specificity to distinguish a benign ovarian mass from ovarian cancer is improved when HE4 is used compared with CA125. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the additional value of biomarker HE4, as second step after the RMI score, in the triage of patients with an ovarian mass. description: In this single-center, open-label, exploratory study, we will enroll 60 patients within two years, including 30 patients with MSS tumors and 30 patients with MSI tumors. name: BAVL50 Understanding tumor immune escape in patients with stage III melanoma
description:
For a detailed description of the background and rationale, please see the study protocol. In short:
Melanoma patients with regional lymphatic metastases (stage III melanoma), for which the primary treatment is surgical resection, have a high risk of progression to distant metastasis and death (five-year survival of 40-78%). However, a significant proportion of patients remains disease-free after surgery. Identifying which patients have a high chance of relapse would allow us to treat these patients with adjuvant therapies, diminishing the chance of relapse. While there exist several clinical parameters that roughly predict chance of relapse, these are not very precise and cannot be used to assess risk on a case by case basis. 

There is a clear need for a better understanding of melanoma progression, which can eventually lead to the development of biomarkers or even new treatments. There is a complex interplay between tumor, tumor microenvironment and host immune response, which will have to be elucidated further to make this possible. This requires the longitudinal study of blood and tumor samples. All patients with lymphatic metastases undergo surgical resection. These metastases range from micrometastases to multiple large, palpable lymph nodes or extensive in-transit metastases. Especially for patients with palpable lymph node metastases or in-transit metastases, the general size of these lesions means that after pathological examination, there remains an abundance of tumor material that can be used for research, with an intact tumor microenvironment. Moreover, these patients have a high chance of progression to distant metastasis, which makes this an ideal patient category to study disease progression. Patients that do not progress will present an ideal control group. Analysis of these tumor samples and subsequent distant metastases can yield a wealth of information on melanoma disease behavior and progression. Moreover, on-treatment biopsies can be collected to better understand response to different treatments and find biomarkers for response.

name: BAVL64 Psychiatric and cognitive function in patients with Neuroendocrine tumours with carcinoid syndrome
description:
Rationale: Patients with a neuroendocrine tumour (NET) report cognitive problems and psychiatric symptoms such as depressed mood, anxiety and irritability. These problems and symptoms are thought to be related to cerebral shortage of the serotonin precursor tryptophan, that is depleted by peripheral overproduction by the tumour. The clinical manifestation of serotonin (5-HT) overproduction (diarrhoea, flushes and wheezing) is known as carcinoid syndrome (CS) which can be present in metastasized (M1) ileal NET tumours. The exact role of 5-HT metabolism in psychopathology, however, is still unclear.
Objective: This study aims to assess impairments in cognition and psychiatric function in patients with metastatic ileal NET and relate this to 5-HT metabolism, by investigating the relation between psychiatric and cognitive function to peripheral 5-HT production. 
The study has two main objectives: First, to study the relation between cognitive function and peripheral 5-HT production, second, to study the relation between the severity of depressive symptoms and peripheral 5-HT production. 
Secondary objectives are to assess psychiatric diagnoses within the patient group and relate them to 5-HT production and to assess the severity of irritability and its relation to 5-HT production.

Exploratory objective: Data collection for biobanking for future research questions
- Blood sample for circulating tumour DNA
- Blood sample for genotyping (eg. polymorphism in serotonin transporter genes)
- Future analysis of other measurements of in the serotonergic pathway, such as TRP or metabolites of 5-HT in blood and urine

NET is a rare tumor, and this study is the first to combine and to relate standardized cognitive and psychiatric testing with measurements of 5HT metabolism. As very little is known about the relation between 5HT metabolism, medication and symptoms, we want to increase the possibility to answer future research questions by biobanking blood and urine samples. 

For more details please see the attached study protocol.

name: BAVL62 Determining the sensitivity and specificity of circulating tumor cells and cytology in cerebrospinal fluid of patients clinically suspected for leptomeningeal metastases
description:
Background: Two to eight percent of patients with solid tumors develop tumor metastases in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), also known as leptomeningeal metastases (LM). Diagnosis of LM is often based on clinical symptoms and typical contrast enhancement of the leptomeninges on MRI of brain and/or spine. However, MRI has a low sensitivity (0.76) and specificity (0.77) for the diagnosis of LM. When MRI results are inconclusive, a lumbar puncture is performed to obtain CSF. Sensitivity of CSF cytology is also low: 55% at first lumbar puncture, increasing to 80% upon second sampling. 
In the recent years, new methods of solid tumor cell detection in blood and CSF have been developed. One method is  the Cell Search System (Veridex) that showed sensitivity rates up to of 100% and  specificity rates up to 97.2% for the detection of Epithelial Cell Adhesion Molecule (EpCAM) positive tumor cells in CSF. Another method is EpCAM based immunoflow cytometry with also high  sensitivity and specificity rates (76-80% and 84- 96% respectively). At the NKI-AvL, an improved EpCAM-based immunoflow cytometry assay was developed to detect CTCs. In a small group of cancer patients with a clinical suspicion on LM and a negative or non-conclusive MRI (n=29) a 100% sensitivity and specificity of this assay for the diagnosis of LM was found. In comparison, CSF cytology showed 61.5% sensitivity and  100% specificity in the same patients group. The immunoflow cytometry assay was adapted for  melanoma patients by using an antibody melanoma chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan (MCSP) instead of EpCAM. 

Goals study The primary goal of the study is to determine the sensitivity and specificity of immunoflow cytometry versus cytology in  CSF of patients that have a history of a (metastasized) epithelial tumor or melanoma and will undergo a lumbar puncture because of a clinical suspicion on LM. Secondary goals are (1) to determine the CSF penetration of targeted and immunotherapeutic agents, when patients are treated with these medicines and (2) to detect tumor mutations in ctDNA and isolated tumorcells from CSF. 

Study design: We enroll patients that treated at the NKI-AVL or MC Slotervaart in Amsterdam and at the Oscar Lambret Cancer Center, Lille in whom a lumbar puncture and venipuncture is clinically indicated for CSF and blood collection.  We  both include CSF and blood samples from patients with a  (clinical) suspicion on LM, and from patients that have a suspicion of a non-malignant neurological disease, eg. infectious or auto-immune meningitis or subarachnoid hemorrhage (control group) (MC Slotervaart). 
From every patient a sample of 1 x 6 ml of CSF for laboratory assessments (cell count, chemistry, ctDNA), 1 x 5 ml of CSF for cytology, 2 x 5 ml of CSF for immune flowcytometry , 1 x 2 ml of CSF for drug quantification (in total 23 ml CSF per sampling) will be obtained.
After the LP, 2x8ml serum for blood cell count and chemistry and 2x10 mL for ctDNA mutation measurement, 1x8 ml sample of whole blood for CTC determination in blood and 1 x 4 ml plasma or serum for drug quantification will be drawn (in total 48 ml blood per sampling). 
If more lumbar punctures are clinically indicated, the same CSF/blood sampling as stated above will be performed. If available, archived primary tumor tissue will be obtained for EpCam/MCSP staining.

Inclusion of patients: The study started in May 2012 as the N12CLM study. This study will now continue as the B16BLM biobank study. Inclusion rate is expected to be 2 patients/month. There is no end date of the study

name: BAVL61 Biobank voor genetische biomarker analyse van weefsel/bloed van patiënten met een HPV-negatieve tumor in het hoofd-halsgebied.
description:
Kanker in het hoofdhalsgebied, de keel, mondholte of het strottenhoofd is een zeer ernstige en levensbedreigende aandoening, zeker wanneer de tumor in een wat meer gevorderd stadium is. Er zijn twee geaccepteerde behandelingen voor een gevorderd stadium hoofdhalskanker: ofwel chirurgie met nabestraling, ofwel een combinatie van bestraling met of zonder gelijktijdige medicatie (radiosensitizer). Het zijn allebei ingrijpende behandelingen maar patiënten verkiezen toch vaak bestraling al dan niet met of zonder een radiosensitizer. Bijna de helft van de patiënten is niet genezen na bestraling in combinatie met een radiosensitizer. Die patiënten hadden naar verwachting beter behandeld kunnen worden met chirurgie en nabestraling, of post-operatieve chemoradiatie of een andere therapie. Helaas kunnen we niet voorspellen welke tumor goed reageert op radiotherapie met of zonder radiosensitizer. 

In dit project zoeken we daarom biomarkers op basis van genetische, pathologische en klinische factoren. Als op basis van biomarkers kan worden aangegeven dat er een grote kans is dat de tumor terug komt na bestraling met of zonder radiosensitizer, dan is de keuze voor een andere behandeling wellicht beter. Patiënten beslissen over de behandeling die ze ondergaan op advies van de behandelend arts. Helaas zijn er tot op heden weinig diagnostische mogelijkheden om subpopulaties met een slechtere response op de huidige standaard behandelingen te identificeren. Om deze reden is onderzoek naar tumorweefsel en bloed bij hoofd-halskanker patiënten van groot belang.


Patiënten met een advanced stage (III/IV) hpv-negatieve oropharynx, larynx en hypopharynx tumor die behandeld worden middels radiotherapie met of zonder combinatie van chemo of andere medicatie komen in aanmerkingen voor deze biobank. De biobank heeft als doel biomarkers te identificeren en valideren die de response op therapie kunnen voorspellen. Een exacte vraag is nog niet te formuleren aangezien het een deels exploratieve en validerende onderzoeksvraag betreft. Momenteel vinden retrospectieve analyses plaats welke met gegevens uit deze biobank dienen te worden gevalideerd. Inzameling van het weefsel komt overeen met de inzameling volgens het B15HHC protocol met inachtneming van de hierboven geformuleerde inclusiecriteria. 
Kortgezegd, alle patiënten die voldoen aan de inclusiecriteria die komen voor een eerste afspraak op de poli Hoofd & Hals Oncologie & Chirurgie krijgen de informatiebrief over het verzamelen van weefsel voor een biobank. De arts-assistenten/nurse practitioner/fellows/hoofd-hals chirurgen geven deze brief. Indien de patiënt heeft besloten weefsel af te staan, wordt het ic-formulier gescand en komt het in het elektronisch patiëntendossier. Op de operatiedag moet de hoofd-halschirurg in Chipsoft controleren of het ic-formulier getekend is ja/nee (gaat de patiënt akkoord met het verzamelen van de biopten). Indien mogelijk worden er 2 biopten tumor vries, 2 biopten tumor paraffine en 2 biopten normaal weefsel  afgenomen. Er is een oranje HHC pathologie Research formulier vervaardigd door Dr. Lotje Zuur voor op de operatiekamer en hierop wordt aangegeven welke weefselsamples verzameld zijn voor welke studie/biobank. Het weefsel en oranje formulier worden na de operatie opgehaald en ingeleverd bij de afdeling pathologie. Aan het weefsel wordt een code gekoppeld en met behulp van deze code is het weefsel terug te vinden. De code van het weefsel is gekoppeld aan de betreffende TRION code (B17GEN). Het afnemen van 1 extra buis bloed zal plaatsvinden tijdens de standaard bloedafname voor het stellen van de diagnose/ opstellen van het behandelplan. Voor het afnemen van 1 extra buis bloed geldt een verwijzing naar het reeds bestaande en goedgekeurde protocol P09BIO.
Samples zullen zoveel mogelijk in een batch verwerkt worden om zo batcheffecten te voorkomen. De FFPE biopten zullen worden verwerkt voor DNA en Fresh-frozen materiaal voor RNA en DNA next-generation sequencing. Het bloed zal hierbij fungeren als controle voor het DNA mutatiepatroon. Het normaal weefsel zal fungeren als controle voor het RNA expressie patroon. Het paraffine materiaal zal worden gebruikt voor immunohistochemie.

name: BAVL72 CONventional TReatment Or Leave DCIS
description:
Since  the population-based breast cancer screening was introduced in the Netherlands in 1989, the incidence of Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS) of the breast has increased more than sixfold. DCIS is considered a precursor of invasive breast cancer and mostly treated as such, with surgery and, in case of breast conserving surgery, radiotherapy. Despite the increased incidence of DCIS, the incidence of invasive breast cancer has not declined. This implies that DCIS does not always progress into invasive carcinoma, resulting in overtreatment of at least part of patients diagnosed with screen-detected DCIS. To test this hypothesis, a randomized, international multicenter, open-label, phase III non-inferiority trial was set up by Elshoff et al (LORD-trial), and has recently started including women. The LORD-trial will compare standard treatment with active surveillance in 1240 women aged ? 45 years with asymptomatic, screen-detected, pure low-grade DCIS based on vacuum-assisted biopsies of calcifications only. Both study arms will be monitored with annual digital mammography for a period of 10 years. The primary end-point is 10-year ipsilateral invasive breast cancer free percentage. Currently, the LORD-trial is open for inclusion in eight Dutch centers and more are to open  in the coming months. In addition, multiple centers in different European countries will start accrual within the next year 
As expected, not all women want to be randomized and not all women are randomized to the study arm of their personal preference. As a consequence, a minority of women (estimated about 25% as outlined in the statistics section of the LORD-trial protocol) decide to undergo either conventional treatment or active surveillance rather than participate in the randomized study. To avoid loss of crucial information from these women regarding their perceptions and reasons for their individual choices, to collect and analyze their tissue samples and to monitor their follow-up, it is essential that these women give consent to participate in the proposed prospective observational study. For this study, identical inclusion criteria apply as for the LORD-trial. 
The potential study participant will be offered at participation in the LORD-trial. If the patient does not want to participate in the trial due to a strong preference for one of the study arms, the patient will be offered the alternative non-randomized observational study.
In conclusion, the aim is to utilize highly important data complementary to the LORD-trial, crucial to evaluate and improve the management of low grade DCIS.

name: BAVL105 POINTING: Towards patient-tailored cancer immunotherapy supported by a multifaceted predictive signature composed of integrative omics and molecular imaging
description:
SUMMARY 
Rationale: Immunotherapy is a novel, rapidly evolving field, with several drugs and combinations under development. Cancer treatment is being revolutionized by these drugs due to broad activity across a variety of cancers, leading to remarkable and durable responses. Unfortunately, no validated tools are available to predict which patients will benefit from these expensive drugs or will experience life-threatening toxicity. Patient selection based on factors such as Programmed Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and somatic mutations in tumor biopsies still undervalues the complexity and dynamics of immune response. 
Objective: Primary objective: To develop and validate multifaceted predictive signatures for anti PD-1 antibody effects using relevant components of integrative omics (histology, immunohistochemistry, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, radiomics and molecular imaging), that predict which patients have a ≤ 5% chance of responding to PD-1 antibody. Secondary objective: Relationship between a multifaceted signature and toxicity. 
Study design: This is a two-center prospective continuously accruing longitudinal cohort study in patients with non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) or metastatic melanoma eligible for standard anti-PD-1 antibody treatment. After successful eligibility screening, all patients will undergo i) a biopsy for whole genome sequencing, IHC, DNA and RNA analysis ii) venous blood sampling for routine assessments and exploratory biomarker analysis, iii) feces sampling, and iv) CT scan, MRI brain, and whole body or total body FDG-PET, according to standard diagnostic criteria and response measurement criteria. 
Data on medication, side effects of treatment, and results from routine assessments will be derived from the electronical patient dossier. Blood samples for exploratory biomarker analysis will be isolated and stored until analysis of for example circulating tumor DNA, peptide profiling, circulating miRNA, cytokine bead assay chemokine profile, cell free tumor DNA changes upon treatment et cetera. The tumor biopsy, venous blood sampling and feces collection will ideally be performed before, during and at the end of standard anti-PD-1 antibody treatment. The data from this prospective longitudinal cohort will be used in the POINTING (towards patient –tailored cancer immunotherapy supported by a multifaceted predictive signature composed of integrative omics and molecular imaging) KWF Kankerbestrijding project. The goal of this project is to develop a multifaceted predictive signature, by using new techniques on tumor characteristics before and during treatment with immune therapy. To do so, researchers will use the ‘omics’ approach. By combining molecular omics comprising genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics with radiomics and molecular imaging a set of factors will arise which can accurately predict the outcome of the treatment. 
Study population: Patients with metastatic NSCLC or metastatic melanoma with an indication for the standard of care anti-PD-1 antibody treatment. Together, the NKI-AVL and UMCG will recruit yearly ~500 patients in the NSCLC cohort and ~200 patients in the melanoma cohort. 
Main study parameters/endpoints: A multifaceted predictive signature by combining molecular omics comprising genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics with radiomics and molecular imaging. 
Nature and extent of the burden and risks associated with participation, benefit and group relatedness: All necessary information on the subjects will be extracted from the (electronic) patient dossier. The risk of blood drawings and stool sampling are considered negligible. Review of the literature shows that in general tumor biopsies can be performed with only minor complications and acceptable risks. Although patients do not directly benefit from this study, results of this study will be valuable for the understanding of the tumor immune response and will guide further prospective research and patient selection thereafter. The purpose of POINTING is to personalize potentially curative immunotherapy, thereby avoiding possibly harmful exposure by these drugs of patients who will not benefit.

Two of the key interests of the NKI-AVL are immunotherapy and personalized medicine. The results from this study can contribute in both these fields and therefore fits the NKI research strategy

name: IRBb22-135 Gene expression analysis of vulvar lichen sclerosus and associated squamous cell carcinoma
description:
In this study we aim to further explore the etiology of LS and LS-VSCC by investigating the genetic signature of these tissues through next generation sequencing. Concurrently we aim to investigate which changes occur in gene expression when LS patients are treated with UTCS, both before and after onset of VSCC. The main study parameter is the gene expression of collected tissue samples, and to identify any differences in these expression patterns between the various study groups.

Participants are adult female patients with vulvar LS (group A), patients with vulvar LS who received surgical resection for LS associated VSCC in the past (group B) and patients undergoing surgery for LS associated VSCC (group C). A total of 30 patients will be included (10 in each group). Patients of study group A and B will receive a 3-month treatment with UTCS (Clobetasol propionate 0.05%) which is regular treatment for LS. Patients of study group C will be surgically treated for LS-VSCC, also according to regular care. 

For this study, two vulvar punch biopsies and a peripheral blood sample will be collected of each patient. gDNA and PBMC's will be isolated from the peripheral blood sample, which we want to store in this biobank. Tissue will be processed by the Pathology department for which arrangements have been discussed (ACT22-016). Isolated gDNA will be used for subsequent RNA/DNA sequencing at CeGaT Genetic Diagnostics in Germany.

name: IRBb23-314 Neoadjuvant trastuzumab, pertuzumab and tucatinib without chemotherapy in HER2- positive breast cancer: the TRAIN-4 study
description:
The TRAIN-4 study is a phase Ib single-center trial to evaluate safety and initial efficacy of neoadjuvant tucatinib, trastuzumab and pertuzumab in stage II/III HER2-positive breast cancer. The primary endpoint is all grade adverse events. All patients will start neoadjuvant treatment consisting of tucatinib, trastuzumab and pertuzumab (and endocrine therapy if indicated). Response monitoring is performed after three cycles using DCE-MRI. In case of functional tumor volume decrease of =65%, patients continue treatment for six more cycles. If tumor response is <65%, however, patients will switch to receive six cycles of PTC-Ptz (standard-of-care treatment). After completion of neoadjuvant treatment, patients will undergo surgery. 
During this study, extra biopsies and blood samples will be collected for translational research purposes.

name: IRBb23-009 Effect of a bundle of non-pharmacologicol interventions on the surgical stress response
description:
We would like to start a biobank of biomarkers of the physiological response to surgical stress. Surgical stress is known to trigger a neuro-humoral response that causes a pro-inflammatory state that can influence oncogenesis and that affects short- and longterm surgical outcomes. Creating a biobank of these biomarlers (cytokines, interleukines, adrenal hormones etc) can help us determine the potentially beneficial effects of anesthesiological interventions. 
Initially, there will be three timepoints for collection: on the morning of surgery (baseline), directly following surgery and the first postoperative morning.

name: IRBb23-024 A first-in-human (FIH) study of IDRX-42 in participants with metastatic and/or unresectable gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)
description:
IDRX, Inc. would like to retain/archive/save any leftover or extra samples (e.g., biopsy samples and/or blood samples) that are not analyzed for 
study IDRX-42-001 for any additional exploratory studies. The collected biomaterials and related data will be stored by IDRX, Inc. in a so-called 
Biobank and made available for future research purposes to help better understand how certain drugs may work in the human body, in addition to 
helping develop new ways to monitor and treat diseases. This may include research to gain more knowledge related to the disease that is 
investigated under this study and may be used to improve methods or design new methods for analyzing, comparing, or combining Study Data with 
data from participants treated with other study treatments. Researchers may study the beneficial or harmful effects of the drug and compare the data 
from this drug with other drugs. This will allow IDRX, Inc. and other research institutions to better understand the disease and how the drug works 
and to be able to identify the best way to treat participants with GIST.
The goal of this research is not to diagnose a specific participant or other individuals. Rather, the comparative study of larger groups of people is 
intended to identify biomedical relationships. The biomaterial is e.g. archival tumor samples and/or blood samples that have been collected as part 
of the main study but are no longer needed for this purpose and would therefore otherwise be destroyed. 
In addition, further data may be obtained during the examination of the biosamples. The biomaterials and data provided by the participant will be 
used exclusively for research related to the investigational product and your disease (GIST). However, the exact questions cannot be specified at the 
present time, and this may also depend on the results of the IDRX-42-001 study. For logistical reasons, it may not be possible for the Biobank to 
make individual restrictions (e.g. exclusion of certain research, exclusion of the transfer of the materials to third parties). If the participant does not 
fully agree with the described duration and use of these biosamples for future research, he/she should not give consent. This additional use of the 
participant samples is voluntary and will only take place if a written consent is obtained. Even if the participant does not consent, he/she can still 
participate in the main study. If the participant does not wish to participate or withdraws his/her consent at a later date, he/she will not be 
disadvantaged

name: IRBb23-085 Hebon DNA side study
description:
The Hebon biobank is an amendment to the ongoing IRB-approved Hebon study. In this Hebon biobank study, we aim to collect additional biospecimens and here specifically request approval for the collection of (non-invasive) buccal swap or saliva for germline DNA analyses. 

This biobank effort will start specifically with a pilot study (N=300) at the NKI-AVL to evaluate methods for continuous routine enrollment of our study population, extended with healthy women of BRCA1/ BRCA2/ CHEK2/ ATM/ PALB2 mutation-negative families. These mostly untested healthy members are seen at the AVL screening clinic and potential Hebon participants. We would like to specifically enroll these women and also collect their DNA sample for future research. Though for the pilot we focus on a specific subgroup, in essence, every family member from a family that has been referred to clinical genetics is eligible for participation. 

For the pilot the approach of participants is slightly different from what we have done so far, which is been solely via the clinical genetic centers. For this pilot we will recruit participants via the screening clinic (of note, clinical genetics are involved in that clinic as well). All visitors of the AVL screening clinic with an increased risk of breast- and/or ovarian cancer will be asked by the nurse specialist to participate in Hebon. They will receive a Hebon participation letter and brochure to be able to register online for Hebon. The standard enrollment in Hebon with online registration was already approved by the IRB. 

The nurse specialist will register Hebon number, patient number, birth month and –year to inform the Hebon coordinator about the invitations. The Hebon coordinator will need limited access in Hix to look for name and address details to send a reminder if necessary and to check if a DNA sample is available for future research. If someone registered online to participate in Hebon and no DNA sample is available, Hebon will send a saliva or buccal swab kit to complete the data collection. The Hebon coordinator will also be able to check if someone is already participating in Hebon. 

The saliva or buccal swab kits will be stored at room temperature at the NKI-AVL and DNA isolation is not planned yet.

Extra info on associated IRB studies:
The Hebon study started in 1997 as the Gen en Omgeving (GEO-Hebon) project and since then several projects have been approved by the  Protocol Toetsingscommissie (reference number GEO1: EV98168 (NKI 98-1854), GEO2: PTC05.0843 (NKI 2004-3088), GEO3: PTC07-1611 (NKI 2007-3756)). The HEBON project protocol was approved on 18-08-2011 (briefkenmerk: PTC11.1799) by the Protocol Toetsingscommissie of the NKI-AVL. Since then, several parts, like the Informed Consent and questionnaires, have been updated and approved by the IRB (IRBd19043 and IRBd21-201).

Extra info on new TRION study code:
We have not requested a new TRION code as this is the same prospective Hebon study as the P05GEO.

name: IRBb23-070 A multicentre randomised open-label phase III study of stereotactic   radiosurgery, in addition to standard systemic therapy for patients with metastatic melanoma or newly diagnosed metastatic NSCLC and asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic brain me
description:
The collected biological material (tissue and blood) is submitted to, catalogued, and maintained at the Central Laboratory and Biobank where the material will be centrally archived and will thereafter undergo central histology review and biomarker testing at the University Hospital of Zurich translational research laboratory. Translational research projects will be continuously adapted according to growing knowledge about immunological modification and potential biomarkers of immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Trans-lational research studies will be conducted by internal and external collaborators of the ETOP IBCSG Partners Foundation in line with the ETOP IBCSG Partners Biobank and Translational Research Policy (Thoracic).All tissue and blood samples collected during the conduct of the trial must be identi-fied with the correct patient ID (Case ID) issued by the ETOPdata EDC system. All in-formation allowing potential identification of the patient must be removed or black-ened.

name: BAVL77 Phase 1 study to assess safety and efficacy of Neo-Adjuvant Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma COmbination-immunotherapy (NABUCCO)
description:
1. Background: Although muscle-invasive urothelial cancer can be cured by surgery, recurrence rates are high and 5-year survival is only 45-55% for pT3N0 tumors, and even worse for pT4aN0 (35-45%) or pTxN+ (10-35%) patients. Neo-adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy has a high rate of response. Despite impressive responses, including a pathological complete response (pCR) rate of 22-40% [1], the absolute benefit in terms of overall survival is only 5%[2], at the cost of substantial toxicity. Given the high rate of distant recurrences, systemic treatment needs to be improved to change the abysmal prognosis of high-risk bladder cancer. Promising activity of anti-PD-L1 and anti-PD-1 antibodies has been observed in patients with urothelial cancer [3]. As responses to immunotherapy appear to be durable, the introduction of immunotherapy in the peri-operative setting may improve prognosis, as has been shown for melanoma [4]. Judging from the metastatic setting however, response rates for monotherapy may not be high enough to translate into sufficient benefit peri-operatively. The addition of anti-CTLA4 treatment could prevent negative regulation of T-cell priming and thereby broaden and intensify the immune response to cancer antigens. We propose to conduct a study of pre-operative immunotherapy in high-risk urothelial cancer patients using an attenuated schedule of ipilimumab and nivolumab. As we will collect pre- and post-treatment tissue, this study will provide a unique opportunity to study effects of treatment on the anti-tumor immune response.

Objectives:  
- Primary objective: 
1. Establish whether a sequenced pre-operative schedule of ipilimumab and nivolumab is safe in urothelial cancer patients
- Secundary objectives:
2. Dissect the tumor micro-environment of urothelial cancers before and after combination immunotherapy using multiplexed immunohistochemistry methods and transcriptional profiles
3. Test efficacy of pre-operative ipilimumab – nivolumab
4. Explore how the (dys)functional state of the tumor-specific T cells is altered by sequenced combination therapy.

name: BAVL78 Evaluating ctDNA as biomarker for treatment in HNSCC
description: Tumors continually shed DNA into the circulation, where it can be accessed. This circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) directly reflects tumor burden and has great potential to be a sensitive biomarker for treatment recurrence. These “liquid biopsies” could give a more real-time picture of the genomic status and evolution of a tumor and can be easily assessed for measurement of different biomarkers. However, in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) patients treated with  definitive radiotherapy, data regarding ctDNA kinetics and its correlation with outcome are scarce. A new or additional tool for response evaluation next to or instead of conventional imaging after treatment would be beneficial to detect recurrences in an earlier stage, thereby increasing the chances of success of salvage therapy. More importantly, an early response parameter during treatment could help to identify patients that have a good treatment response and might benefit from treatment adaptation. With this study, we aim to reveal ctDNA as an effective tool for future dose (de)-escalation trials in HNSCC.

name: BAVL86 Are circulating hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells a potential biomarker for therapy response and disease progression in patients with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck?
description:
We hypothesize that cytokines secreted by head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC)perturbs hematopoiesis in patients, as measured by the frequency and composition of circulating and tumor-resident hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). We additionally hypothesize that this perturbation can be restored after local treatment of the tumor.

We aim to prospectively include 30 patients with HNSCC that are eligible for treatment consisting of surgery, radiotherapy, immunotherapy (as part of the N16IMC trial) or a combination of these modalities. We aim to investigate the frequency, composition and differentiation commitments of circulating and tumor-resident HSPCs in treatment-naïve HNSCC patients, and compare them with the results from healthy controls. Next, we aim to assess whether treatment can restore the perturbed hematopoiesis by comparing the sample profile before and after treatment. We will correlate our findings to 2-year follow up clinical and survival parameters.

This biobank fits in the NKI research strategy, because we ensure the material may be used in further (immunotherapeutic) research.

name: BAVL93 Health After eaRly Menopause due to Oophorectomy
description:
A risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) is advised to all women carrying a BRCA germline mutation at age 35-40 years for BRCA1 and at age 40-45 years for BRCA2 mutation carriers. Little is known about the potential long-term health effects of a RRSO. We will perform a nationwide cross-sectional study nested in a cohort to examine the long-term health effects of the RRSO in women with a high genetic risk of ovarian cancer. This project is funded by the Dutch Cancer Society, grant number 10164. 

We will specifically look at cardiovascular disease, bone health and cognition. 
Currently, there are several hypotheses regarding the relationship between early menopause and cardiovascular risk. One hypothesis states that women with a natural early menopause are at higher risk of developing cardiovascular disease because of the diminished levels of hormones, such as estrogen, in the blood. Another hypothesis states that because of a high risk of cardiovascular disease women get into menopause earlier. 
There is also a hypothesis stating that BRCA-gene mutation carriers have a higher genetic risk of cardiovascular disease. 

Furthermore, there is a hypothesis that BRCA-gene mutation carriers are at higher risk of developing Alzheimer's Dementia.

name: BAVL94 Tumor and blood sampling sampling in patients with urinary tract cancer

This study will be a succession of the N13KCM study, in which we studied the longitudinal kinetics of cancer mutations in approximately 60 patients with urothelial cancer treated with chemotherapy.  To be able to comprehensively study the effect of systemic therapies in UTC, we would like to continue the collection of tumor, blood and urine samples in UTC patients. Tissue, blood and urine collection will usually be part of standard clinical practice. PIF and IC of the N13KCM study are changed accordingly. 

For patients with locally advanced or metastatic urinary tract cancer (UTC: cancers of the bladder, ureter, urethra and renal pelvis including urothelial and variant histology), platinum-based chemotherapy is the mainstay of treatment. Unfortunately, virtually all patients with metastatic UTC and a substantial proportion of patients with locally advanced UTC will eventually present with platinum-refractory disease. At this stage, patients can be treated with immunotherapy, providing a 20% chance of response. Activated molecular pathways and inhibitory components in the tumor-immune micro-environment (TME) could provide targets for new treatments in advanced bladder cancer. 
In order to provide biomarkers for treatment response and new targets for therapy, we will study pre-treatment biopsies, post-treatment surgery specimens, peripheral blood components and/or urine before, during and after systemic therapy in UTC patients. These samples will not only allow us to study pre-treatment biomarkers associated with response, but also perform in depth analyses of possible resistance mechanisms. These analyses will provide strategies to improve systemic therapy (chemotherapy as well as immunotherapy) for UTC.

name: BAVL97 afatinib and cetuximab in EGFR exon 20 insertion positive non-small-cell lung cancer
description:
Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 20 insertions are oncogenic drivers. However, in contrast to the classic EGFR mutations, insertion mutants in exon 20 are associated with primary resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Standard treatment is platinum based chemotherapy, after progression treatment options are lacking. Treatment with afatinib and cetuximab, a combination of an irreversible ErbB family blocker and a chimeric, human-murine anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody is able to overcome resistance to first generation EGFR TKI’s in patients with classic EGFR mutations. The present study will assess anti-tumor activity of afatinib in combination with cetuximab in patients harboring an EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation.
At baseline and at progression, tumor biopsies will be analysed for mechanisms of de-novo and acquired resistance. 
At baseline, during treatment and at progression, cfDNA will be collected to analyse possible resistance mechanisms and to evaluate its predictive value for early response assessment.

name: BAVL98 Blood sampling of healthy volunteers for immunological research
description: The majority of patients generally does not benefit from current immunotherapies, likely due to specific defects in the interaction between the tumor and the immune system leading to active immune escape. To improve the response rate to immunotherapy, there is a strong need for a better understanding of these defects in early and late stage cancer. Moreover, more information is needed on specific aspects of the immune system in healthy individuals. Detailed information on the healthy immune system of non-cancer patients will serve as a reference to define cancer related defects.

name: BAVL99 The Netherlands facility for Cancer-Immune Analysis (N-CIA)
description:
The N-CIA is a KWF_funded infrastructure project together with University Medical Center Groningen, Radboud UMC and Rijnstate Ziekenhuis (starting May 2023). The N-CIA project has two parts. The first part is biobanking of tumor, blood(products), and feces of 1043 cancer patients spread over 8 tumor types. The second part is immune analyses of (part of) these materials and coupling of all the generated data to (medical) data of the patient. In some cases, previously biobanked materials from other studies will be added to the NCIA database (clinical data of patients + NCIA analyses performed on materials). So far this is the case for samples from the B16MEL study and the N14ITO study. This use is with consent of the study PI and approved by the IRB.

The N-CIA aims to describe cancer-immune interactions across malignancies. By determining the immune landscape of tumors (stratified by factors such as tissue of origin or driving oncogene) it will be possible to identify immune suppressive mechanisms at play and thus the most relevant immunotherapy that can be applied.

This biobank fits in the NKI research strategy as the generated data can be used for studies in the field of immunotherapy. This is one of the focus area's of the institute. Also, the material that is biobanked for the N-CIA can be used as a basis for other studies. The N-CIA material can then be used as the pre-treatment sample in longitudinal studies.

name: BAVL102 Image-guided de-escalation of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in HER2-positive breast cancer: the TRAIN-3 study (BOOG 2018-01)
description: The TRAIN-3 study is a single arm phase II multicenter trial to evaluate the efficacy of image-guided de-escalation of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in stage II/III HER2-positive breast cancer. The  primary endpoint of the TRAIN-3 study is 3-year event-free-survival. All patients will be treated with paclitaxel, trastuzumab, carboplatin, and pertuzumab neoadjuvant. Radiologic evaluation will follow every three cycles and patients with a rCR will receive early surgery. During the course of this study biopsies, blood samples and the resection specimen will be collected for translational research purposes. The aim of the translational part of the study is to identify biomarkers to predict treatment response. This to gain further insight into the genetic pathways and biological processes that underlie tumor dissemination and response. We will specifically evaluate the use of liquid biopsies in monitoring response.

name: BAVL104 T-DM1 and osimertinib in EGFR positive non-small-cell lung cancer with HER2 bypass track resistance
description: Despite the high response rate, resistance develops in every patient with EGFR+ NSCLC treated with EGFR TKIs. We hypothesize that EGFR and HER2 blockade by concurrent T-DM1, a HER2 antibody-drug conjugate that releases a cytotoxic anti-microtubule agent,  and osimertinib, a third generation EGFR TKI, can induce tumor responses in patients harboring HER2 bypass track resistance with manageable toxicity. This study is a multicenter single arm phase II study with a phase I run in to study the toxicity and efficacy of T-DM1 and osimertinib combination treatment in patients with EGFR mutated NSCLC and HER2 bypass track activation (HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) =2+ and/or HER2 amplification) after progression on an EGFR TKI. At baseline and at progression tumor biopsies  and cfDNA will be collected and analyzed for mechanisms of de-novo and acquired resistance and to evaluate its predictive value for early response assessment.

name: BAVL105 POINTING: Towards patient-tailored cancer immunotherapy supported by a multifaceted predictive signature composed of integrative omics and molecular imaging
description:
SUMMARY 
Rationale: Immunotherapy is a novel, rapidly evolving field, with several drugs and combinations under development. Cancer treatment is being revolutionized by these drugs due to broad activity across a variety of cancers, leading to remarkable and durable responses. Unfortunately, no validated tools are available to predict which patients will benefit from these expensive drugs or will experience life-threatening toxicity. Patient selection based on factors such as Programmed Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and somatic mutations in tumor biopsies still undervalues the complexity and dynamics of immune response. 
Objective: Primary objective: To develop and validate multifaceted predictive signatures for anti PD-1 antibody effects using relevant components of integrative omics (histology, immunohistochemistry, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, radiomics and molecular imaging), that predict which patients have a = 5% chance of responding to PD-1 antibody. Secondary objective: Relationship between a multifaceted signature and toxicity. 
Study design: This is a two-center prospective continuously accruing longitudinal cohort study in patients with non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) or metastatic melanoma eligible for standard anti-PD-1 antibody treatment. After successful eligibility screening, all patients will undergo i) a biopsy for whole genome sequencing, IHC, DNA and RNA analysis ii) venous blood sampling for routine assessments and exploratory biomarker analysis, iii) feces sampling, and iv) CT scan, MRI brain, and whole body or total body FDG-PET, according to standard diagnostic criteria and response measurement criteria. 
Data on medication, side effects of treatment, and results from routine assessments will be derived from the electronical patient dossier. Blood samples for exploratory biomarker analysis will be isolated and stored until analysis of for example circulating tumor DNA, peptide profiling, circulating miRNA, cytokine bead assay chemokine profile, cell free tumor DNA changes upon treatment et cetera. The tumor biopsy, venous blood sampling and feces collection will ideally be performed before, during and at the end of standard anti-PD-1 antibody treatment. The data from this prospective longitudinal cohort will be used in the POINTING (towards patient –tailored cancer immunotherapy supported by a multifaceted predictive signature composed of integrative omics and molecular imaging) KWF Kankerbestrijding project. The goal of this project is to develop a multifaceted predictive signature, by using new techniques on tumor characteristics before and during treatment with immune therapy. To do so, researchers will use the ‘omics’ approach. By combining molecular omics comprising genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics with radiomics and molecular imaging a set of factors will arise which can accurately predict the outcome of the treatment. 
Study population: Patients with metastatic NSCLC or metastatic melanoma with an indication for the standard of care anti-PD-1 antibody treatment. Together, the NKI-AVL and UMCG will recruit yearly ~500 patients in the NSCLC cohort and ~200 patients in the melanoma cohort. 
Main study parameters/endpoints: A multifaceted predictive signature by combining molecular omics comprising genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics with radiomics and molecular imaging. 
Nature and extent of the burden and risks associated with participation, benefit and group relatedness: All necessary information on the subjects will be extracted from the (electronic) patient dossier. The risk of blood drawings and stool sampling are considered negligible. Review of the literature shows that in general tumor biopsies can be performed with only minor complications and acceptable risks. Although patients do not directly benefit from this study, results of this study will be valuable for the understanding of the tumor immune response and will guide further prospective research and patient selection thereafter. The purpose of POINTING is to personalize potentially curative immunotherapy, thereby avoiding possibly harmful exposure by these drugs of patients who will not benefit.

Two of the key interests of the NKI-AVL are immunotherapy and personalized medicine. The results from this study can contribute in both these fields and therefore fits the NKI research strategy

name: BAVL108 Multicenter Phase 2 Study to Identify the Optimal neo-Adjuvant Combination Scheme of Ipilimumab and Nivolumab (OpACIN-neo)
description:
The OpACIN-neo trial is an open-label multi-center three-arm phase 2 trial consisting of 90 stage III melanoma patients randomized 1:1:1 to receive either 2 courses 3 mg/kg ipilimumab + 1 mg/kg nivolumab every 3 weeks (Arm A), 2 courses 1 mg/kg ipilimumab + 3 mg/kg nivolumab every 3 weeks (Arm B), or 2 courses ipilimumab 3 mg/kg, directly followed by 2 courses nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (Arm C). All three treatment arms are applied prior to surgery at week 6, 30 patients per arm. The pathological response will be centrally revised.The aim of this trial is to identify the optimal dose schedule of neoadjuvant ipilimumab + nivolumab for patients with stage III melanoma in terms of efficacy (pathological response) and toxicity. OpACIN-neo identified ipilimumab 1mg/kg + nivolumab 3mg/kg as best tolerable while efficacy was preserved with a pRR of 77%. Therefore in the PRADO extension conhort the main objective is to confirm efficacy and toxicity of this dosing regimen. As none of the patients with a pRR has relapsed until now, patients will have surgery and adjuvant therapy in this extension cohort according to pRR
At week 6 only one lymph node will be removed. Patients with pCR or near-pCR will not have addtional surgery/therapy. Patients with a pPR will undergo CLND and patients with pNR will undergo CLND, radiotherapy and start adjuvant nivolumab.

name: BAVL110 An Open-label Single-arm Pharmacokinetic Trial, Investigating the Effect of CYP3A4 inhibitor Ritonavir on the Pharmacokinetics of Erlotinib

name: BAVL111 Improve Checkpoint-blockade Response in Advanced urothelial cancer
BAVL112 Pre-operative phase II trial for breast cancer with nivolumab in combination with novel IO (BELLINI trial)
description: The absolute benefit in terms of overall survival of adjuvant chemotherapy in early breast cancer (BC) is relatively low (±10%), at the cost of substantial toxicity. Therefore, the identification of BC patients who could benefit from more targeted treatment approaches that improve outcome, thereby preventing the toxicity of chemotherapy, is of high priority for breast cancer management.  We aim to test the activity of nivolumab monotherapy, or nivolumab combined with low dose doxorubicin or a novel IO in primary breast tumors. This study is a pre-operative window of opportunity phase II study with an adaptive design (Simon’s two-stage) to identify the patients with newly diagnosed TNBC or ER-positive BC that might benefit from nivolumab as monotherapy or combined with low dose doxorubicin or novel IO. Since presence of an endogenous anti-cancer immune response is a requirement for response to anti-PD1, the proposed clinical trial will incorporate an enrichment for BCs with moderate-high stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL). The primary objective is to determine whether short-term pre-operative nivolumab either as monotherapy or in combination with low dose doxorubicin or novel IO combinations can induce immune activation  in early BC. We will assess immune activation by studying the pretreatment biopsy and posttreatment biopsy/surgical specimen, allowing us to study the immune infiltrate, gene expression, genetic alterations and pathological response/residual cancer burden. One piece of the study biopsies will be used for the in vitro tumor fragment platform of Daniela Thommen (in house, B6), to study the effect of anti-PD1 on the tumor cells. In addition, peripheral blood for PBMC, serum, DNA en ctDNA analyses will be drawn at several timepoints during the study. Lastly, a MRI pre- and posttreatment will allow us to study changes in the tumor.

We plan to perform a planned first analysis of 30 patients. We will investigate logistics, Ki67-labeling index, gene-expression, ChIP-sequencing.

We perform a randomized, open-label, multi-institution study. It will compare the efficacy of three different endocrine treatment regimens (Anastrozole, Fulvestrant or Tamoxifen) in changing proliferation-index during a 3 week (+/- 1 week) pre-operative treatment period in breast cancer patients. These results will be correlated to gene expression profiles, phosphorylation status of the ER, SNPs in CYP450 sequences, tamoxifen metabolite concentrations, changes in estrogen serum levels and protein expression patterns. Additionally, we will perform exploratory analyses using ChIP-sequencing of all paired tumor samples.
Samples will be included from 2008 and onward.

name: BAVL121 BILBAD study: Biomarkers In Liquid Biopsies for high-risk Adenoma Detection
description:
Rationale: Blood-based liquid biopsies can be used to identify a range of tumor products, that reflect the biology of the lesion from which they originate and are therefore potentially useful as biomarkers for early detection. We hypothesize that the molecular biomarkers derived from large colon adenomas can be detected in blood samples of these patients and may be used for the early detection of high-risk adenomas and early-stage CRC. 
Objective: To identify proteins and DNA targets for screening for large polyps.
Study design: patients who are planned for polypectomy of large flat or sessile colon polyps >2 cm will be approached for informed consent. Prior to polypectomy, blood will be drawn from the patients out of their in situ venflons. At the surveillance colonoscopy 6 months later, another blood sample will be taken. Proteins and DNA-remnants will be checked in the blood and tested for their predictive value in screening for the presence of large polyps. 
Study population: patients with large flat or sessile colonic polyps, aged 18 years and older.
Main study parameters/endpoints: No intervention will be given in this study. Only blood samples will be collected. Main study parameters are the levels of biomarkers in the blood at baseline prior to polypectomy, and at surveillance when the polyp is no longer present. The second main parameter is the presence of copy number aberrations (CNA’s) in the polyp tissue.
Nature and extent of the burden and risks associated with participation, benefit and group relatedness: Blood samples will be collected from patients with large adenomas prior to polypectomy and surveillance colonoscopy from the existing venous access. 2 Streck tubes of blood will be collected each time. Consent will be asked to request the polyp tissue after pathologic evaluation for DNA testing. The chances of unexpected findings in the DNA tests that influence the patients’ health are minimal, but will nonetheless be discussed with the patient. Patients have to agree to be informed of these findings in order to participate in the study.

name: BAVL139 Cardiomyopathy and heart failure risk after treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma or aggressive B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
description: Over the past decades, the 5- and 10-year survival of especially patients with aggressive B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and to a lesser extent of patients with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) has improved. There is increasing evidence that late cardiovascular complications of cancer treatment cause substantial excess morbidity and mortality in long-term lymphoma survivors. In HL survivors, it has been found that treatment with anthracyclines and cardiac radiation exposure are important risk factors for the development of heart failure. However, variation in anthracycline dose in previous studies among HL survivors was limited and the majority of included patients had received mediastinal radiotherapy as part of the lymphoma treatment, therefore researchers were unable to reliably assess the dose-response relationship of anthracyclines with heart failure and had limited ability to study the interaction between anthracycline exposure and cardiac radiation exposure. In order to better quantify the individual effects of (mediastinal) radiation and anthracycline exposure, we will therefore conduct a case-control study in a combined multicentre cohort of HL and aggressive B cell NHL survivors. Combining these two lymphoma cohorts will provide a much broader range in both anthracycline-dose and radiation exposure. Also, little is known about the possible interaction between treatment (radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy) and conventional cardiovascular risk factors or genetic risk factors and the risk of cardiomyopathy and/or heart failure. It is important to know which lymphoma survivors have an increased risk of treatment-related late effects in order to provide more targeted screening advice, medical interventions and ultimately prevention.

name: BAVL143 Immune induction strategies to improve response to immune checkpoint blockade in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients: the TONIC-2 trial
description: TNBC patients have a relatively high relapse rate and upon relapse the median overall survival is less than a year. No targeted therapies are currently available for this subgroup. The first clinical trials with immune checkpoint inhibition in advanced TNBC look promising but the number of patients with benefit is still relatively low: approximately 5% in unselected patient populations. In patients with PD-L1-positive TNBC, response rates go up to 13-23% and a survival benefit of approximately 7 months was observed in patients treated with anti-PD-L1 and nab-paclitaxel, as compared to nab-paclitaxel monotherapy. We have previously demonstrated a promising response rate of 20% for unselected advanced TNBC patients when anti-PD-1 was given after a short induction treatment with low dose chemo- or radiotherapy. Clinical and immunological responses to anti-PD-1 after induction using cisplatin or doxorubicin deserve further validation. In the current TONIC-2 trial, we aim to i) validate the findings of cisplatin induction treatment with a focus on extensive translational studies and ii) investigate potential benefit of the continuation of the low dose doxorubicin during anti-PD-1 treatment. Furthermore, other cohorts testing novel combinations of immune induction treatments and immune checkpoint inhibitors can be opened within this protocol, providing a unique platform to prioritize combination immunotherapy.

name: BAVL144 Understanding tumor immune escape in patients with Merkel cell carcinoma

There is a complex interplay between tumor, tumor microenvironment and host immune response, which will have to be elucidated further to improve understanding and treatment of MCC. name: IRBb20-230 Neo-adjuvant T-VEC + Nivolumab combination therapy for resectable early metastatic (stage IIIB/C/D-IV M1a) melanoma with injectable disease.

The concept is that T-VEC can turn an immune desolate “cold” tumor into an immunogenic “hot” tumor. The hypothesis is that this will upregulate the expression of PD-L1 and make it more susceptible for treatment with an anti-PD-1 agent. During the course of the trial, tumor samples, serum and PBMCs will be collected at various time points for translational research.

name: IRBb22-094 Late effects: insight into cardiovascular disease risk after Hodgkin lymphoma or breast cancer treatment
description:
This application for a biobank is submitted on request of Tiny Korse, as all LICHT samples have been collected in the past and are currently already stored at the AVL. When the protocol was first submitted a biobank application apparently has not been filed. 

Between 2012 and 2017 several case-cohort studies, nested in larger multicenter cohorts, were performed which assessed risk of and risk factors for development of cardiovascular disease among patients treated for Hodgkin's lymphoma (NL 36481.031.11/ METC 16.0738) and breast cancer (approved amendment of the aforementioned study). All enrolled subjects who were still alive were approached by their treating physician for study participation. If consented, a risk factor questionnaire (established CVD risk factors, family history of heart disease, reproductive factors, exogenous hormones, lifestyle, exercise, smoking, alcohol use) was mailed and the (Hodgkin lymphoma) participants were requested to donate a 20ml blood sample for examination of susceptibility genes and biomarkers for CT- and/or RT-induced CVDs. Breast cancer patients were asked to donate 1x 10 ml (purple) EDTA-tube and 1x 8,5 ml (yellow) gel-tube 


The biobank comprises the blood samples donated by these participants.

name: IRBb22-116 EValuating bIomarker Strategies to ImprOve Low dose CT based lung caNcer Screening(VISIONS)
description: 4ITLR is an implemenation study for LDCT based lung cancer screening (LCS). The Nelson and NLST trials have shown that LDCT based screening achieves a stage shift in detected lung cancers which resulted in a significant reduction in mortality. Despite these results there are still concerns regarding the cost-effectiveness and feasibility of a LCS program. The 4ITLR explores the impact of an annual vs bi-annual sollow-up of participants. From a biomarker point of view there are many promising/innovative biomarkers which could potentially impact a LCS program. At this moment large sample collections combining well defined pre-analytical handling, clinical data and imaging data are lacking. The current biobank will build on the inclusion and collection of clinical and imaging data of the 4ITLR study to collect and store blood samples for the evaluation of innovative biomarkers in the context of LCS. This biobank will allow proper evaluation of new biomarkers in a real-world screening setting.

name: IRBb22-098 Association of silicone breast implant Reconstruction and –Enlargement with Overall wellbeing, Lymphoma and Auto-immune disease – Anaplastic large cell lymphoma of the breast
description: In the Areola-A trial all cases of BIA-ALCL in the Netherlands are identified through PALGA and asked to fill out a patient-reported questionnaire and to give up a blood sample. For deceased patients non-tumour tissue will be requested at PALGA from which DNA will be isolated. These samples are analysed at the DNA level to identify genetic risk factors for the development of BIA-ALCL in women with silicone breast implants. Given the unique opportunity of gathering genetic material of this complete national cohort of BIA-ALCL patients, material shall be stored in a biobank to enable future research on BIA-ALCL

name: IRBb22-137 Anti-PD-1 re-challenge after immune priming by ipilimumab and immune boosting by radiotherapy  in advanced NSCLC
description:
During the RAD-IO study patients with stage IV NSCLC that have progressive disease on previous anti-PD(L)1 therapy will be treated with one dose of anti-CTLA4 and stereotactic body radiation therapy (SRBT) to 1-4 tumor lesions. This will be followed by retreatment with anti-PD-1 therapy.
We will collect tumor samples pre treatment and after anti-CTLA4 and SBRT, but before the first course of PD-1 inhibition. For both samples, baseline and on-treatment, at least 4 samples will be obtained of the same lesion when feasible. 
Whole blood sample together with ctDNA and PMBC will be collected at baseline, and at 4 additional timepoints ctDNA and PMBC will be collected.

description:
This Biobank samples set contains different specimens containing HE4. The samples (n=245) are prospectively collected within a pilot study to evaluate the possibility of detecting HE4 in different body fluids of healthy women, patients with benign or borderline ovarian lesion, and patients with EOC (n=53).

Per participant an extra blood sample was collected and participants were asked to donate a saliva and urine sample and
