name: BAVL155 Diagnostic yield colonoscopy surveillance testicular cancer survivors platinum
description:
Testicular cancer (TC) survivors treated with platinum-based chemotherapy have an increased risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC).[Groot et al, JCO 2018] This prospective multicenter study will be performed in the NKI-AVL, RadboudMC, ErasmusMC and UMCU. TC survivors are eligible when treated with =3 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy (cisplatin) before age 50 years. Colonoscopy will be performed =8 years after initial
treatment (minimum and maximum ages at colonoscopy, 35 and 75 years, respectively). We will evaluate the diagnostic yield of colonoscopy, molecular profile of advanced colorectal neoplasia and normal colorectal tissue, burden and cost-effectiveness of colonoscopy and platinum levels in plasma and urine.

The collection (endoscopical polypectomy or biopsies) of neoplasia detected during colonoscopy will be performed according standard protocol. This will be used to evaluate the molecular profile of colorectal neoplasia detected in TC survivors treated with platinum-based chemotherapy. For study purposes, additional biopsies of normal colorectal tissue will be taken after informed consent for this specific item. These biopsies of normal colorectal tissue will consist of 4 biopsies of the colon transversum and 2-4 biopsies of the colon descendens. In case a polyp of = 1 cm is detected, additional field biopsies will be taken for study purposes. 

Furthermore, we will investigate the effectiveness of stool testing (fecal immunochemical test – FIT) with colonoscopy as a reference. FIT will be evaluated in the laboratorium of the gastroenterology in the Erasmus MC, but remaining feces after analysis will be stored in the AVL. 
We will assess current platinum levels in blood and correlate blood-platinum levels with prevalence of colorectal lesions. This analysis will be performed in the Bio-analytical Laboratorium of the NKI-AVL. TC survivors treated with platinum-based chemotherapy are expected to have a higher yield of advanced colorectal neoplasia compared to the general population. Insight into the carcinogenesis of cisplatin-related advanced colorectal lesions will contribute to CRC prevention in the increasing number of cancer survivors. The results are also important for the great many other cancer survivors treated with platinum-based chemotherapy. In case of a polyp/CRC, 

A venipuncture will be performed to obtain plasma to evaluate whether platinum is still detectable in plasma, which will be performed in the Bio-informaticus laboratory of the AVL.
Finally, TC survivors treated with cisplatin-based chemotherapy also have an increased risk of developing bladder cancer. Therefore we also want to collect urine to determine the platinum levels in urine. A single urine sample will be collected and stored at -80 degrees in the collaborating centers, and analysis will be performed at once.

name: BAVL157 Neo-adjuvant nivolumab or nivolumab with ipilimumab in advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma patients prior to standard of care surgery
description:
The MATISSE study is an investigator-initiated randomized non-comparative phaseII trial consisting of 40 patients with resectable stage III-IVa CSCC randomized 1:1 to receive either 
2 courses of nivolumab 3 mg/kg in week 0 and 2 (ARM A) or 2 courses of nivolumab 3 mg/kg in week 0 and 2 plus 1 course of ipilimumab 1mg/kg in week 0 (ARM B). Both treatment arms are neoadjuvant and applied prior to standard of care (consisting of surgery at week 4 with or without adjuvant RT). The aim of this trial is to determine histopathological tumor response after neo-adjuvant ICI, defined as the proportion of viable tumor cells left in the resected specimen.

name: BAVL159 Cervixcarcinoom Biobank: collecting specimen in NEOCON trial and controls
description:
We have a grant for the CONTESSA/NEOCON trial in which women with early stage cervical cancer will be treated with neo-adjuvant chemotherapy to enable less radical fertility sparing surgery with the final goal to improve fertility in the future. 
In this small biobank we would like to collect blood and biopsies in patients enrolled in the NEOCON/CONTESSA study before and after chemotherapy and as a control in women with early stage cervical cancer before surgical treatment.

name: IRBb20-202 Neo-Adjuvant Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma COmbination-immunotherapy Translational Research Cohort 2
description: In this randomized open-label trial we will investigate preoperative ipilimumab/nivolumab in resectable urothelial cancer. This study is a direct continuation of the original NABUCCO protocol. We will study the tumor micro-environment (composition, phenotype, architecture) through Multiplex Immunohistochemistry of proteins modulating the immune response to investigate the reason for non-response. We will focus on studying the presence of inhibitory cells and proteins in resistant tissue, as these processes could potentially be targeted to overcome resistance. We will also perform pre- and post treatment DNA (whole exome) and RNA sequencing.

name: IRBb21-146 Biobank for Peritoneal metastasis and Ascites in patients with Gastric cancer
description:
Patients with gastric carcinoma and peritoneal metastasis have a very poor prognoses, with a 5-years survival rate of 0%. Unfortunately,the biological process of peritoneal carcinomatosis is not yet well understood. Peritoneal metastasis are diagnosed during the work-up of locally advanced gastric cancer, by performing a staging laparoscopy. The purpose of this laparoscopy is to detect visible peritoneal metastasis and perform peritoneal washing to analyze cytology. To collect these materials for future research like new diagnostic strategies and translational research purposes, we would like to store left-over samples in this biobank. For every patient with gastric cancer undergoing diagnostic laparoscopy we would like to store ascites/or peritoneal washing and material from peritoneal metastasis as well as material of normal tissue (skin, fat, peritoneum). If gastroscopy is performed in AvL, we would like to collect also a sample from the primary tumor.
Additionally we would like to store ascites from patients who undergo palliative drainage for future research purposes, as they have a high concentrate of malignant cells and this material is not used in current practice.

name: IRBb22-247 MEND-IT: Neo-adjuvant FOLFOXIRI and chemoradiotherapy for high risk (“ugly”) locally advanced rectal cancer
description:
Certain tumour characteristics on MRI have been suggested to identify patients, diagnosed with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), facing a particularly bad prognosis: mesorectal fascia involvement, grade 4 extramural venous invasion, tumour deposits and/or lateral lymph nodes. The aim of this study is to assess whether the addition of intensified neoadjuvant chemotherapy to the current standard treatment regimen in patients diagnosed with high risk (hr-)LARC, will improve complete response rates after neoadjuvant treatment, resulting in improved oncologic outcomes. 

This is a multicentre, single-arm, open-label, phase II trial. Patients diagnosed with non-metastatic hr-LARC are eligible for inclusion provided that they are fit for triplet chemotherapy. Exclusion criteria  are the presence of a homozygous DPD deficiency, recent treatment with chemo- and/or radiotherapy and any contraindications for the planned treatment. All patients will be planned for FOLFOXIRI (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin and irinotecan) prior to chemoradiotherapy (CRT; 25 times 2Gy or 28 times 1.8Gy with concomitant capecitabine). After radiologic confirmation of resectable disease, a surgical resection will be performed. A watch-and-wait strategy might be considered in case of a clinical complete response (cCR) after neo-adjuvant treatment. The primary endpoint is the complete response rate, described as pathologic complete response (pCR) or a sustained cCR one year after treatment. The main secondary objectives are (disease-free) survival, radiological response, R0 (a resection with clear resections margins) rate, treatment related toxicity, surgical morbidity, health-related costs and quality of life. Liquid biopsies will be collected after patients’ consent for translational research. 

All patients participating in the study are asked for separate informed consent to collect blood samples for future translational research. If patients give consent, an additional 20ml blood is drawn during regular blood draws. In total, blood for translational research will be drawn at 7 time points during treatment and follow-up.

name: BAVL149 Osimertinib resistance analysis of leptomeningeal metastasis in patients with EGFR mutation positive non-small-cell lung carcinoma that have LM progression on osimertinib treatment.
description:
Initially, patients with EGFR mutation positive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) respond well to osimertinib, a third generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), but eventually progress. At this time point patients are frequently diagnosed with metastases in the central nervous system (CNS). These metastases influence the survival and quality of life of patients. There is especially an unmet need in treating leptomeningeal metastases (LM) because of the treatment-refractory character of this disease site.   
Upon progression on osimertinib, multiple resistance mechanisms have been described and new therapeutic strategies are being developed to target these resistance mechanisms. In contrast to the lesions outside the CNS, characteristics and targeted therapeutic options of molecular mechanisms of EGFR TKI resistance in CNS lesions are largely unknown. Thorough and complete osimertinib resistance analysis (including analysis of CSF) enables optimal treatment decision making and might identify new targets for molecular treatment to treat LM in patients with EGFR mutation positive NSCLC that progress on osimertinib, thereby potentially improving patient outcome.

name: BAVL150 Tumor-educated platelets in cerebral radiation necrosis
description: In this biobank blood samples for TEPs will be collected at inclusion of the N18PET study (at diagnosis of brain metastases (group 1 +2), cerebral radiation necrosis (group 3+4) and diagnostic dilemma groups (either progressive brain metastases after radiotherapy or cerebral radiation necrosis; group 5+6). Furthermore in group 5+6 bloodsamples will also be drawn at follow-up at 3 and 6 months.  The goal  of this study is to determine whether TEPs in the blood can help to discriminate between progressive brain metastases and radiation necrosis.  This biobank fits into the NKI research strategy to improve the treatment of cancer.

name: BAVL153 Monalizumab and trastuzumab in metastatic HER2 positive breast cancer: MIMOSA-trial
description: The cornerstone of the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer is targeting HER2 with trastuzumab. The mechanism of action of trastuzumab is partly based on the lysis of tumor cells via antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), a cell-mediated immune mechanism requiring NK cells. Monalizumab is an antibody targeting the inhibitory receptor NKG2A on NK cells and CD8 T cells and has demonstrated clinical activity when combined with cetuximab (anti-EGFR antibody) in head and neck cancer. We hypothesize that the combination of trastuzumab and monalizumab can promote anti-tumor immunity by unleashing NK cells and CD8 T cells in HER2-positive breast cancer and thereby induce durable clinical responses. Within the study, tumor samples and blood samples will be collected to investigate treatment-induced changes with a special focus on CD8 T cells and NK cells. This study tests a novel NK cell checkpoint inhibitor fitting within the immunotherapy & immunology research theme.

name: IRBb20-210 Establishment of a PDX/PDO collection for gynecological cancers
description: Patient-derived preclinical models are indispensable tools in translational cancer research. They recapitulate the inter- and intratumor heterogeneity observed in patients and have strong value in terms of prediction of response. For gynecological cancers only few collections exist at the moment. For this reason, we aim to esablish a collection of PDX/PDO models for the different tumor types originating from the female reproductive system.

name: BAVL163 WGS Implementation in standard cancer Diagnostics for Every cancer patient
description:
The WIDE study investigates the feasibility and impact of WGS-based diagnostics in clinical practice. 1200 patients with (a suspicion of) metastatic cancer will be included in order to analyse tumour tissue with WGS, in parallel to standard of care (molecular) diagnostics. This tumor material may be derived from a biopsy, a resection, or a collection of body fluids containing tumor cells. A 10ml blood sample (1 tube) is drawn to discriminate somatic mutations from the patient’s germline DNA background variations from the WGS. 



At present, 800 patients are included in the WIDE study, for the remaining 400 patients We would like to add 2 EDTA tubes (20ml) to the blood draw in order to build a plasma biobank. This plasma biobank would accommodate future tissue and plasma validation studies with regards to the identified genetic aberrations with WGS.

name: BAVL164 Archipelago of Ovarian Cancer Research
description:
This biobank is a Dutch nationwide multidisciplinary platform to centralize and expand (pre)clinical and translational research for ovarian cancer to improve diagnostics, treatment and outcome of patients: the Archipelago of Ovarian Cancer Research (AOCR).
This fits the NKI research strategy beacuse it enables research in (molecular) subgroups of patients leading to more personalized treatment.

name: IRBb20-175 Multicenter phase I/IIa study using T-cell receptor gene therapy in metastatic melanoma
description:
Prior preclinical and clinical studies have provided proof for a beneficial effect of T lymphocytes in melanoma and other tumor types. Preclinical mouse models have shown that tumor reactivity can be endowed on nonreactive T cells by the transfer of T cell receptor (TCR) genes. In this phase I/IIa study the aim was to investigate the feasibility and safety of TCR gene therapy in patients with advanced melanoma. The trial was conducted from 2011 until 2018. 

During the course of the study, serum samples were taken at multiple timepoints for study purposes. There was never a biobank registration of this trial during the course of the trial. On request of Tiny Korse the serum samples need to be registered in a biobank. No new specimens will be retrieved from patients for this biobank.

name: IRBb20-200 Biobank of gastric tissue and organoids from patients with a germline CDH-1 mutation
description: The goal of the project is to set up a biobank of tissue from patients with a germline CDH-1 mutation to be able to grow stomach organoids and perform functional studies on these organoids. Patients with germline CDH-1 mutations who have a 60-70% lifetime risk of developing diffuse gastric cancer who undergo surveillance gastroscopy will be asked to participate in this study. During endoscopy at which most often 30 biopsies are taken for clinical purposes, 6 extra biopsies from normal gastric mucosa will be taken, placed in medium and transported to the Hubrecht institute (HI). When tissue samples go to HI they will be provided to our collaborators that perform growth optimisation studies and/or characterisation studies. Upon successful establishment of an organoid line from the donated tissue, experiments involving genetic manipulation of the CDH1 gene will be performed. Logistic issues and protocol of transportation will be established with ‘PA klinische studies’ (Involved pathologist L. Kodach).

name: IRBb20-262 Onderzoek naar de resistentie mechanismen van endocriene therapie en chemotherapie bij borstkanker: Een translationeel onderzoeksproject van de EORTC 10041/BIG 3-04 MINDACT studie (Het MINDACT Recidief Project)
description:
In this study tumor tissue of relapsed breast cancer will be collected for patients who participated in the EORTC-10041 MINDACT trial. The tumor tissue to be collected for the retrospective part is already available in the hospitals and was previously collected with a biopsy/surgerey as part of diagnosis or treatment of the patient (according to standard procedures of the hospital).
Furthermore, if available, normal tissue (non-malignant) will be collected. This can be either a blood sample, or tissue block, for example a block of normal breast tissue from the edge of the surgical specimen at time of the primary breast cancer. 
These tissues will be sent to the Integrated BioBank of Luxembourg (IBBL). There they will be matched to the Original tissue sample of the primary breast cancer that is stored there, and then sent to the Central Laboratories where the actual research on the tissues will be performed. 
All tissues that are left over after these analyses will be shipped back to IBBL to be stored there for future research (if the patient consents to this).   
Any left-over materials can always be returned to the site upon request.

name: IRBb20-284 The BETER-REFLECT Biobank: a REsource For studies on Late Effects of Cancer Treatment
description:
Due to the introduction of multi-agent chemotherapy and improved radiation techniques, Hodgkin lymphoma has become the prototype of a curable malignancy. While the number of long-term lymphoma survivors is increasing, their life expectancy is compromised by the occurrence of late complications of chemotherapy and radiotherapy which may emerge several decades after initial treatment. Especially second malignant neoplasms and cardiovascular diseases cause substantial excess morbidity and mortality. 

The nationwide BETER consortium (Better care after (non-)Hodgkin lymphoma, Evaluation of long-term Treatment; Effects and screening Recommendations) is initiated to reduce the morbidity and mortality from late adverse events of treatment in lymphoma survivors treated at ages 15-60 years and who survived 5 years or longer. 

The aim is to establish a national biobank 'BETER-REFLECT' with biospecimens of all5-year lymphoma survivors identified through the Dutch BETER consortium project in order to examine genetic susceptibility for treatment-related adverse events and to examine early biomarkers for adverse events. The biobank will be integrated with clinical data stored in the established national BETER database and will become an (inter)national resource for late effects research.

name: IRBb20-320 Liquid biopsies for improving the pre-operative diagnosis of ovarian cancer
description:
This is a investigator-initiated, prospective case-control study.
450 will be included in 7 participating centers.
Women with a suspected malignant ovarian tumor referred to a center for gynecological oncology or one of the four affiliated hospitals for surgery.

From all participants 5 extra veils of blood (50ml) will be collected during a clinical ordered blood withdrawal, one EDTA-tube and four STRECK tubes, the liquid biopsies. 
Questionnaires on the QoL and CEA will be filled in on two separate moments: before surgical procedure and 8 – 10 weeks after.

ctDNA and TEPs will be analysed at the participating laboratories, mentionned above. 

Clinical data, postoperative pathology reports and sequencing data from ctDNA and TEPs will be matched to develop the diagnostic algorithm for diagonizing ovarian cancer. 

Primary aim: We will develop a diagnostic algorithm using ct-DNA and TEPs sequencing data in combination with the existing ultrasound models to differentiate between early ovarian cancer and benign ovarian tumors pre-operatively, with a sensitivity of at least 90% and a specificity of at least 80%, in patients with an ovarian tumor referred to a specialized center for surgery. 
We will use 180 malignant and 180 benign ovarian tumors to creat the algorithm. 

Secondary aims:
We wil calculate the cost-effectiveness of the developed algorithm in the triage of patients with an ovarian tumor
And we will evaluate the psychological burden of the uncertainty of having cancer or not before surgical treatment.

For example from patients receiving different treatments or just to study the immune system in cancer patients in general. name: IRBb21-227 Blood and tissue sampling to find biomarkers for early diagnosis and individualizing treatment in breast cancer
description:
In this breast cancer biobank, we aim to to combine the various NKI breast cancer biobanks (B16BHW, B16NBC) into one overarching biobank in order to collect various biospecimens, simplify logistics, and stimulate collaborations within the institute. The protocol is written to function as a platform for current and future research. The biobank may include anyone who presents at the NKI-AVL for 1) analysis/treatment of a lesion in the breast or associated regions (benign or malignant), 2) screening because of increased risk of breast cancer, or 3) a second opinion when diagnosed with in situ carcinoma or invasive breast cancer. Blood and tissue samples will be collected once or multiple times, depending on the patient characteristics, such as breast cancer stage and treatment schedule. Demographics, clinical data, pathology data, imaging data, and genetic data will be obtained and linked to parameters derived from the biomaterials. Data will be collected by the researchers in Castor EDC.

Patients participating in the biobanking will either undergo a single blood withdrawal at baseline (simplified patient information PIF1) and/or will be asked for follow-up blood withdrawals and tissue collection (PIF2). In general, all patients presenting at the outpatient clinic with a lesion in the breast (including DCIS) may be asked for part 1 of the study. Only patients with invasive breast tumors, receiving treatment in the NKI, will be asked to participate in part 2 of the biobank. For more details, please see the full protocol. Tumor tissue may be collected during a routine investigation (standard of care or clinical trial-related) or therapeutic/palliative surgery. In some cases the investigators may request additional biopsies for the biobank. All researchers with a specific research question in need of materials collected in the biobank may use the proposed logistics of the protocol via their research-specific IRB application.

name: IRBb21-234 Bioimmunoradiotherapy (BIR) with concurrent Avelumab, Cetuximab and Radiotherapy as first line treatment in patients with locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. A feasibility study in patients unfit for cisplatin.
description: In patients with locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), unfit for cisplatin treatment with Bioradiation, i.e. concurrent radiotherapy and anti-EGFR (i.e. cetuximab), the 5-years overall survival is 45.6%. Addition of immunecheckpoint inhibitors, e.g. anti-PD1 or anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibodies to Bioradiation might ameliorate treatment outcome in SCCHN via specific T-cell responses raised against viral antigens (i.e. in case of HPV positive SCCHN) or neo-antigens (i.e. HPV negative and positive SCCHN). This study aims to explore the feasibility of BioImmunoRadiotherapy (BIR), i.e. concurrent anti-EGFR (i.e. cetuximab), anti-PD-L1 (i.e. avelumab) and radiotherapy with anti-PD-L1 maintenance in 10 patients with locally advanced SCCHN, who are not suitable for concurrent chemoradiation. Although the total amount of included patients in this trial won’t enable definitive conclusions, tissue biopsies obtained from primary tumors or involved lymph nodes prior and at day 14 (± 2 days) after start of treatment will be used to investigate therapy induced changes in tumor microenvironment. Analyses may include, but not necessarily be limited to measurement of different subsets of T-cells (e.g. CD4, CD8, FoxP3), Macrophages (e.g. CD68, CD163, CD206), CD137, PD-1 and PD-L1 within the tumor and tumor border or within the involved lymph node. In addition changes in tumor microenvironment will be compared in HPV positive and HPV negative tumors. In addition in sequential bloodsamples activation markers of the complement system en neutrophils will be assessed.

name: Arrhythmia genetics in the Netherlands
description: The AGNES case-control set consists of individuals with a first acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction. AGNES cases have ECG- registered ventricular fibrillation occurring before reperfusion therapy for an acute and first ST-elevation myocardial infarction. AGNES controls are individuals with a first acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction but without ventricular fibrillation. All cases and controls are recruited at seven heart centers in The Netherlands. The investigators' exclude individuals with an actual non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, prior myocardial infarction, congenital heart defects, known structural heart disease, severe comorbidity, electrolyte disturbances, trauma at presentation, recent surgery, previous coronary artery bypass graft or use of class I and III antiarrhythmic drugs. Individuals who develop ventricular fibrillation during or after percutaneous coronary intervention are not eligible. Furthermore, because early reperfusion limits the opportunity of developing ventricular fibrillation, potential control subjects undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention within 2 h after onset of myocardial ischemia symptoms were not included. This time interval is based on the observation that >90% of cases develop ventricular fibrillation within 2 h after onset of the complaint of symptoms.

name: Cognitive decline in older patients with ESRD
description:
The COPE study is a prospective, multicenter cohort study in the Netherlands, including prevalent and incident pre-dialysis patients ≥65 years old with eGFR ≤20 ml/min/1.73 m2, awaiting either dialysis or conservative care initiation. At baseline extensive data is collected including a comprehensive geriatric assessment and laboratory tests. Brain and cardiac MRI for analysis of structural and functional abnormalities are performed at baseline and repeated following therapy change. All other measurements are repeated annually during four years of follow up, including an extra evaluation six months after initiation of dialysis.
Study objectives are as follows: Firstly, to examine the severity of cognitive impairment in older patients reaching ESRD before dialysis and the rate of decline after dialysis or CCM initiation. Secondly, to study the association of blood biomarkers for microvascular damage and MRI derived measurements of small vessel disease with the rate of cognitive decline. Thirdly, to examine to what extent cardiac function is related to brain structure and perfusion in patients reaching ESRD. Finally, to study the association of cognitive and functional capacity with quality of life in pre-dialysis patients, as well as after dialysis or CCM initiation.

name: Healthy Aging  Through Internet Counselling  in the Elderly
description:
The overall aim of HATICE was to develop a comprehensive, innovative internet-based intervention strategy for optimisation of management of elderly with multiple cardiovascular risk factors or diseases to improve healthy aging. In HATICE, this widely applicable and generic intervention strategy is immediately put to the test of an investigator-initiated randomised controlled trial.

To this end HATICE has been divided into three phases, which are closely related and which interact with each other:

Phase 1
Development of a shared data platform for optimisation of pooled data from different RCTs.

Phase 2
Development of a generic internet-based intervention platform to optimise treatment of elderly with multiple cardiovascular diseases and risk factors.

Phase 3
Randomised controlled clinical trial for optimisation of management of elderly with multiple cardiovascular diseases and risk factors.
Specific objectives to achieve this general aim of HATICE are:

1. To compare various treatment regimens to determine which aspects of multi-component interventions are most effective in management of elderly patients with multiple cardiovascular diseases and risk factors
2. To identify different target populations (based on age, gender, ethnicity, socio-economic status, cultural background) which can benefit from different approaches
3. To develop a generic, standardised, internationally applicable internet-based intervention strategy specifically targeted at elderly with multiple cardiovascular diseases and risk factors
4. To design this platform in a way that it can be incorporated in different health care systems and be of added value to existing health care structures
5. To develop a state-of-the-art adverse event monitoring system incorporated in the internet-based intervention platform
6. To evaluate the efficacy of this internet-based intervention in a randomised controlled trial, with optimisation of management of cardiovascular disease and risk factors as primary outcome and incident cardiovascular disease, disability, cognitive decline, depression, QOL, mortality and institutionalisation as main secondary outcomes
7. To evaluate whether an internet-based intervention strategy improves independent living, social cohesion, patient empowerment and reduces depression
8.To model the costs and effects of an internet-based strategy targeted at multiple cardiovascular diseases and risk factors in older persons

This multi-centre randomized placebo-controlled study will look into the effect of vedolizumab to prevent recurrence of CD after ileocolonic resection. All patients will undergo an ileocolonoscopy at week 26 following surgery (in line with current recommendations). The endpoint is the proportion of patients with clinically significant recurrence of CD (Modified Rutgeerts Grade 2b, 3 or 4) after 6 months after surgery.
In most centers across the world, patients in the postoperative phase are routinely undergoing ileocolonoscopy 6 months after surgery. To justify a 50% placebo-arm, we will exclude patients with an unfavorable disease course or severe perianal fistulas.
Primary Objectives:
To evaluate the safety and efficacy of vedolizumab (VDZ) to prevent severe postoperative endoscopic recurrence of CD (Modified Rutgeerts Grade 2b, 3 or 4) after 6 months. This outcome measure has been a reliable predictor of the further clinical course of CD.Secondary Objectives:
To evaluate the safety and efficacy of vedolizumab (VDZ) to prevent postoperative clinical recurrence of CD after 6 months.
To evaluate the safety of VDZ in postoperative CD.

The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients with clinically significant endoscopic recurrence (Rutgeerts i2b, i3 or i4) at week 26. All endoscopic procedures will be video-taped for later review.
Secondary endpoints for this study are:
- Proportion of patients without endoscopic recurrence (i0)
- Symptomatic recurrence (CDAI increase >70 points compared to baseline)
- Proportion of patients with normalized serum CRP at all time points and CRP at all visits
- Proportion of patients with normal fecal calprotectin (<50) at all visits
- Quality of life measured by IBDQ and SF-36
- Serum concentrations of vedolizumab and antibodies to vedolizumab before every infusion

name: Advanced understanding of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infections in EuRopE â€“ Intensive Care Units
description:
The epidemiology of ICU pneumonia, caused by S. aureus and P. aeruginosa in Europe has not been fully described, in part due to variation in the case definitions and surveillance systems utilized by European countries. Efforts to standardize assessments of disease measures in hospitals
across different countries are hampered by temporal and geographic variation in disease risk. In this era of decreasing availability of effective therapies for multidrug-resistant bacteria, new approaches are required to prevent and treat infections caused by these bacteria. Targeted prophylaxis or therapy with mAb is a promising intervention that may be used in the future in selected patient populations at risk for acquiring specific nosocomial infections. Prospective studies are required to assess possible risk factors by which we can identify subsets of patients that may benefit most from new interventions. Thus, the goal of this proposed study is to systematically assess the impact of patient-related and contextual factors on the incidence of S. aureus and P. aeruginosa ICU pneumonia in Europe and to identify the patient subgroups that are at greater risk for disease and bear a disproportionate disease burden. Understanding the patient populations at risk for developing this HAI is essential to support future clinical trials of effective interventions.

name: Nationwide prospective study on community-acquired bacterial meningitis: from genetics to therapy
description: Our objectives are to identify and characterize host genetic traits and bacterial virulence factors controlling occurrence and outcome of bacterial meningitis. In a nationwide prospective cohort study, using pathway and total exome sequencing, we will search for genetic variants in 2000 patients with community-acquired bacterial meningitis and 2000 controls. On the pathogen side, using whole genome sequencing, we will systematically search for new bacterial virulence factors in the 2000 causative bacteria. Subsequently, by analyzing clinical data, serum and cerebrospinal fluid, we will examine the potential impact and functionality of these host and pathogen factors. Next, we will validate and explore our findings in an animal model of meningitis and investigate whether treatment against these specific components can improve outcome. Finally, we will initiate an open-access European database on the genetics in bacterial meningitis. In addressing our objectives, I will combine my expertise in bacterial meningitis with groundbreaking, translational approaches using clinical data, human samples, next generation sequencing, in vitro techniques, and a mouse model. The results of this project will be translated into novel therapeutic strategies to advance patient care and will also be important for the development of disease prevention and vaccines.

name: Physical Activity and Dietary intervention in OVArian cancer (PADOVA): a RCT evaluating effects on body composition, physical function, and fatigue
description:
In this single blind randomized controlled trial, patients with ovarian cancer are randomly allocated to a combined exercise and dietary intervention or a waitlist control group. The primary aim is to evaluate the effectiveness of a combined supervised exercise and dietary intervention in women receiving chemotherapy treatment for ovarian cancer. The secondary aim is to conduct an extensive process evaluation to get insight into how and why this intervention is (in)effective.

Primary outcomes are body composition, physical function and fatigue. Secondary outcomes include physical activity and fitness, body mass index, dietary intake, health-related quality of life and symptoms related to ovarian cancer and its treatment (pain, fatigue, nausea/vomiting, neuropathy), anxiety and depression, sleep disturbances, chemotherapy completion rates, and behavior determinants. Outcome measures will be assessed at baseline before randomization and the start of chemotherapy (T0), three weeks after completion of chemotherapy (T1), and 12 weeks later (T2). In addition, blood samples will be drawn at T0 and T1, and a process evaluation will be conducted.

name: Platelet RNA as biomarker for delayed Cerebral lschemia in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
description:
Rationale: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a relatively rare subtype of hemorrhagic stroke with a devastating outcome: a mortality of 32-39% and a permanent disability rate of 50% among the survivors. Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) is a common complication, which develops between day three and day 12 after ictus and contributes significantly to a poor clinical outcome. DCI has a complex multifactorial pathophysiology, existing of both cerebral vasospasm and several key pathophysiological pathways, including cortical spreading depolarisations, endothelial dysfunction, microthrombosis, neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. As a result of this not fully understood complex pathophysiology no sufficiently effective diagnostic test nor treatment strategy has been found yet.
Platelet RNA as biomarker has proven to be an accurate diagnostic and prognostic tool in primary and metastatic brain tumors. Consequently, this diagnostic method had been investigated in other brain diseases, e.g. Alzheimer’s disease, epilepsy and multiple sclerosis. The use of platelet RNA as biomarker for DCI in SAH may contribute to improved selection and identification of DCI-development, possibly resulting in a more efficient management and improved outcome of these patients.
Objective: The main objective of this study is to determine whether platelet RNA analysis can identify patients at risk of developing DCI after an SAH. Secondly, this study will evaluate whether platelet RNA analysis can predict clinical outcome in patients who develop DCI after SAH. Finally, if these objectives can be met, this study will evaluate whether 1) patients with DCI development show chronic changes in platelet RNA-profile six months after SAH. 2) specific subtypes of SAH (aneurysmal/perimesencephalic/angio-negative) show a distinguished platelet RNA-profile, 3) other common complications of SAH show a significantly different platelet RNA-profile, 4) to evaluate the influence of tranexamic acid on platelet RNA profiles, 5) to evaluate whether hypercoagulability can predict onset of DCI in SAH patients. Also, this study might provide biological observational insight into the role of platelets in the pathophysiology of DCI.

name: Biobank: Archipelago of Ovarian Cancer Research (VUmc)
description:
Elk jaar krijgen in Nederland ongeveer 1300 vrouwen de diagnose eierstokkanker. Bij het merendeel van de vrouwen is ten tijde van de diagnose de ziekte al in een vergevorderd stadium (FIGO IIB en hoger). De standaardbehandeling bestaat uit een combinatie van chirurgie en chemotherapie. Momenteel is de (chirurgische) behandeling van eierstokkanker gecentraliseerd in Centra voor Gynaecologische Oncologie (CGOs). De chirurgische behandeling wordt altijd uitgevoerd onder leiding van een gynaecoloog-oncoloog. Ondanks deze centralisatie van zorg, nieuwe chirurgische technieken en nieuwe systemische therapie is de langetermijnoverleving van vrouwen met eierstokkanker de afgelopen 25 jaar niet verbeterd.
Onderzoek naar nieuwe behandelingsmogelijkheden voor eierstokkanker (klinisch onderzoek) wordt vaak in samenwerkingsverband uitgevoerd. Echter, fundamenteel onderzoek (onderzoek naar de oorzaak van een ziekte) en translationeel onderzoek (het vertalen van fundamenteel onderzoek naar de praktijk) naar eierstokkanker worden, vanwege de kleinschaligheid, veelal op individuele basis uitgevoerd door (academische) ziekenhuizen. Om fundamenteel en translationeel onderzoek te centraliseren, is structurele samenwerking, uniformiteit en overzicht nodig. Dit zal ervoor zorgen dat Parelreglement Parel Ovariumcarcinoom – Archipelago of Ovarian Cancer Research (AOCR) de uitvoering van wetenschappelijk onderzoek naar eierstokkanker vergemakkelijkt wordt en de resultaten sneller in de praktijk toegepast zullen worden.

name: Faecal Metabolomics and Microbiota as Non-Invasive Biomarkers for Disease Activity and to Predict Treatment Response in Paediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease
description: In this proposed study, the aim is to validate previously described (pilot) study results in a larger cohort of pediatric IBD patients and to develop microbiota-metabolomics based algorithms for diagnostics, monitoring and predicting therapy response in IBD. We hypothesize that specific alterations in the core of the gut microbiota composition are associated with the onset of paediatric IBD. These findings may be used to develop a microbiota-metabolomics based diagnostic tool to be used in clinical practice. We will collect both mucosal ileal/colonic samples and faecal samples for investigating gut microbiota. In this way, we aim to compare paired faecal and biopsy profiles within each patient at baseline to assess the extent of community structure. Additionally, we will search for immunological factors in mucosal biopsies and blood samples to widen our knowledge about the pathophysiology of paediatric IBD on one hand and investigate their role in predicting treatment response on the other

name: Serologic Surveillance SARS-CoV2 in healthcare workers
description: Measuring serologic response in this population also allows for determining the presence and effect of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) in COVID-19, which is an effect that has been demonstrated in the SARS-CoV outbreak and also in dengue and can increase severity of disease and mortality.(1,2) Specifically, individuals with prior low dengue antibody titres have been shown to have higher risk for severe disease or death compared to both unexposed individuals and individuals with high dengue antibody titres.(2) Therefore, previous exposure to related but different (heterotopic) dengue strains is thought to be a risk factor for severe disease. Since current mortality estimates of COVID-19 vary significantly between regions, it is hypothesized that prior exposure to other (non-SARS-CoV-2) coronaviruses like those that cause cold-like illnesses in the Netherlands may influence disease course. We hypothesize that individuals with prior antibody titres for these other coronaviruses are at increased risk for a more severe disease course.

name: The follow up of pregnant women who received COVID‐19 vaccination through the Dutch national vaccination program
description: Thus far over 64 million people worldwide have been infected with the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) resulting in over 3 million global deaths (WHO Coronavirus (COVID-19) Dashboard | WHO Coronavirus (COVID-19) Dashboard With vaccination Data) (1), but understanding the effect of SARS-CoV-2 on pregnant women is still incomplete. Although severe COVID-19 illness is uncommon, compared to non-pregnant women of the same age, pregnant women are more likely to require admission to an intensive unit predominantly in the third trimester when the diaphragm is moved up from its pre-pregnancy position (2). Due to scarcity of studies on safety data, most effective novel drugs are contraindicated for pregnant women. These factors show that pregnant women are important candidates or preventive measures, of which vaccination is gold standard (3). Pregnancy is an immunotolerant state and therefore the immune responses to vaccination in pregnant women cannot be assumed from that in non-pregnant women. Knowledge on the immune response after COVID-19 vaccination in pregnant women is an urgent matter. From other widely used vaccinations in pregnancy, such as influenza and pertussis, the goal of vaccination in pregnancy is twofold: to protect both the pregnant woman and her offspring, for which antibody response and trans placental antibody transfer are prerequisite. Thus far, it is unknown which trimester of pregnancy offers the best vaccine efficacy in terms of maternal protection by antibody response and fetal protection by antibody transfer. This is an important knowledge gap; as recent CDC data indicate that infants aged 0 to 2 months comprise 20% of all COVID-19 hospitalizations among children below 18 years (4). Initially the Dutch Society of Obstetrics and Gynaecology (NVOG) advised to vaccinate pregnant women with occupational SARS-CoV-2 exposure and women at increased risk for severe or critical COVID-19 only. As of April 22 2021, the NVOG changed this advice (Update standpunt ‘Vaccinatie tegen COVID-19 rondom zwangerschap en kraambed’ | NVOG) (5) and currently advocates to vaccinate all pregnant women.

name: Amsterdam UMC Sickle Cell Disease Biobank (VUmc-zijde)
description:
Rationale: Sikkelcelziekte (SCZ) is een ernstige, erfelijke multi-systeemziekte, waarbij abnormaal hemoglobine wordt aangemaakt. Ondanks dat sikkelcelziekte veroorzaakt wordt door een enkele genmutatie, is deze ziekte klinisch erg heterogeen. Zelfs binnen hetzelfde genotype is er veel variabiliteit in de klinische presentatie en zijn complicaties dus heterogeen en slecht te voorspellen. Op dit moment zijn er (nog) niet voldoende biomarkers van bekend, die bij kunnen dragen in de management van sikkelcelziekte. Voor het identificeren van biomarkers is het van belang om niet alleen materiaal van volwassenen met SCZ, maar juist ook materiaal van kinderen met SCZ te gebruiken. Dit, omdat het op kinderleeftijd zeer moeilijk is om kinderen met toekomstige orgaanschade en complicaties te onderscheiden van patiënten met een milder beloop. De enige curatieve behandeling van sikkelcelziekte is hematopoiëtische stamceltransplantatie wat bij voorkeur op jonge leeftijd wordt gedaan wanneer de mate van orgaanschade nog beperkt is. Om deze reden is het van groot belang biomarkers te ontwikkelen die van hulp kunnen zijn om de groep van kinderen met een infaust beloop te herkennen. Biomarkers kunnen van waarde zijn voor het vroegtijdig opsporen en voorspellen van orgaanschaden en het tijdig initiëren van preventieve therapieën. Met het includeren van kinderen in de AMC-SCD biobank, worden er patiënten die op moment van inclusie nog geen of weinig complicaties hebben maar waarvan een deel dit in loop van de jaren daarna zal ontwikkelen. Daarom is het noodzakelijk om het onderzoek naar nieuwe biomarkers juist op jonge leeftijd uit te voeren. Daarnaast kunnen er leeftijdsspecifieke factoren zijn die de biomarkers kunnen beïnvloeden, dit is onder andere van toepassing voor metabole biomarkers. Om optimaal bij te dragen aan het verbeteren van de ziektemanagement van SCZ en het identificeren van nieuwe en betrouwbare biomarkers (onder andere voor de preventie van SCZ gerelateerde complicaties) is het daarom belangrijk om materiaal van zowel volwassenen als jonge en oudere kinderen te gebruiken voor het toekomstige biomarker onderzoek.
Doel: Het doel van deze AMC-SCD biobank is het verzamelen van lichaamsmateriaal van patiënten met sikkelcelziekte voor toekomstig onderzoek. Het verzamelde materiaal zal gebruikt worden om meer inzicht krijgen in de genotype-fenotype interactie bij patiënten met sikkelcelziekte. Zo kunnen uitkomstmaten als ziekte-ernst, ziekteheterogeniteit, response op behandeling en andere gezondheid gerelateerde uitkomstmaten in de toekomst onderzocht worden. Dit onderzoek met als doel de verbetering van de ziektemanagement van sikkelcelziekte.

name: PRISM2: Exploring biological measures to facilitate the discovery and development of new treatments for social and cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s disease, schizophrenia, and major depression: replication and generalisability of the PRISM1 study
description: The PRISM 2 project also has several specific objectives associated with the biobank. For example, we aim to replicate the finding from the original PRISM project that found epigenetic patterns, as represented by the biotype score, are negatively associated with social functioning in patients with SZ, AD, and in HCs in a transdiagnostic manner. The results and interpretation of epigenetic analyses become far more powerful if they can be linked to alterations at the DNA, RNA, and proteome level (Sun and Hu, 2016). For example, if epigenetic alterations are found on inflammatory genes, we can then also measure inflammatory processes within RNA, DNA, and the proteome, in order to better test and understand our findings. As such, DNA and RNA isolation from PRISM 2 blood samples will allow transcriptomic and proteomic profiling. This will support the exploration of inflammation, synaptic integrity, and neurodegeneration gene expression in peripheral blood samples as biomarkers of transdiagnostic clinical phenotypes; an objective of PRISM 2. More focused approaches, such as RT-qPCR, mass spectrometry, and immunoassays, can then be used to verify the identified genes and pathways as biomarkers of transdiagnostic clinical phenotypes. The PRISM 2 project also aims to determine multivariate relationships between identified biomarkers and demographic characteristics, that can predict social functioning, irrespective of clinical diagnosis.

name: IcoSApent ethyL to slow down aortic VAlve stenosis proGrEssion (SALVAGE-study)
description:
Rationale: Aortic valve stenosis (AVS) is a slowly progressive disease, characterized by calcification of the aortic valve. Once AVS becomes severe and symptomatic, valve replacement is the only treatment. Medical treatment to delay AVS progression is warranted. Fatty acid metabolism has been implicated as a causal risk factor for AVS. Objective: To study the impact of icosapent ethyl on AVS progression, as compared to matching placebo.

name: A care path for the detection of advanced NAFLD-fibrosis: the NLA2 biobank
description:
Rationale: Niet-alcoholische leververvetting (NAFLD) neemt de afgelopen decennia sterk toe in prevalentie en ernst, in directe samenhang met de toename van obesitas en diabetes mellitus type 2. Heden komt NAFLD voor bij 22% van de volwassen Nederlanders, en NAFLD met leverfibrose bij 5%. De laatste jaren komen de ernstige NAFLD-stadia, zoals ernstige fibrose, levercirrose en hepatocellulair carcinoom steeds meer voor.
NAFLD is een complexe multifactoriële ziekte die in relatie staat met vele metabole en inflammatoire processen. Voor toekomstig onderzoek is het dus van grote waarde om informatie te kunnen verkrijgen uit menselijk materiaal van personen met NAFLD. Het veld van NAFLD-onderzoek is groeiende en onderzoek naar verscheidende biomarkers in bloed wordt veelvuldig in toenemende mate uitgevoerd. In het Amsterdam UMC is echter nog geen bestaande grote biobank met materiaal van patiënten met NAFLD. De NLA2 studie is de eerste studie waar op ruime schaal bloed wordt afgenomen van patiënten in de breedte van het hele ziektespectrum, variërend van ernstige tot niet ernstige gevallen. Doordat bij alle patiënten van het NLA2 cohort meerdere niet-invasieve testen worden verricht, is dit een zeer waardevolle populatie voor toekomstig onderzoek met lichaamsmateriaal. Mede aangezien de huidige, en naar alle waarschijnlijkheid toekomstige, diagnostiek in toenemende mate leunt op deze niet-invasieve testen.
Doel: De “NLA2 studie biobank” heeft als doel het opslaan en beheren van bloedmonsters verkregen van patiënten met (een verdenking op) ernstige NAFLD ten behoeve van toekomstige onderzoeksvragen op het gebied van leververvetting.

name: Role of the central brain clock in the pathophysiology of insulin resistance
description:
Rationale: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has an increasing worldwide incidence. Insulin resistance is a key pathophysiological process in the development of hyperglycemia in patients with T2DM. Disruption of circadian synchrony leads to insulin resistance. Animal studies and post-mortem human brain studies suggest that the master brain clock in the hypothalamic suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) plays a role in the development of insulin resistance. Up to now, no-one has investigated whether the in vivo activity rhythm of the SCN is affected in patients with insulin resistance. We hypothesize that the master brain clock has an important role in the development of human insulin resistance.
Objective: To determine the activity rhythm of the SCN in humans with progressive stages of insulin resistance using advanced functional brain imaging (7 Tesla functional MRI).

name: Minimally invasive detection of early Alzheimer’s disease pathology at the eye clinic using blood tests and eye-scans: the BeyeOMARKER study
description:
Rationale: A biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis currently requires expensive and sometimes invasive procedures that are only accessible in highly specialized clinics (i.e. a lumbar puncture or amyloid positron emission tomography (PET)). Consequently, the time to diagnosis in current clinical practice is relatively long and this contributes to the increasing societal and economic disease burden of AD. Early detection of AD is expected to significantly improve early patient management and, forward-looking, selection for disease modifying therapies. To progress towards this goal, accessible, low-cost, and minimally invasive biomarkers for AD are imperative. Currently, blood based biomarkers (e.g. markers for plasma phospo-tau (p-tau) isoforms, amyloid beta (Aβ), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and Neurofilament light (NfL)) and eye-based biomarkers (e.g. hyperspectral (HS) retinal scanning) are emerging as highly promising tools to distinguish between subjects with and without AD pathology. Thus far, studies on these biomarkers did not resemble “real-world” clinical application as these were mostly retrospective, included participants with high diagnostic certainty, few medical comorbidities and did not use  priori defined cut-offs. The BeyeOMARKER study aims to provide real-world proof-of-concept for early detection of AD pathology outside the memory clinic through prospective evaluation of plasma p-tau (and complementary HS retinal scanning) in an eye clinic with high patient-throughput. Eye clinics are an important setting with a high likelihood of early detection of AD given (1) the high patient throughput of patients within the age-range where AD typically starts (i.e. 50-80 years old) and (2) an increased risk of AD pathology individuals presenting with visual impairment (e.g. HR = 1.47 and 1.26 for visual impairment and cataract, respectively). Furthermore, visual impairment may mask cognitive complaints leading to significant diagnostic delays and underrepresentation of these individuals in clinical studies. Altogether, the BeyeOMARKER study utilizes this unique setting to assess whether these novel tools can facilitate early detection of AD and an accelerated diagnostic process in this clinically relevant group. 
Objective: The primary aim is to (1) evaluate the real-world predictive value of blood- and eye?based biomarkers for detection of AD-related clinical progression and biological changes in eye clinics. Secondly, we aim (2) to assess the individual and complementary clinical predictive 
value of blood-based biomarkers and retinal scanning through multivariate modelling of clinical outcomes, (3) to provide head-to-head comparison of the accuracy of blood- and eye-based biomarkers for early detection of AD pathophysiology, (4) to explore the pathophysiological mechanisms linking AD and eye disease by comparing the clinical and neurobiological manifestation of AD in the BeyeOMARKER cohort against a traditional memory clinic cohort, (5) to investigate enrichment for AD in an eye clinic population based on a relative) prevalence estimate of p-tau positivity, and (6) to ultimately provide a roadmap for future studies on minimally invasive early detection of AD in alternative diagnostic settings.

Het gebruik van bloed-biomarkers om te screenen naar Alzheimer is een nieuw en snel ontwikkelend veld. Op het moment worden nog constant nieuwe potentiele biomarkers gevonden, worden bestaande assays verbeterd en worden verschillende combinaties van markers getest om de detectie van Alzheimer pathologie te verbeteren. oogziekten en de ziekte van Alzheimer door klinische en neurobiologische uitkomsten van het BeyeOMARKER cohort te vergelijken met een standaard cohort uit de geheugenkliniek, (5) om verrijking voor Alzheimer pathologie in de oogkliniek te onderzoeker op basis van een (relatieve) prevalentie van p?tau positiviteit, en (6) om uiteindelijk een blauwdruk te maken voor toekomstige studies die onderzoek doen naar minimaal invasieve detectie van de ziekte van Alzheimer in alternatieve instellingen.

description: Het betreft onderzoek naar het verbeteren van de diagnostiek, opvang en behandelingen bij pasgeborenen, waarbij het grootste percentage van de populatie prematuur geboren zal zijn. Deze lange bewaartermijn is gekozen vanwege twee redenen. Ten eerste ondergaat een prematuur pasgeborene, vergeleken met de volwassen populatie een daarna niet meer te evenaren ontwikkeling op alle orgaansystemen, zoals brein, -long, en andere vitale organen tot de adolescente leeftijd. name: Biobank Cardiogenetica
description:
Rationale: De Biobank Cardiogenetica is opgezet om DNA-materiaal, eventueel ander beschikbaar restweefsel, plasma samples en gegevens van patiënten met (een verdenking op) een erfelijke hartziekte of personen met een erfelijke hartziekte in de familie te verzamelen, op te slaan en te bewaren ten behoeve van wetenschappelijk onderzoek. Het DNA en de plasma samples zullen samen met de patiëntgegevens worden gebruikt voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek dat zich richt op het beter begrijpen van erfelijke hartziekten, verbetering van het opsporen van erfelijke hartziekten en het verbeteren van de behandelingsmogelijkheden van erfelijke hartziekten. Er wordt bijvoorbeeld onderzoek gedaan naar factoren die bepalen waarom de ene persoon met een erfelijke hartziekte oud wordt zonder klachten en de andere persoon met dezelfde ziekte op jonge leeftijd plots overlijdt. Ook wordt onderzoek gedaan om moleculen te ontdekken die kunnen worden gebruikt voor het ontwikkelen van nieuwe therapieën of voor de evaluatie van de effecten van de nieuwe therapieën.
Doel: Het doel is het verbeteren van de zorg voor mensen met een erfelijke hartziekte middels wetenschappelijk onderzoek gericht op de identificatie van erfelijke factoren die een rol spelen bij het ontstaan van erfelijke hartziekten, het verbeteren van de behandel mogelijkheden voor patiënten met erfelijke hartziekten en participatie aan (internationale) studies. Door bijvoorbeeld te kijken welke klinische parameters geassocieerd zijn met ventrikelfibrilleren bij dragers van een erfelijke aanleg kan preventief een ICD worden geadviseerd aan mensen met een verhoogd risico hierop.

name: Dutch-Depression Outcome trial comparing 5 day multi daily neuronavigated Theta burst sessions with 6 weeks standard rTMS (D-DOTT study)
description:
Rationale: Novel therapies are crucial for patients with unipolar depression since more than 33% of these patients are medication‐resistant. As a consequence, there is a high burden of illness for patients with depression, leading to increased suicide rates, inability to maintain proper work and/or social role functions, and reduced quality of life. A promising novel treatment strategy is an intensive five‐day course of intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS), a form of transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), which could lead to exceptionally high remission rates (79%) in patients with treatment resistant depression. However, it remains unclear whether this novel treatment strategy is more effective in depressed patients when compared to standard 10Hz rTMS (remission 30%).
Hypothesis: 5‐day multi daily neuronavigated iTBS sessions (developed by Stanford University and coined, SNT,
i.e., Stanford NeuromdulaTion protocol) are more (cost‐) effective than standard 10 Hz rTMS in patients with treatment resistant depression.  
Objective: To determine remission of depression and cost effectiveness using the SNT protocol, in patients with treatment resistant depression who did not respond to two or more evidence‐based treatments

name: Multiple Sclerosis treatment with Autologous Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (MS-ACT study)
description:
Rationale: In December 2022, autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (aHSCT) was approved in the Netherlands for reimbursement for patients with treatment refractory relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). The Dutch Healthcare institute (‘Zorginstituut Nederland: ZIN’) requested research of the outcomes of aHSCT for this indication.
Objective: To perform long-term pre-specified follow-up of patients undergoing aHSCT for refractory RRMS.
Study design: This is a multicenter, prospective, long-term observational study. This is a collaboration between departments of neurology and haematology of the two designated centers which offer aHSCT for treatment refractory RRMS patients in the Netherlands (Amsterdam UMC, location VUMC and St Antonius Hospital).

name: Biobank: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
description:
Primaire angiitis van het centraal zenuwstelsel (PACNS) is een zeldzame aandoening, de enige schatting over de incidentie komt uit de Verenigde Staten en bedraagt 2.4 per miljoen persoonsjaren. Ondanks deze lage incidentie is er regelmatig een verdenking op een PACNS aangezien de aandoening een brede differentiaal diagnose heeft die onder andere secundaire vasculitis door infecties, reumatologische systeemziekten of medicatie en het reversibel cerebraal vasoconstrictie syndroom (RCVS) omvat. De diagnose PACNS is notoir moeilijk te stellen en uitgebreid aanvullend onderzoek waaronder een hersenbiopt kan noodzakelijk zijn. Het stellen van de juiste diagnose is erg van belang gezien de verschillen in behandeling bij de verschillende differentiaal diagnostische overwegingen en de invasieve behandeling voor PACNS zelf. Omdat de ziekte zeldzaam en moeilijk te diagnosticeren is, is er nauwelijks iets bekend over de pathogenese en daardoor is er ook weinig bewijs voor de meest optimale behandelstrategie.
Deze biobank zal gebruikt worden voor opslag van materiaal en klinische gegevens van patiënten met de verdenking op PACNS. Doel is om meer inzicht te krijgen in de pathofysiologie, specifieke diagnostische kenmerken in vergelijking met hierop gelijkende aandoeningen en de behandeling van deze ziekte.

name: Pembrolizumab alone versus pembrolizumab‐chemotherapy in first line NSCLC
description: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for more than 85% of all lung cancers. Historically, platinum-based doublet chemotherapy was the standard first-line treatment for metastatic NSCLC in the absence of targetable alterations. Chemotherapy alone produces response rates ranging only between 15-30%. Since the introduction of immunotherapy, the treatment landscape for patients with NSCLC has fundamentally changed. Monoclonal antibodies targeting programmed death-1 (PD-1) and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) have received regulatory approval for first-line treatment in patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Pembrolizumab (a PD-1 monoclonal antibody) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) compared with platinum-based chemotherapy in patients with a PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) of 50% or greater. Indeed, the KEYNOTE-042 showed for patients with a TPS ≥50% a longer OS (HR 0·69, 95% CI 0·56–0·85, p=0·0003). The median survival values were 20·0 months (95% CI 15·4–24·9) for pembrolizumab versus 12·2 months (10·4–14·2) for chemotherapy (Mok et al. 2019). In another study, the KEYNOTE-024, pembrolizumab showed a median OS of 30.0 months (95% CI, 18.3-to not reached) with pembrolizumab and 14.2 months (95% CI, 9.8-19.0) with chemotherapy (HR 0.63; 95% CI, 0.47-0.86) (Martin Reck et al.). In addition; adding pembrolizumab to standard chemotherapy resulted in significantly longer OS and PFS than chemotherapy alone regardless of PD-L1 expression. The KEYNOTE-189 study, showed that pembrolizumab and chemotherapy demonstrated a HR of 0.49 (95% CI 0.38-0.64; P<0.001) and in the subgroup of patients with TPS ≥50% a HR of 0.42 (0.26–0.68). A 12-month overall survival rate was seen of 73.0% vs. 48.1% (HR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.26 to 0.68). So, in patients with PD-L1 ≥50%, both pembrolizumab monotherapy and pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy can be given as a first line option. In practice, pembrolizumab monotherapy is being used as a standard first line therapy because it has less toxicities as compared to pembro?chemotherapy. However, these 2 regimens have not been compared with each other for efficacy yet. Knowing which regimen provides the highest response rate is of importance in situations where a patient needs an urgent tumor response. For example, a newly diagnosed lung cancer that invades mediastinal structures can be quickly life?threatening. In such medical urgencies, clinicians need to know which regimen has the highest likelihood for response. Therefore, the aim of this project is to determine which regimen (pembro mono or pembro-chemo) provides the highest response rates in patients with high tumor burden and high PD-L1 expression.

name: The Netherlands ME/CFS Biobank (NMCB)
description:
Biomedical research into Myalgic Encephalomyelitis and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) in the Netherlands lacks an infrastructure for patient data and sample collections. Even though ME/CF) has an estimated prevalence of 40,000-150,000 patients in the Netherlands, little has been invested in biomedical research into the disease. Most importantly, an infrastructure for patient data and biomaterial collection is lacking. Meanwhile, such research is urgently needed: patients experience debilitating physical symptoms with little hope of spontaneous recovery; in the absence of biomarkers, the diagnosis relies on clinical judgement by excluding other diagnoses; and treatment is symptomatic. Furthermore, ME/CFS is often stigmatised and linked with high unemployment rates, leading to substantial personal and societal costs. To address this situation, ZonMw developed a “ME/CFS Research Agenda” to initiate “substantive and long-term biomedical research into ME/CFS”. The Netherlands ME/CFS Cohort and Biobank (NMCB) consortium was co-created with Dutch patient organisations to implement the clear directives provided by this research agenda. The NMCB mission is to establish a collaborative national research infrastructure that collects and secures high-quality patient data, to allow testing of biomedical hypotheses that will lead to a sound mechanistic understanding of ME/CFS, and to see their translation into rational diagnosis and treatment. The core activity of the NMCB is the establishment of a national patient cohort and biobank at the Amsterdam UMC. Separate projects, from researchers based at the 7 Dutch UMCs that are part of the NMCB consortium, will utilise these resources for research purposes. The NMCB will actively disseminate its data, including bodily materials, to improve the lives of patients and their position in society. Hence, open access and FAIR data management are core principles of the ME/CFS cohort and biobank.
The primary aim of the NMCB is to build a sustainable infrastructure for ME/CFS research by establishing a well-defined ME/CFS patient cohort including relevant clinical and healthy controls, and a corresponding biobank.

name: FeAsiBility of a treatment free interval in newly diagnosed mUltiple myeLOma patients treated with DaratumUmab-Lenalidomide-DexamethaSone – the FABULOUS study
description: In de FABULOUS studie worden patiënten geïncludeerd met multipel myeloom nadat zij een jaar behandeld zijn met de standaardbehandeling met daratumumab-lenalidomide-dexamethason (Dara-Rd). De helft van de geïncludeerde patiënten gaat door met deze standaardbehandeling, terwijl de andere helft van de geïncludeerde patiënten tijdelijk stopt met de behandeling en weer hervat bij biochemische progressie. De duur van het behandelvrij interval zal verschillend zijn, en het is nog niet bekend wat daar de oorzaken van zijn. Tevens is nog niet bekend welke patiënten het meest baat hebben bij een therapievrij interval. Op het materiaal dat wordt verzameld tijdens deze studie kunnen biomarkers voor de duur van het therapievrije interval en de algehele uitkomst worden bestudeerd.

name: AmStErdam Cohort StUdy of Patients at Risk for VEntricular Arrhythmias
description:
Rationale: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is the third leading cause of death in Europe. An implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) can prevent these deaths, but risk assessment for SCD remains challenging. Circulating fibrosis biomarkers might be associated with SCD, but information on the predictive value of these biomarkers is lacking.
Objective: To investigate the predictive value of relevant fibrosis biomarkers identified in literature and to identify new biomarkers that are of predictive value for ventricular arrhythmias (VA).

name: Oral fecal microbiota transplantation capsules from healthy donors in patients with locally advanced, resectable gastric or gastro-esophageal junction adenocarcinoma (CAPGO-study)
description:
Rationale: The gut microbiota has gained attention in recent years as a new target for improving therapy response in cancer. Important links have been established based on (pre)-clinical observations regarding chemotherapy response and the gut microbiota. We recently published that a fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from an allogenic donor is safe and can improve chemotherapy response in metastatic gastroesophageal cancer (GEC) patients. Recently, a new safe and feasible FMT method has been developed using FMT capsules from healthy donors. We hypothesize that FMT capsules in non-metastatic patients can improve chemotherapy response. 
Objective: Confirm the efficacy and safety of allogenic freeze-dried fecal microbiota capsules to modulate the microbiome and thereby improve treatment outcome, reduce adverse events and investigate the gut-immune axis.

name: HOVON 158 NEXT STEP CLL trial studie
description: Voor chronisch lymfatische leukemie (CLL) zijn recent nieuwe, effectieve maar ook kostbare medicamenten ontwikkeld. In tegenstelling tot chemotherapie zijn voorspellende markers voor response en/of resistentie nog niet goed onderzocht. Op het materiaal dat wordt verzameld tijdens klinische studies kunnen klinisch relevante biomarkers worden bestudeerd. De HOVON 158 NEXT STEP CLL trial studie bestudeert een geheel chemotherapievrije behandeling voor CLL patiënten in de eerste behandelingslijn. De behandeling bestaat uit een combinatie van de BTK remmer ibrutinib en een remmer van het anti-celdood eiwit Bcl-2 (venetoclax) gevolgd door intensivering met obinutuzumab alleen voor patiënten die niet in remissie klinisch of biologisch zijn. Tijdens deze studie zal er op vaste momenten bloed voor de biobank worden afgenomen.

name: A prospective randomized phase I/II trial of venetoclax treatment (26 cycles) with 6 cycles or 12 cycles of epcoritamab in patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma
description: Although new targeted inhibitors induce durable responses in  chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and are generally well tolerated, they are not curative. As a consequence, in patients refractory to these inhibitors there is an emerging unmet clinical need for novel treatment strategies. One of the current standard second line treatments is time limited venetoclax plus rituximab therapy. Bispecific antibodies are promising new therapeutics in B cell malignancies. Whether they lead to potent T-cell activation despite described T-cell dysfunction in CLL is currently unknown. Treatment with the BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax results in particular rapid clearance of the blood and the marrow compartment while T-cells are not negatively affected. In this study, efficacy and safety of 2 regimens that combine the CD3-CD20 T-cell engager epcoritamab with venetoclax will be tested in relapsed/refractory CLL and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) patients. The trial starts with a phase I part to establish the recommended phase 2 dose level (RP2D) of epcoritamab in combination with venetoclax for the phase II trial.

name: Immune monitoring after anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy with patients with B-cell NHL
description:
Rationale: Anti‐CD19 CAR T‐cell therapy has revolutionized the treatment of aggressive B‐cell lymphoma and two products are currently registered by EMA and the FDA for the treatment of diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma (DLBCL), primary mediastinal B‐cell lymphoma (PMBCL) and transformed follicular lymphoma (tFL). Although results are impressive, only a minority of patients benefit and toxicity can be severe. Also, since there is a manufacturing time of 4 weeks, not all patients eligible for this treatment will actually receive it, since often patients become too symptomatic in the waiting time. Several mechanisms of failure to respond to CAR T‐cell therapy and/or relapse following initial response are known, such as upregulation of checkpoint molecules, loss of antigen, lack of persistence or T‐cell exhaustion but we still have limited understanding of how we can predict failure or success. However, factors that contribute to T‐cell evasion can be analyzed by ‘immune typing’ tumor and peripheral blood with genetic and molecular techniques, as has been performed successfully in solid tumors.  In order to get better understanding of the specific mechanisms responsible for CAR T‐cell resistance and to identify those patients who benefit from this treatment we need to analyze combined blood and tumor tissue samples, aligned with clinical data, of all patients undergoing this treatment. also, since the field of CAR T‐cell therapy is rapidly expanding, in parallel with the development of techniques by which these resistance mechanisms can be studied, it is important to biobank tissue for future research.
Objective: To determine the factors that contribute anti‐tumour T‐cell evasion in CAR T‐cell therapy, both at the tumour‐end, as well as on the T‐cell side. More specifically, to determine if the expression of checkpoint molecules before infusion, at day 15 post infusion and at relapse are associated with progression free survival (PFS).  A secondary objective is to collect and store biological patient material combined with clinical data in a national Dutch biobank for future research.

description:
The ‘ADAPT’ Biobank is a collection of body material and data from patients with cardiac arrhythmias who underwent or will undergo (non-) invasive treatment for this disease. Its main objective is to obtain a comprehensive collection of patient information and material to facilitate research and gain better insight into the complex pathophysiology of the different arrhythmias, the multifactorial process, the heterogeneity in clinical presentation, and prognosis.
Bodily material is used for biochemical marker assessments, histological and molecular analyses for research in cardiac arrhythmias.

name: Premature atherosclerose (PAS biobank)
description: Vroegtijdige aderverkalking kan leiden tot verschillende hart- en vaatziekten zoals een hartinfarct of tot het langzaam dichtslibben van de aderen rondom het hart, waarvoor een dotterbehandeling of een zogenaamde bypassoperatie van de hartvaten nodig is. Dit is een groot probleem, aangezien dit jonge mensen betreft die plots geconfronteerd worden met een vervelende ziekte. Voor het krijgen van vroegtijdige aderverkalking zijn enkele risicofactoren bekend zoals roken, overgewicht, hoge bloeddruk, suikerziekte en een verhoogd cholesterol. Ook erfelijkheid speelt een grote rol in het krijgen van vroegtijdige aderverkalking. Mensen met deze risicofactoren hebben een hogere kans op hart- en vaatziekten. Ondanks de kennis over deze risicofactoren is in veel gevallen niet bekend waarom mensen vroegtijdige aderverkalking krijgen. Om hier beter inzicht in te krijgen doen wij onderzoek binnen families met veel hart- en vaatziekten. Zo hopen wij in de toekomst meer hart- en vaatziekten te kunnen voorkomen.

name: PLN-biobank
description:
Rationale:
De Stichting PLN is een stichting voor en door patiënten met een mutatie in het PLN-gen. De mutatie in het PLN-gen (PLN p.Arg14del) kan leiden tot een levensbedreigende hartspierziekte die zich kenmerkt door dilatatie en aritmieën. Er zijn nu iets meer dan 1.200 PLN-dragers bekend. Naar schatting zijn er in heel Nederland zo’n 10.000 tot 14.000 PLN-dragers. De Stichting PLN is opgericht met als doel een einde te maken aan de hartspierziekte als gevolg van de PLN-mutatie. Naast het initiëren en stimuleren van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, brengt de stichting PLN de ziekte onder de aandacht, informeert zij haar leden over de laatste ontwikkelingen en brengt zij lotgenoten en hun familie(s) bij elkaar.
Doel:
In lijn met bovenstaande willen NLHI en de Stichting PLN starten met het verzamelen van bloed van patiënten met een PLN-mutatie. Het doel is het prospectief verzamelen en opslaan van bloed met bijbehorende gegevens met het oog op toekomstig fundamenteel en translationeel wetenschappelijk onderzoek voor het testen van potentiële nieuwe behandelmethodes. Dit houdt in er in de toekomst o.a. diverse onderzoekslijnen ontwikkeld zullen worden voor toepasbaar onderzoek op het gebied pluripotente stamcel?hartspiercel onderzoek bij patiënten met de PLN mutatie. Gezien de activiteit waarmee Stichting PLN nieuw onderzoek initieert, voorziet het NLHI veel vraag naar lichaamsmaterialen uit de PLN Biobank. In samenwerking met de farmacie kunnen potentiële behandelmethodes getest worden met materialen uit de PLN Biobank.

name: CovidPredict: central national patient database
description:
We're gathering pseudonymized data on COVID-19 patients from Dutch hospitals. The goal is to better predict the course of COVID-19 patients and to optimise their treatment. Importantly, we ask no time from healthcare workers taking care of COVID-19 patients. There are two parts to this project. First, intensive care data from COVID-19 patients is extracted from electronic health records. The second part involves specialties that are reduced in their workload to fill out case report forms about COVID-19 patients. This project is from all participating Dutch hospitals, and is supported by the NVIC and the NICE foundation. It is coordinated by Amsterdam UMC, Vrije Universiteit, and MUMC.
