In addition, a quality of care questionaire will be filled in and compared with reference measurements in the near past.

name: Surveillance Epidemiology of Corona Virus (COVID-19) Under Research Exclusion - Atopic Dermatitis (SECURE-AD)
description: "Given the interest in the emerging and evolving coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic and the questions regarding how this will impact patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) who are treated with systemic immunomodulating medication, we have created a secure, online, de-identified Personal Health Identifier (PHI)-free reporting registry: www.covidderm.org. SECURE-AD (Surveillance Epidemiology of Corona Virus (COVID-19) Under Research Exclusion - Atopic Dermatitis) is a secure, online, de-identified Personal Health Identifier (PHI)-free international reporting registry for health care providers to report outcomes of COVID-19 in AD patients who are treated with and without systemic immunomodulating medication. By collecting worldwide observational data on cases of COVID-19 in AD patients treated with and without systemic immunomodulating therapy, the SECURE-AD registry will enable description of the impact of COVID-19 on these patients and how factors such as age, comorbidities, and AD systemic immunomodulating treatments impact COVID-19 outcomes. Through broadscale participation and collaboration the data collected through the SECURE-AD registry will benefit the entire AD patient population and international clinical community. SECURE-AD is closely aligned with recently established partner databases for outcomes to COVID-19 in other immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (such as www.covidibd.org, www.psoprotect.org and www.rheum-covid.org). We will continue to collaborate closely with these research teams in order to facilitate valuable cross-disease analyses. Objectives: - To uncover the underlying determinants of the outcome of COVID-19 in patients with AD who are treated with systemic immunomodulating medication, and to investigate if this is influenced by age, sex, ethnicity, and comorbidities. - To determine the impact of COVID-19 on the disease course/severity of atopic dermatitis;-To create a data resource To enrich other allied datasets through cross-disease collaboration: e.g. psoriasis, alopecia areata, inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatology. To create a data resource to enrich other allied datasets through cross-disease collaboration: e.g. psoriasis, alopecia areata, inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatology. This is a registry-embedded case series study of COVID-19 outcomes in AD patients. We will include patients who are treated with immunomodulating therapy and patients who are not treated with immunomodulating therapy as a control group. De-identified real-world observational clinical data is collected using the web-based SECURE-AD case report form. The scope of the study is to investigate disease epidemiology. Healthcare providers are encouraged to upload patient data after the patient has had COVID-19 for a long enough duration to experience partial or complete recovery, hospitalization or death. One case report form will be completed for each patient and should take approximately 5 minutes to complete. All observational data is de-identified. The data includes demographic variables such as age, sex and ethnicity; patient characteristics such as BMI, comorbidities and concomitant medication; date of diagnosis and severity of AD (pre- and post-COVID-19); details of systemic immunomodulating AD treatments and COVID-19 disease course and outcomes. "

name: Study of Tumor Educated Platelets for early detection of breast cancer in blood in BRCA1/2 mutation carriers (STEP)
description:
Rationale: Women with a genetic predisposition for breast cancer (BrCa) due to a BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation have a strongly increased lifetime risk of developing BrCa. As treatment and survival chances of BrCa strongly depend on disease stage, it is paramount that BrCa is detected in the earliest stage possible. Therefore, these women are monitored yearly from age 25 (clinical examination, X-ray/ MRI scans). Current screening strategies with mammography and MRI have suboptimal sensitivity and specificity. In this study, we will validate prospectively a test
for early detection of BrCa in blood. This test is called ThromboSeq and is based on analysis of tumour RNA biomarkers in Tumour Educated Platelets (TEPs). Proof-of-concept studies are highly promising. However, the ThromboSeq test needs validation in a prospective screening
study to evaluate its use for early breast cancer detection in women. In the current study we aim to validate the ThromboSeq test for detection of breast cancer in the specific clinical setting of women with a BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation who are annually being screened for BrCa with MRI
and mammography. Moreover, we will collect additional blood samples of all women for future studies of ctDNA for early detection of cancer in blood. 
Objectives:
- To study sensitivity and specificity of the ThromboSeq test for detection of incident BrCa in a screened population of female BRCA1/2 mutation carriers.
- To compare performance of the the ThromboSeq test with the imaging techniques accounting for interval cancers
- To explore if the ThromboSeq test can detect BrCa earlier in time than current surveillance tools (MRI/mammography) in female BRCA1/2 mutation carriers.
- To set-up a biobank with blood samples of BRCA1/2 mutation carriers undergoing regular breast screening, for future research aimed at early detection of cancer in blood using the ThromboSeq test and other blood markers, like ctDNA.

name: Training and protein recommendations for frail seniors (Study)
description: As society ages, the incidence of physical limitations and frailty is dramatically increasing. For frail community-dwelling older adults, these limitations will lead to assistance in activities of daily living, like in-home care services. An important cause of physical limitations and frailty is the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength and performance also referred to as sarcopenia. Resistance-type exercise training is the most promising intervention to prevent or treat sarcopenia in frail older adults. Evidence of resistance exercise training is based on well-controlled studies, but the current protocols are difficult to apply in daily physiotherapy practice for this frail community-dwelling population. In practice, the execution of the training protocol depends on various resistance exercise training variables (e.g. load, repetitions and volume) and personal characteristics such as frailty status, gender, age, co-morbidity, cognitive and mental performance. In addition, about 40% of the frail community-dwelling older adults receiving in-home services are undernourished. As such, physiotherapists are in need of evidence-based training protocols to optimize skeletal muscle mass, strength and performance for the heterogeneous population of frail community-dwelling older adults. And if applicable, providing evidence-based care in collaboration with the dietician. As adequate dietary protein intake is suggested to be essential to improve skeletal muscle mass, strength and performance during resistance exercise in frail older adults. More research is warranted on the impact of (in)adequate dietary protein intake on resistance exercise training variables and sarcopenia related outcomes.

description: The 2019 pandemic of SARS-CoV-2 causing COVID-19 has led to widespread and significant morbidity and mortality around the world, as well as a severe disruption of daily life. name: Amyloid pathology in cognitively normal elderly subjects
description:
Rationale: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterised by progressive neuronal loss and eventually death. Abnormal aggregation of beta amyloid (A) is the first event in AD and is present in 20-40% of cognitively normal elderly. To design AD prevention trials it is key to find cognitively normal subjects at high risk for amyloid pathology and to find predictors of cognitive decline in these subjects. Previous studies have identified a number of diagnostic and prognostic markers but these need to be replicated. Novel markers may further increase diagnostic and prognostic accuracy.
Objective: The main objectives are to validate known and to discover novel diagnostic markers and risk factors for amyloid pathology in cognitively normal subjects and to validate known and to discover novel predictors for cognitive decline in cognitively normal subjects with amyloid pathology. Secondary objectives are to determine the concordance of amyloid and other AD markers in monozygotic twins, to investigate the overlap between amyloid pathology as assessed in CSF and assessed on PET scan, and to collect normative data for cognitive markers and biomarkers that can be used in clinical practice.

name: Pulmonary Hypertension REversal in Clusters of Patients With ldentical Pathobiological Substrates 6-Mercaptopurine Proof-of-Concept Trial (PRECISE-MP)
description:
Rationale: Background: Pulmonary arterial hypertension is an incurable disease of pulmonary vascular remodelling and right heart failure. Exuberant lung microvascular endothelial proliferation is one of the lead causes of PAH but is currently not specifically targeted by medical treatment. Treatment with 6 mercaptopurine (6-MP) showed encouraging results, mitigating endothelial proliferation in vitro and reversing pulmonary vascular remodelling in relevant animal models. Lung vascular proliferation in PAH patients is heterogeneous, however, and can be estimated by transcriptome analysis of lung educated platelets (LEPs). Patients with a LEPs profile consistent with exuberant proliferation are expected to respond better to 6-MP treatment than patients with LEPs profiles consistent with quiescent lung vascular remodeling. 
Objective: The primary objective of this clinical trial is to obtain pilot safety and efficacy data on treatment of PAH patients by 6-MP. The secondary objective of this clinical trial is to determine whether LEPs transcriptome analysis will identify a subset of PAH patients that 
responds to 6-MP treatment with hemodynamic and functional improvement.

name: The importance of early brain changes in patients with MS with regard to cognitive and physical outcome
description:
Rationale: Within five years after diagnosis, approximately 50% of the patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) develop cognitive decline and 65% of the patients become unemployed, negatively impacting the quality of life. To be able to postpone or ultimately prevent these negative effects of MS, we urgently need to understand which underlying mechanism(s) lead to such a rapid decline in daily functioning and whether we can predict such an early clinical and cognitive decline. Understanding these early changes is key to develop new treatment targets in order to halt the disease, i.e. to identify a window-of-opportunity for early interven-tion. Until now, these very early changes, measured with advanced imaging and biomarkers, remain unknown.
Objective: The main objective of this project is to identify the early brain changes in MS that can be measured by advanced structural and functional (network) imaging measures. Additionally, we will determine how and when these changes relate to clinical and cognitive decline and serum biomarkers. Finally, we will determine which of the measures is most predictive for clinical and cognitive decline in patients with relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS).

name: InFrastructure fOr Rare Cancers in the nEtherlands – Neuroendocrine Neoplasms Multicenter Clinical Biobank (FORCE-NEN)
description:
Background
FORCE is a KWF-funded infrastructure project aiming to improve treatment outcomes of rare cancers by collecting clinical data on patients with rare cancers and by large-scale biobanking of their peripheral blood components and tumour tissue. Data will be collected retrospectively and prospectively and used to build a data warehouse that provides a comprehensive insight into the long-term biology of each rare cancer type. Within FORCE, rare cancers are categorized according to EURACAN domains and the FORCE-NEN Clinical Biobank – the subject of the current Protocol - is dedicated to the Neuroendocrine Neoplasms (NEN) which comprise EURACAN domain 4. 

Aim
FORCE-NEN is a collaboration between the Dutch NEN expert centres in a multicenter clinical biobank aimed to create and maintain a comprehensive collection of clinicopathological data, imaging data and large-scale biobanking of donors with Neuroendocrine Neoplasms. The FORCE-NEN Clinical Biobank will be used for research in the field of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms with the primary goal of determining the value and efficacy of USccfDNA assays in early detection, personalized treatment and follow-up. Secondary goals are (2) identifying and validating novel markers for diagnosis, prognosis and follow-up, therapy stratification and evaluation of treatment (3) Providing comprehensive insight in the long-term biology (4) Improving clinical decision-making (5) Improving treatment outcomes and (6) Early detection. 

Biobank population
Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of Neuroendocrine Neoplasm, ≥18 years or older and treated at one of the participating centres are eligible. Exclusion criteria are (1) a diagnosis of a Small Cell Lung Carcinoma (2) Active malignancy other than NEN at baseline, with exception of non-melanoma skin cancer (3) A known hereditary syndrome causing the Neuroendocrine Neoplasm (4) a diagnosis of a Mixed adeno-neuroendocrine carcinoma (5) Unable to provide informed consent.

name: Development of blood-based monitoring techniques in lymphatic malignancies
description:
Rationale: The aim of this current study is to develop blood-based monitoring techniques in malignant lymphoma’s. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging can be used by clinicians to detect increased metabolic activity in tissues and masses. PET is used for evaluation of the extent of the disease and treatment response in non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). Although PET imaging in general has a high negative predictive value, the downside of PET imaging is a relatively poor positive predictive value and increased radiation burden from repeated scanning for disease monitoring. Hence, there is a clinical need for blood-based monitoring techniques that can be frequently repeated to monitor treatment response and help facilitate personalized treatment per patient. Therefore, blood based methods for monitoring of tumor activity are under development. In a previous study, we were able to detect and quantify genetic disease markers (miRNAs) and protein (TARC) in patient plasma, which levels corresponded with the presence of vital tumor in HL. Hence this method may be an alternative for, or complement to the current PET imaging for monitoring treatment response in lymphoma. Circulating cell free tumor DNA (cfDNA) is another alternative method and is being explored as a companion-diagnostic or treatment monitoring tool for multiple types of solid tumors but may also serve as an alternative method for treatment monitoring.
Objective: Development of blood-based monitoring techniques for treatment response evaluation and diagnostics in lymphoid neoplasms, including HL and NHL by using extracellular vesicle, protein and cfDNA techniques for biomarker discovery, assay development and prospective validation.

name: Prediction of complications after major gastrointestinal surgery with machine learning and point of care ultrasound: an observational cohort study.
description:
Rationale: Major complications occur frequently in patients after major gastrointestinal surgery. Changes in patients physiology often precedes deterioration and early detection of these changes may improve outcomes. The hemodynamic profile of these patients may hold information for the prediction of deterioration and the optimal choice of resuscitation therapy. In addition, point of care ultrasound can be used to assess fluid responsiveness and fluid intolerance. We hypothesise that a machine learning algorithm alongside point of care ultrasound can predict deterioration and determine whether an intervention with fluids or vasopressors is the optimal choice in each individual setting.
Objective: The primary aim of this study is to develop a machine learning framework to predict major complications after major gastro-intestinal surgery. Secondary aims include combining this framework with point of care ultrasound to determine the best initial resuscitative strategy; and to determine which ultrasound parameters are best predictive of fluid intolerance. Furthermore, if the renin-angiotenis-andosteron-system(RAAS) is more active after liver resection.

name: Blood protein level fluctuations within cognitively normal individuals
description: Assessing reproducibility of results within persons, across study cohorts and between laboratories is required prior to clinical implementation of new biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease. Levels of biomarkers might fluctuate from day to day within persons, caused by for example diet, poor sleep, or other biorhythms or environmental influences. Considering biotemporal fluctuations of a new potential biomarker is needed to adequately calculate sample size of biomarker validation studies that assess the diagnostic potential of biomarker across study cohorts.4 Additionally, in daily clinical practice, just one sample is collected to determine the biomarker levels. If a biomarker level fluctuates within a person over a short period of time, unrelated to disease state, this might result in a less reliable diagnosis using this biomarker. In this project we focus on the within-person reproducibility of blood-based biomarker levels; blood biomarker analysis is a new emerging field for neurodegenerative diseases.

name: stRess systEm dynAmics in Childhood Trauma-related depression (REACT studie)
description:
Rationale: Childhood trauma (CT) is a significant risk factor for several psychiatric disorders including major depressive disorder (MDD). Not only does it increase the risk of onset, but CT-related depression has been shown to critically differ from non-CT-related depression in its earlier emergence, more severe and recurrent symptoms, and worse treatment outcomes. While a wealth of evidence demonstrates altered stress system functionality across the life span following exposure to CT in relation to depression, it is currently unknown which CT-related changes in development of the stress system explain why individuals with CT-related depression have poor outcomes at adult age. Recent work has made clear that dynamic functionality of the stress system is key to an adequate and coordinated stress response, spanning across several modalities including endocrine responses, brain functions/networks, and behavioral responses. We hypothesize that impaired dynamics in the stress response is central in the persistent vulnerability of patients with CT-related depression. Specifically, we hypothesize that mood disorder patients with CT have a reduced proficiency for dynamic adaptation of brain function, which is necessary after stress. This would then result in an impaired response to stress compared to non-CT mood disorder patients and healthy controls, with lower stress-induced (de)activation and connectivity of the salience network, executive control network, and default mode network. We expect that this loss of normal stress-related functional network dynamics also relates to altered physiological and psychological responses to stress in daily life.
Objective: The primary objective is to investigate if the stress-induced dynamics across stress systems are impaired in patients with CT-related depression compared to non-CT-related depression and healthy controls. The secondary objective is to examine how stress system dynamics in the laboratory translate to real-life stress in daily life in these three groups.

the long term. SpA is a complex disease, as evidenced by the involvement of axial and
peripheral articular structures, extra-articular manifestations, presence of co-morbidities such
as osteoporosis and vascular inflammation and the histopathological combination of
inflammation, tissue destruction, and new tissue formation. Mechanistic understanding of
which 'targetable' pathways steer these different disease manifestations is required to
optimize and tailor treatment to all these different facets of the disease.
Bath TNFa and IL-17 are pivotal pathogenie cytokines in SpA. Therapeutic inhibition of each
of these cytokines leads to both significant improvement of clinical symptoms and
suppression of inflammation in SpA. Studies show that anti-TNF decreases inflammatory
activity, and may inhibit progression of bene formation after langer use. Anti-lL-17 treatment,
such as Secukinumab, has a very promising profile to inhibit not only inflammatory activity,
but potentially also bone formation.
In order to investigate therapeutic effects of Secukinumab on enthesitis and related bone
formation, sensitive imaging techniques are required for monitoring early in the course of
treatment. Conventional X-rays and CT-scans still play an important rele for determination

The technique allows sensitive and quantitative imaging of functional tissue changes in the

name: Subjective Cognitive impairment Cohort (SCIENCE): a focus on the earliest changes leading to Alzheimer's disease
description:
Rationale: The largest part of the Alzheimer disease (AD) disease process occurs before onset of clinical symptoms (preclinical AD). Patients presenting with subjective complaints at a memory clinic offer an excellent population to study preclinical AD.
Objective: The general objective of the SCIENCe project is to establish a prospective cohort of patients with subjective complaints, to study the earliest brain changes ultimately leading to cognitive decline and dementia due to AD.

name: Clinical Implementation of Amyloid Neurodegeneration and Tau testing in Primary Care (study)
description:
Rationale: Cognitive complaints have a broad differential diagnosis. The challenge for the general practitioner is to facilitate an optimal diagnostic trajectory, optimal treatment and/or management for each patient. Blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease and neurocognitive disorders in general may aid in this process.
Objective: We aim to take a first step towards identifying the utility of blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease and neurocognitive disorders in general in primary care. Our objectives are:
(a) To investigate if plasma biomarkers are associated with working diagnosis in primary care.
(b) To ascertain if diagnosis and patient management differ between patients with and without plasma evidence of underlying AD.
(c) To explore associations between plasma biomarkers and (1) the nature and severity of cognitive complaints, (2) global cognitive performance and (3) functioning in iADL.
(d) To qualitatively identify scenarios in which plasma biomarkers can improve current care.

name: CANTATE-PC Biobank
description:
Dit biobank-protocol vormt de “CANTATE-PC biobank”, een dataverzameling ten behoeve van het evalueren van verschillende bloedbiomarkers voor diagnostiek van de ziekte van Alzheimer en neurodegeneratie door het neurochemisch lab van het Amsterdam UMC.
De ziekte van Alzheimer (AD) is de meest voorkomende vorm van dementie, in Nederland zijn er ongeveer 200.000 mensen die lijden aan AD. Vroege tekenen van de ziekte van Alzheimer zijn moeilijk te herkennen en aspecifiek, hierdoor is het stellen van een accurate diagnose lastig en kan AD aangezien worden voor een andere (psychiatrische) ziekte. Het stellen van de diagnose AD op een accurate en kosteneffectieve manier is echter van groot belang voor de patiënt, vooral nu de eerste ziekte-modificerende therapieën beschikbaar worden. Bloedbiomarkers zouden hierbij kunnen helpen. Pathologische veranderingen die kenmerkend zijn voor deze ziekte worden normaal gesproken opgespoord middels PET of liquor. Deze methoden zijn echter ofwel invasief ofwel duur waardoor deze methoden geen plek hebben in de 1e lijn.
De Clinical Implementation of Amyloid Neurodegeneration and Tau testing in Primary Care (CANTATE-PC) studie onderzoekt wat het verband is tussen de uitkomst van de bloedbiomarkers voor AD en de klinische werkdiagnose en het beleid van de huisarts. Daarnaast willen wij bepalen wat het verband is tussen de waarde van de uitkomst van deze bloedbiomarkers en de klachten van de patiënt, de resultaten op de cognitieve testen en het functioneren in het dagelijks leven. Materiaal wat overblijft na het voltooien van deze studie zouden wij graag willen gebruiken voor aanvullend onderzoek naar bloedbiomarkers.

name: HEADing in footbalL: Impact on NEural blood biomarkers
description:
Rationale:
With an estimated 265 million active players around the world, football (soccer) is the most popular sport worldwide.1 Football is unique in that it is the only sport that allows intentional use of the head to play the ball.2 There is growing concern about possible harmful effects of heading for the brain due to repetitive head impact, in both amateur and elite football players. Nevertheless, to date there is limited evidence or either acute or cumulative effects of heading on the brain of active football players. Biomarkers of neural damage have proven diagnostic value for brain damage caused by traumatic brain injury 3 4 and neurodegenerative disease 4, and therefore represent a promising method to investigate the impact of heading exposure on brain integrity. Existing studies lack sufficient sample sizes to detect small effects and have often not assessed a realistic exposure to ball heading in a real-world setting. Moreover, the biomedical field has recently brought forward novel biomarkers of neural damage. Taken together, the field is in need of a study with substantial sample size to investigate the impact of naturalistic heading exposure on the brain using biomarkers of neural damage.
Objective:
To determine the potential impact of ball heading in football on brain integrity as assessed by blood biomarkers for neural damage in a real-world setting.

name: Youth of Utrecht
description:
The YOUth cohort is funded through a NWO Gravitation grant to the Consortium Individual Development. YOUth is a longitudinal cohort study with repeated measurements that focuses on neurocognitive development (i.e. brain and cognitive development) involved in two core characteristics of behavioural development: social competence and behavioural control. The YOUth cohort includes participants either during pregnancy, or around 9 years of age. The first group, YOUth Baby & Child, aims to include 3000 pregnant women at 20 weeks of pregnancy, and their partners through hospitals and midwifery practices. The second group, YOUth Child & Teenager, aims to include 3000 children aged 8, 9 or 10 and their parents through primary schools. So, in total 6000 children and their mothers and fathers will be repeatedly tested using a test battery including EEG/ERP (in infants and young children), structural and functional MRI (in school-age children), and eye-tracking, behavioural, and computer tasks, suited to study the effect of biological, child-related and environmental characteristics on the developing brain, and subsequently on the developing behaviour.

YOUth applies a flexible longitudinal design for the cohorts. This means that children will be measured at broader age ranges (3-year age ranges) at each wave. The main benefit of the flexible age design is that it will provide more detailed information on the neurodevelopmental curves over time.

name: Second Manifestations of Arterial Disease-Magnetic Resonance study
description: The Second Manifestations of ARTerial disease-Magnetic Resonance (SMART-MR) study is a prospective cohort study at the University Medical Center Utrecht, the Netherlands, with the aim to investigate risk factors and consequences of brain changes on MRI in patients with symptomatic atherosclerotic disease. Baseline examinations took place from 2001 through 2005, when 1309 middle-aged and older adult persons (58 +/- 10 years, 80% male) newly referred to the UMC Utrecht for treatment of symptomatic atherosclerotic disease (coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm) and without MRI contraindications were enrolled. On a one day visit to our medical center the participants received a 1.5T brain MRI, neuropsychological tests, a physical examination, ankle-brachial index assessment, ultrasonography of the carotid arteries, blood and urine sampling, and questionnaires to assess risk factors, medical history, and daily functioning. Between January 2006 and May 2009, after an average of 4 years of follow-up, 754 patients had follow-up measurements, and measurements were then added as part of the Second Manifestations of ARTerial disease-Memory, depression and aging (SMART-Medea) study, including depression assessment, psychosocial risk factor questionnaires, saliva sampling for stress hormones, and a 3-dimensional T1-weighted MR image to assess hippocampal volumes. The SMART-Medea study has the objective to investigate psychosocial vulnerability and stress factors and vascular risk factors of brain changes on MRI, course of depressive symptoms, and cognitive decline. Between November 2013 and October 2017, after an average of 12 years of follow-up since baseline, 329 surviving participants of the SMART-MR and SMART-Medea cohort had follow-up measurements, including neuropsychological and depression assessment, and a 1.5T brain MRI scan. In addition, 213 participants had an additional 7T brain MRI.

name: CAPACITY
description: CAPACITY is a registry of patients with COVID-19 across Europe and has been established to answer questions on the role of cardiovascular disease in this pandemic. It is an extension of the Case Record Form (CRF) that was released by the ISARIC (International Severe Acute Respiratory and Emerging Infection Consortium) and WHO (World Health Organisation) in response to the emerging outbreak of COVID-19. The aim of CAPACITY is to collect data regarding the cardiovascular history, diagnostic information and occurrence of cardiovascular complications in COVID-19 patients. By collecting this information in a standardized manner, CAPACITY can aid in providing more insight in (1) the incidence of cardiovascular complications in patients with COVID-19, and (2) the vulnerability and clinical course of COVID-19 in patients with an underlying cardiovascular disease. The CAPACITY study is an initiative of the DCVA (Dutch CardioVascular Alliance) involving numerous biobanks and hospitals across the Netherlands. For more information see https://capacity-covid.eu or contact Info@capacity-covid.eu

name: CAIRO 4
description:
The role of surgery of the primary tumour with few or absent symptoms in patients with synchronous unresectable metastases of colorectal cancer: a multicenter randomized phase III study. Study design: Patients with synchronous metastatic colorectal cancer with few or absent symptoms of their primary tumour are randomized 1:1 between systemic
treatment without resection of the primary tumour and resection of the primary tumour followed by systemic treatment. 
Primary objective: To determine the clinical benefit in terms of overall survival of resection of the primary tumour in synchronous unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer. Inclusion criteria: Resectable primary tumour in situ, unresectable distant metastases, no indication for neo-adjuvant (chemo)radiation. Data collection: Questionnaires. Sample collection: Tissue, plasma, serum.

name: Colopec II
description: Second and third look laparoscopy in pT4 colon cancer patients for early detection of peritoneal metastases: a randomized multicentre trial. Primary objective: To determine the added value of a third look diagnostic laparoscopy (DLS) after a negative second look DLS in pT4N0-2M0 colon cancer patients to detect peritoneal metastases (PM) at a subclinical stage. Inclusion criteria: Curative intent resection (R0/R1) of pT4a,bN0-2M0 colon cancer, proximal rectal  cancer, or small bowel cancer, with or without adjuvant systemic therapy. Data collection: CT scans, questionnaires. Sample collection: Tissue, plasma, ctDNA. Experimental data: Genomics

name: FORCE trial
description: Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation to improve functional Outcome and quality of life after surgery for Rectal Cancer: a randomized controlled trial. Primary objective: To evaluate the effect of Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation compared to standard treatment on fecal incontinence in patients after low anterior resection, by measuring the Wexner-score. Inclusion criteria: Patients who underwent low anterior resection for rectal carcinoma. Data collection: Questionnaires

name: MOCCAS
description: Molecular stool testing for Colorectal CAncer Surveillance (MOCCAS) study. Primary objective: To determine the performance characteristics of two established non-invasive tests, the multitarget stool DNA test Cologuard® and the faecal immunochemical test (FIT) in the detection of colorectal cancer (CRC) as an alternative for colonoscopy surveillance. Inclusion criteria: Subjects in the age group 50-75 years, with history of polypectomy or CRC, as well as subjects under surveillance for familial colorectal cancer (FCC). Data collection: Questionnaires. Sample collection: Feaces. Experimental data: Genomics, methylation, quantification of haemoglobin.

name: BIOPEX-2
description: Perineal wound closure using gluteal turnover flap or primary closure after abdominoperineal resection for rectal cancer: a randomised controlled multicenter trial. Study design: This is a multicentre study in which patients undergoing an abdominoperineal resection (APR) are randomised between standard care using primary closure of the perineum and the experimental arm with assisted closure using a gluteal turnover (GT) flap. Primary objective: To determine the additional value of a minimally invasive gluteal turnover flap for perineal wound healing after APR for rectal cancer in comparison to primary closure. Inclusion criteria: Resection of primary or recurrent rectal carcinoma by abdominoperineal resection. Data collection: CT scans, questionnaires.

name: IMARI
description: Multi-Interventional program for prevention and early Management of Anastomotic leakage after total mesorectal excision in Rectal cancer patIents, the IMARI-trial. This is a multicenter prospective clinical effectiveness trial. Primary objective: To increase the one year anastomotic integrity rate in patients undergoing total mesorectal excision (TME) for rectal cancer by the routine and quality controlled implementation of a multi-interventional program. Inclusion criteria: Patients with a diagnosis of primary rectal cancer with the lower border below the level of the sigmoid take-off on MRI, or regrowth in a watch and wait protocol, or undergoing completion/salvage surgery after local excision.  Data collection: CT scans, questionnaires. Sample collection: Tissue, serum, swab precacral cavity, swab anastomotic site, feaces. Experimental data: Genomics, microbiotica profilling, metatranscriptomics.

name: CAMINO
description: Clinical added value of MRI over CT in patients scheduled for local colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) therapy: a prospective, multicenter incremental diagnostic accuracy study. Primary objective: To evaluate the clinical impact (i.e. finding additional clinically significant (CS)-CRLM) of liver-MRI in addition to CT chest/abdomen in patients scheduled for curative therapy for primary or recurrent CRLM. Inclusion criteria: All patients with primary or recurrent CRLM who are considered candidates for curative surgery, (percutaneous or open) ablation only or combination of curative surgery and per-operative ablation based on CT chest/abdomen. Data collection: MRI scans, CT scans (Clinical data currently not available for third parties).

description:
PROCORE is a prospective population-based study with the focus on chemotherapy
induced peripheral neuropathy and the impact on colorectal cancer patients lives. Primary objective: To gain insight into the incidence and severity of chemotherapy induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) symptoms in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. Inclusion criteria: CRC patients stage I-IV. Data collection: Questionnaires. Sample collection: Whole Blood, Plasma, DNA,  Buffy Coat. name: CAIRO 5
description: Treatment strategies in colorectal cancer patients with initially unresectable liver-only metastases CAIRO5: a randomized phase 3 study of the Dutch Colorectal Cancer Group (DCCG). Primary objective: To determine the median progression-free survival (PFS) upon induction systemic treatment in colorectal cancer patients with initially unresectable liver-only metastases, stratified by RAS and BRAF tumor mutation status and primary tumor location. Inclusion criteria: Unresectable metastases confined to the liver, RAS and BRAF mutation status known. Data collection: BRAF status, RAS status. Sample collection: Tissue, DNA, microRNA, plasma. Experimental data: Genomics , metabolomics , proteomics, transcriptomics. Molecular analysis: CNV, WGS, WES.

name: CAIRO 6
description: Perioperative systemic therapy and cytoreductive surgery with HIPEC versus upfront cytoreductive surgery with HIPEC alone for resectable colorectal peritoneal metastases: a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, phase II-III, randomised superiority study. Primary objective: To compare the oncological efficacy of perioperative systemic therapy and cytoreductive surgery with Hypertherme Intraperitoneale Chemotherapie (HIPEC) (experimental arm) versus upfront cytoreductive surgery with HIPEC alone (control arm) for isolated resectable colorectal peritoneal metastases (PM). Inclusion criteria: No previous HIPEC, pathologically proven peritoneal metastasis (PCI <20), no systemic metastases, no systemic chemotherapy <6 months. Data collection: CT scans, questionnaires. Sample collection: Tissue, plasma, ctDNA. Experimental data: Genomics. Molecular analysis: WES, CNV.

name: FIT
description: Multicentre randomized controlled trial comparing ferric(III)carboxymaltose infusion with oral iron supplementation in the treatment of preoperative anemia in colorectal cancer patients. Primary objective: To investigate which route of iron supplementation is superior in the treatment of iron deficiency anemia in patients with colorectal carcinoma. Inclusion criteria: Patients with M0- stage colorectal carcinoma and concomitant iron deficiency anemia (Hb < 8 mmol/l (13 g/dl) for men and TSAT < 20 %) who will undergo a laparoscopic/open segmental colonic resection or (low) anterior resection. Data collection: Case record forms, questionnaires

name: PUMP trial
description: Adjuvant hepatic arterial infusion pump chemotherapy after resection of colorectal liver metastases in patients with a low clinical risk score: a phase III randomized controlled open label, multicenter trial. Primary objective: To compare the progression-free survival (PFS) of surgery with adjuvant hepatic arterial infusion pump (HAIP) chemotherapy to surgery alone in patients with resectable colorectal liver metastases with a low clinical risk score (CRS 0-2). Inclusion criteria:: Patients with resectable colorectal liver metastases (CLM) without extrahepatic disease (EHD). Data collection: CT scans, questionnaires. Sample collection: Tissue, Plasma, Serum, ctDNA. Experimental data: Genomics, Pharmacokinetics.

name: Collison
description: Colorectal liver metastases: surgery versus thermal ablation: a phase III single-blind prospective randomized controlled trial. Primary objective: To prove non-inferiority of thermal ablation compared to hepatic resection in patients with at least one resectable and ablatable colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) and no extrahepatic disease. Inclusion criteria: Resectable and ablatable CRLM, (≤3cm) (= target lesion),  maximum of 10 CRLM, additional resections for unablatable CRLM and/or ablations for unresectable CRLM are allowed. Data collection: Questionnaires

name: Collision-XL trial
description: Unresectable colorectal liver metastases: stereotactic body radiotherapy versus microwave ablation: a phase II prospective randomized controlled trial for colorectal liver metastases 3-5 cm. Primary objective: To compare efficacy of microwave ablation (MWA) to the efficacy of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) with regards to the primary endpoint (local tumour progression free survival at 1 year in patients with unresectable colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) (3 – 5 cm). Inclusion criteria: Patients with 1-3 unresectable CRLM size 3-5 cm eligible for both MWA and SBRT (target lesions), additional CRLM are allowed if considered either resectable or ablatable and <3cm. Data collection: Questionnaires

name: ENCORE
description:
Energy for life in colorectal cancer survivors: How do physical activity and dietary factors affect their quality of life?
Primairy objective: To investigate the influence of physical activity and dietary factors on the quality of life of colorectal cancer survivors after treatment.
Study design: In a cohort of colorectal cancer survivors, changes in physical activity and dietary factors in relation to changes in quality of life after treatment will be studied prospectively. In addition, the proposed research questions will be studied cross-sectionally in individuals from two to ten years after treatment of colorectal cancer. Inclusion criteria: Established diagnosis of stage I, II or III CRC, including recurrent CRC (Prospective study), history of stage I, II or III CRC, including recurrent CRC, for which the cases concerned received treatment in the preceding 2 to 10 years (Cross-sectional study). Data collection: MRI scans, CT scans and questionnaires. Sample collection: From 80 patients per year  (prospective) + 216 patients (cross-sectional) is expected to collect; Tissue, plasma, serum and DNA. Experimental data: Genomics, proteomics, metabolics.

name: MEDOCC-CrEATE
description: Circulating tumor DNA based adjuvant chemotherapy in stage II colon cancer patients: the MEDOCC-CrEATE trial. A phase III randomized controlled trial according to Trials within Cohorts design.  Primary objective: To investigates how many patients with detectable ctDNA accept adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) and whether ACT reduces recurrence rate. Inclusion criteria: Histological confirmed stage II colorectal cancer, fit enough to receive treatment with combination chemotherapy (fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin) according to the treating physician. Data collection: Questionnaires.  Sample collection: Tissue, plasma, ctDNA. Experimental data: Genomics

name: MEDOCC
description: A prospective observational trial to evaluate the prognostic value of ctDNA after resection of the primary tumor in stage II colorectal cancer patients. Primary objective: To determine the association between presence of ctDNA after surgery and recurrence and survival of disease in stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. Secondairy objective: To determine if mutational status of detected ctDNA is associated with tumor characteristics and clinical outcome. Inclusion criteria: Histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the colon or proximal rectum without indication for neoadjuvant treatment. Suspected stage II or III CRC before surgery of the primary. Data collection: Questionnaires.  Sample collection: Plasma, ctDNA, celpellet. Experimental data: Genomics

name: OPTIC
description: OPTIC (Organoids to Predict Treatment response In mCRC) is an multicenter observational cohort study. Primary objective: To validate the concept that ex vivo organoid response correlates to in vivo response to standard first-line, second-line or third-line treatment in mCRC patients on a metastasis level. Study design: This early phase biomarker development study is the first step in the evaluation of tumor organoids as a screening tool to predict treatment response to standard of care drugs in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Whole genome sequencing can additionally be performed to relate genetic characteristics to organoid drug screening results and patient response to treatment. lf the study results are promising we will use the data to expand the use of the technology for positive selection/prediction of treatment. Inclusion criteria: Patients with mCRC and a liver metastasis who will receive 1st, 2nd or 3rd line of chemotherapy and/or targeted agents. Data collection: Clinical response information (including CT scan RECIST values) and organoid drug response data (e.g. IC50) and WGS data. Sample collection: Tissue, organoids, serum, plasma, cell pellets, DNA, RNA. Experimental data: Genomics, Transcriptomics. Molecular analysis: RNA sequencing

name: CONNECTION
description: Improving clinical management of colon cancer through CONNECTION, a nationwide Colon Cancer Registry and Stratification effort (CONNECTION II Trial). A prospective, single arm, multicenter intervention study. Primairy objective: To evaluate the pathological tumor response to neoadjuvant systemic chemotherapy per consensus molecular subtype (CMS) in patients with microsatellite stable (MSS) high risk stage II and stage III colon cancer. Inclusion criteria: MSS based on pre-treatment biopsy by immunohistochemistry, adequate bone marrow, liver and renal function, fit to undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy with CAPOX and subsequent surgery judged by the primary treating physician. Data collection: CT scans, MMR status, CMS data. Sample collection: Tissue, plasma.

name: NTRK
description: Prevalence of NTRK fusions in metastatic colorectal cancer patients. Primary objective: To estimate the prevalence of an Neurotrophic Tyrosine Receptor Kinase (NTRK) gene fusion in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) patients with an microsatellite instable (MSI) tumor or a right sided colon cancer (CC) and determine the survival using the PLCRC infrastructure. Inclusion criteria: mCRC patients with a MSI tumor or right sided mCC, included in PLCRC with informed consensus for use of tissue. Data collection: Clinical data, NTRK fusion data. description: The Heart Tissue Bank, founded in June 2020, is a non-profit biobank including biomaterial (including cardiac tissue and blood samples) and clinical data of individuals with and without previously known cardiac disease(s). All individuals aged ≥ 18 years living in the Netherlands are eligible for inclusion as potential future donor. All stored samples and data can be requested for downstream analysis. More details are provided at www.hartenbank.nl .

name: Hartwig Medical Foundation
description:
Unique genomics dataset for research into better cancer treatment
Hartwig Medical Foundation established the first national genomic database for cancer research in 2015. The Foundation is also responsible for the management of this database. The first data was made available to researchers in 2017.
The database combines genetic and clinical data (including treatment outcomes) of patients in the Netherlands with metastatic cancer. The database continues to grow with the addition of data from about 100 new patients every month. The genetic data are generated using Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), making this unique database the most comprehensive source of data in the world for research into cancer and better treatments of this disease.
Purpose of the database: to find new biomarkers
The genomic database is helping researchers to improve their understanding of cancer. This requires large quantities of data in order to recognize patterns in the disease. This is also how biomarkers are discovered, by identifying the links between genetic mutations, tumor characteristics, drugs and treatment outcome. Hartwig Medical Foundation systematically generates genetic data and collects clinical data and makes these data available to physicians, practitioners and researchers, so that new biomarkers can be discovered faster and existing biomarkers can be improved. In addition to the discovery of new biomarkers, the information can also be used to improve the effectiveness of existing treatments.

name: GENAYA Hartwig Medical Foundation
description:
Patients who were aged between 18 and 39 years when the cancer first manifested, with:

Metastatic disease (excluding testicular cancer prior to treatment by primary care provider).
Recurrent metastatic testicular cancer, recurrent Hodgkin’s or Non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (after an initial treatment).
Primary tumors with predicted 5-year survival rate <60%, being:
All brain tumors (includes a small proportion with a better prognosis, but this cannot be determined in advance).
Ewing sarcomas, embryonic rhabdomyosarcomas, nerve sheet tumors and other sarcomas with a poor prognosis (if necessary, in consultation with Hartwig).
Triple-negative mammary carcinomas without a pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
Rare tumors: esophageal, gastric, hepatic, bile duct, pancreatic, pulmonary, respiratory and urinary tract tumors, or other rare tumors with a poor prognosis (if necessary, in consultation with Hartwig).
After registration

A WGS test is performed and the results are immediately used for the diagnosis and treatment plan.
The patient’s genetic data, treatment history and outcomes are stored in the Hartwig Medical Database. The attending physician first asks for the patient’s consent to include the data in the database.

name: Living and Working in Coronavirus Times Project and Survey
description: WageIndicator Foundation is surveying / interviewing people in 140 countries to explore the COVID-19 effect on jobs, workload, working from home, job losses, and working conditions. Control variables relate to occupation, firm size, employment contract, household composition, life satisfaction, and Corona-cases in respondent’s networks at home and at the workplace. The surveys are in the national language(s). Given that a random sampled global survey is beyond budget and impossible in a brief time frame, the survey is a volunteer web-survey with snowball recruiting through many frequently visited websites with high quality search engine optimization and through social media. The results are shown in maps and graphs, updated on a daily basis. Researchers from CLARIN ERIC, SSHOC Project and the University of Amsterdam are cooperating in the project. In addition, WageIndicator collects for a few countries the COVID-19 response of companies, and has developed a data collection regarding country-level measures related to work and employment.The surveys are accessible here (select a country and a language in case of multilingual countries):https://wageindicator.org/salary/living-and-working-in-times-of-the-coronavirusThe codebook is available here:https://wageindicator.org/documents/publicationslist/publications-2020/corona-survey-codebook_20200330.pdfThe data of the survey is available for non-commercial use at IZA DATA ARCHIVE in Bonn, and is every weekday updated at noon:https://datasets.iza.org/dataset/1388/living-and-working-in-coronavirus-times-surveyThe maps are available here:https://iltuosalario.it/carriera/vivere-e-lavorare-ai-tempi-del-coronavirus/coronavirus-mappeThe country-level overview of measures is available here:https://paycheck.pk/career-tips/living-and-working-in-times-of-the-coronavirus/covid-19-labour-market-reforms

name: COVID-19 in rheumatic patients: a prospective cohort study
description: The influence of the presence of an inflammatory rheumatic disease and its treatment on the severity of and immune response to (viral) infections is not clear. The emergence and pandemic of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) provides the opportunity to assess these influences on COVID-19 incidence, its clinical severity, and the antibody response, compared to a control population. This is a prospective observational cohort study with a follow-up of 6 months. The study population will consist of participants with a systemic autoimmune disease. Each patient will be asked to provide a healthy control without a systemic autoimmune disease from his/her social group or household to ensure that there is a comparable chance of exposure to SARS-CoV-2 in the control group. All participants will be at least 18 years old. In total, we expect to include 8000 subjects. Our primary study parameter is the percentage of subjects with a positive IgM or IgG response admitted to the hospital. Other parameters include the geometric mean antibody titre over time in participants and the percentage of IgM/IgG positive participants admitted to the ICU, or death. Another study parameter will be the geometric mean and incidence of different antibody profiles (IgM/G/A, IgG1/3) and repertoire (anti-SP, anti-NP), and the geometric mean antibody avidity in participants. In addition, the percentage of patients that adjusted their DMARD treatment will be compared between IgM/IgG positive and negative patients. The effect of these adjustments on the mean rheumatic disease activity will also be investigated.

name: NBCS (Nijmegen Blaaskankerstudie)
description: The Dutch patients were recruited for the Nijmegen BladderCancer Study (NBCS: http://dceg.cancer.gov/icbc/membership.html). The NBCS identified patients through thepopulation-based regional cancer registry held by the ComprehensiveCancer Centre East, Nijmegen, that serves a region of1.3 million inhabitants in the eastern part of the Netherlands(www.ikcnet.nl). Patients diagnosed between 1995 and 2006under the age of 75 years were selected and their vital statusand current addresses updated through the hospital informationsystems of the seven community hospitals and one universityhospital (Radboud University Nijmegen MedicalCentre, RUNMC) that are covered by the cancer registry.All patients still alive on 1 August 2007 were invited to thestudy by the Comprehensive Cancer Center on behalf of thepatients’ treating physicians. A second group of patients, diagnosedbetween 2007 and 2008, was invited in 2009. In case of consent, patients were sent a lifestyle questionnaire to fill outand blood samples were collected by Thrombosis Servicecenters which hold offices in all the communities in theregion. In total, 1940 patients were invited to participate. Ofall the invitees, 1275 gave informed consent (66%): 1185filled out the questionnaire (61%) and 1219 (63%) provideda blood sample. The number of participating patients wasincreased with a non-overlapping series of 439 bladdercancer patients who were recruited previously for a study ongene–environment interactions in three hospitals (RUNMC,Canisius Wilhelmina Hospital, Nijmegen, and StreekziekenhuisMidden-Twente, Hengelo, the Netherlands). Ultimately,completed questionnaires and blood samples were availablefor 1429 and 1691 patients, respectively. All the patientsselected for the analyses (n ¼ 1631) were of self-reportedEuropean descent. The median age at diagnosis was 62(range 25–93) years. Eighty-two percent of the participantswere males. Data on tumor stage and grade were obtainedthrough the cancer registry.

name: Prospectieve landelijke Von Hippel Lindau cohort
description: De ziekte van von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) is een zeldzaam erfelijk tumor syndroom dat gekenmerkt wordt door de ontwikkeling van multipele benigne en maligne tumoren. Patiënten met de ziekte VHL dienen levenslangs jaarlijkse follow-up te ondergaan. De Prospectieve Landelijke VHL cohort (PLVHLCc) is ontwikkeld om meer inzicht te krijgen in het natuurlijk ziekteverloop en het effect op de verschillende behandelingen ter verbetering van de zorg voor VHL-patiënten.

name: D-DOTT: Versnelde rTMS voor de behandeling van depressie
description: In een multi-center RCT (D-DOTT) onderzoeken wij de mate van remissie van depressie en de kosteneffectiviteit bij het toepassen van het SNT protocol in vergelijking met standaard 10Hz rTMS voor het behandelen van patiënten met behandelingsresistente depressie. In aanvulling op het D-DOTT onderzoek richten wij een deelbiobank op dat gevuld zal worden met lichaamsmateriaal van patiënten met een unipolaire depressie die meedoen aan D-DOTT.

name: Sunrise deelbiobank
description: Met deze deelbiobank willen we wetenschappelijk onderzoek doen naar de relatie tussen herseninfarcten en boezemfibrilleren om de diagnostiek, behandeling en prognose van patiënten in de toekomst te verbeteren.

name: Biobank Hereditary Colorectal Cancer
description: Affected and unaffected patients at increased risk of hereditary colorectal cancer and/or polyposis, or with a proven germline mutation causing colorectal cancer and/or polyposis are included. Both clinical data (demographic data, details on medical and family histo¬ry, information on surveillance, endoscopy and surgery, results of microsatellite instability and molecular genetic tests) and biomaterial (DNA, plasma, serum and tissue) are collected in a standardized manner.

name: Diabetes
description: Het Parelsnoerinitiatief heeft als doel om binnen de academische centra een infrastructuur te realiseren voor het verzamelen van klinische data en opzetten van biobanken op interuniversitair niveau. Het UMC St Radboud neemt als universitair medisch centrum deel aan het Parelsnoerinitiatief. Het ziektebeeld diabetes is binnen het UMC St Radboud één van de parels waarvoor het implementatie traject gestart wordt. Implementatie houdt in het proces van inclusie van een patiënt in het parelsnoercohort, vastleggen van klinische gegevens, afname en opslag van biomateriaal en publicatie van deze gegevens aan het centrale Parelsnoer Initiatief.

name: Clinical features of SARS-CoV-2
description: There is a great need for detailed clinical data to help improve diagnostic and therapeutic management and identify predictors for poor outcome. Our study aims to describe clinical, laboratory and radiological characteristics and to identify prognostic biomarkers for poor outcome of COVID-19 cases that are hospitalized in five hospitals in the south of The Netherlands. This will help to gain scientific knowledge of the emerging disease and improve clinical algorithms and prognostic factors for outcome of COVID-19. At this moment, we have a large database including detailed clinical information and plasma/serum samples of multiple timepoints for more than 1100 PCR-confirmed COVID-19 patients from 6 hospitals in The Netherlands. This combined database provides the opportunity to identify prognostic factors for poor outcome of COVID-19 based on clinical characteristics as well as biological factors. The primary aims of this database are 1) to describe the clinical course of COVID-19 in hospitalised patients and to identify clinical risk factors for severe disease, 2) to identify and validate new prognostic biomarkers for poor outcome of COVID-19, and 3) to study a biological basis for the diversity in clinical presentation of COVID-19. In addition, this database provides the opportunity to study subgroups or subquestions related to COVID-19.

description: The aim of the Stibion biobank foundation is to enable and support research on and development of methods for health monitoring and early detection of disease. The Stibion biobank is building a collection of longitudinal bio-fluid sample series from the average population including all risk groups and chronic health problems, including obesity (>1000), diabetes (332), COPD (84), Crohns (43), high cholesterol (>400), high blood pressure (>400), kidney and liver dysfunction (~50). Currently, 5200 unique donors are participating of which the longest ones already for over 5 years. 3-monthly urine and yearly blood samples are collected in combination with data on health history, medication use and current health generated by donor questionnaires, information from GP records and national registries (NKR/PALGA). A key feature of the Stibion collection is the presence of sample series containing the pre-diagnosis stage of serious diseases like cancer (155) and cardiovascular events (164) that enable biomarker discovery for early disease detection.

name: AcuteLines
description: Research in acute care faces many challenges, including enrollment challenges, legal limitations in data sharing, limited funding, and lack of singular ownership of the domain of acute care. To overcome some of these challenges, the Center of Acute Care of the University Medical Center Groningen in the Netherlands, has established a de novo data-, image- and biobank named "Acutelines". Acutelines is initiated to improve recognition and treatment of acute diseases and obtain insight in the consequences of acute diseases, including factors predicting its outcome. Thereby, Acutelines contributes to development of personalized treatment and improves prediction of patient outcomes after an acute admission.

name: Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands (CeDNN)
description: Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands, CeDNN, is collecting (bio)materials from celiac disease patients, relatives, partners and IBS patients. The aim is to get a better understanding of how CeD risk genes, the microbiome and environmental factors contribute to disease aetiology. To achieve this, a holistic approach will be applied in which we will study the behaviour of immune cells and the microbiome in CeD patients and compare that to non-patients using “omics” technology (i.e. the full repertoire of all transcripts, cytokine profiles, proteins, metabolites etc.) in the background of the genetic profile of each individual. To generate this information we will profile different immune cells from patients and controls. These datasets will be analysed and integrated using bioinformatics approaches to develop insights into the mechanisms underlying celiac disease. The hope is that the newly gained knowledge will contribute to disease prevention in patients with increased risk for developing celiac disease and to the discovery of novel treatment targets in patients that have developed disease already.

name: DiaLines
description: DiaLines is a biobank in with material and medical data are collected form patients with chronic kidney disease stage 5 treated with hemodialysis. Hemodialysis is, together with kidney transplantation the only life-saving treatment in patients with den-stage renal disease. Unfortunately, many patients on hemodialysis suffer from complaints or conditions like chronic fatigue, loss of muscle strength, loss of muscle mass, malnutrition and a high incidence of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. In DiaLines we study the factors that are associated with these complaints and conditions with the goal of improving the long-term outcomes and quality of life of hemodialysis patients. Such improvements in overal functioning will also result in higher proportion of patients being eligible for kidney transplantation.

name: DIALINES Dialysis procedure
description: DiaLines is a biobank in with material and medical data are collected form patients with chronic kidney disease stage 5 treated with hemodialysis. Hemodialysis is, together with kidney transplantation the only life-saving treatment in patients with den-stage renal disease. Unfortunately, many patients on hemodialysis suffer from complaints or conditions like chronic fatigue, loss of muscle strength, loss of muscle mass, malnutrition and a high incidence of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. In DiaLines we study the factors that are associated with these complaints and conditions with the goal of improving the long-term outcomes and quality of life of hemodialysis patients. Such improvements in overal functioning will also result in higher proportion of patients being eligible for kidney transplantation.

name: DonorLines
description: DonorLines is a nationwide prospective biobank and cohort study of deceased organ donors in the Netherlands. The study includes all deceased organ donors, including donors whose organs are ultimately not transplanted. DonorLines integrates prospectively collected clinical data with blood, urine and tissue biospecimens to support research on donor pathophysiology, donor management, organ quality and transplant outcomes. Through integration with TransplantLines, donor data can be linked to recipient outcomes, enabling comprehensive donor-recipient research.

name: Groningen Leeuwarden Axiale Spondyloartritis cohort (IMMUNOLINES - GLAS)
description:
The Groningen Leeuwarden Axial Spondyloarthritis (GLAS) cohort is an ongoing prospective longitudinal observational cohort study. This cohort is embedded in daily clinical practice and >900 patients are included in the northern part of the Netherlands. 
Since November 2004, consecutive AS outpatients who started TNF-α blocking therapy because of active disease at the UMCG and the MCL were included in this cohort. In 2009, this inclusion was extended to all consecutive axial SpA outpatients, irrespective of treatment regimen. Patients treated with TNF-α blocking therapy are evaluated at baseline, after 3 and 6 months, and then every 6 to 12 months. Patients without anti-TNF-α treatment are evaluated every year. The standardized protocol consists of patient characteristics, medication use, questionnaires, physical examination, and biobanking (serum, plasma, DNA samples). Every 2-4 years, radiology of the pelvis and cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine as well as BMD measurements of the lumbar spine and hip are performed. 
Overall, our objective is to carefully monitor axial SpA and to gain more knowledge about the long-term course of the disease when patients are treated according to national (NVR) and international (ASAS, EULAR) guidelines.

name: Groningen Longitudinal Glaucoma Study (GLGS)
description: A prospective, observational cohort study that comprises of both glaucoma patients and glaucoma suspects, started in 2000 at the UMCG. All subjects were followed for at least 4 years. Patients were classified as having either glaucoma (>450) or suspect glaucoma (>400),  a group of healthy subjects was recruited outside the hospital (>200). Later, since 2015, new patients were included with their current and past systemic medications.

name: Lifelines Cohort Study (Lifelines Biobank)
description:
Lifelines is a longitudinal multigenerational population cohort and biobank founded in 2006. Lifelines includes over 167,000 participants, covering 10% of the population in the three northern provinces of the Netherlands. 
We follow our participants, who have all ages and are often members of the same families. The aim of Lifelines is to be a resource for the national and international scientific community searching for insights into healthy ageing. 
To facilitare research we make our collected biosamples (e.g. blood and urine) and data (e.g. questionnaires, diagnostic instruments, and physical measurements) available for use on the condition of a valid project proposal, a signed DMTA, and a fee to cover our sample- and datamanagement services and secure data access infrastructure.

name: Lifelines NEXT (LLNEXT)
description:
Lifelines NEXT (LLNEXT) is a birth cohort designed to study the effects of intrinsic and extrinsic determinants on health and disease as epidemiological research has shown there is a strong relationship between pre-conceptional, prenatal, birth and early-life factors and lifelong health. It is embedded within the Lifelines cohort study, a prospective three-generation population-based cohort study recording the health and health-related aspects of 167,729 individuals living in Northern Netherlands. The nesting of the study within Lifelines enables us to include pre-conceptional transgenerational data which can be used to identify other factors that influence health in other families in a four-generation design.
LLNEXT included 1.450 pregnant women and their children residing in the northern provinces of The Netherlands. The women are followed from the third month of their pregnancy. As of 2018, partners were also invited to enroll in LLNEXT.
Standardized protocols and guidelines are available upon request.

name: Lifelines DEEP (LL_DEEP)
description:
The LifeLines-DEEP cohort is a sub-cohort of the LifeLines population-based prospective cohort (167,729 participants) that employs a broad range of investigative procedures to assess the biomedical, socio-demographic, behavioral, physical and psychological factors that contribute to health and disease in the general Dutch population (Scholtens 2015). A subset of approximately 1,500 participants aged 18 years and older took part in LifeLines-DEEP. 

For these participants, additional biological materials were collected. We collected additional blood (n = 1387), exhaled air (n = 1425) and faecal samples (n = 1248), and elicited responses to gastrointestinal health questionnaires (n = 1176) for analysis of the genome, epigenome, transcriptome, microbiome, metabolome and other biological levels. Lifelines DEEP can be used to examine the determinants of gastrointestinal health by using collected questionnaire data on food intake and quality of life assessments and by using detailed data on genetic, genomic and metabolic variation for a wide range of phenotypic outcomes. This multi-level data also allows for translational research on disease biomarkers, disease mechanisms and prevention.

Also available on the EGA website = https://metadata.ega-archive.org/studies/EGAS00001001704 
And on the Lifelines wiki = https://wiki-lifelines.web.rug.nl/doku.php?id=deep

name: Oncology Life Study (OncoLifeS)
description:
We have established a hospital-based data-biobank, entitled OncoLifeS (Oncological Life Study: Living well as a cancer survivor) to link routinely collected clinical data with preserved biological specimens and quality of life assessments. The OncoLifeS data-biobank has been designed to facilitate cancer research by providing clear phenotypic and genotypic data in a clinical context.

Observational study involves collecting routine clinical data about carefully selected patient groups, and this can be combined with genetics and omics data from biological specimens. Indeed, understanding cancer heterogeneity, its temporal evolution over time, and the outcomes of guided treatment depend on accurate data about patient characteristics and their clinical management. Linking these routine clinical data to preserved biological specimens can then enable reproducible research capable of discovering biomarkers of cancer and/or treatment response, evaluating personalized treatment approaches, and increasing patient awareness. Including quality of life assessments may provide relevant information on how cancer and its treatment affects the subjective well-being of patients.

description:
We have established a hospital-based data-biobank, entitled OncoLifeS (Oncological Life Study: Living well as a cancer survivor) to link routinely collected clinical data with preserved biological specimens and quality of life assessments. The OncoLifeS data-biobank has been designed to facilitate cancer research by providing clear phenotypic and genotypic data in a clinical context.

Observational study involves collecting routine clinical data about carefully selected patient groups, and this can be combined with genetics and omics data from biological specimens. Indeed, understanding cancer heterogeneity, its temporal evolution over time, and the outcomes of guided treatment depend on accurate data about patient characteristics and their clinical management. Linking these routine clinical data to preserved biological specimens can then enable reproducible research capable of discovering biomarkers of cancer and/or treatment response, evaluating personalized treatment approaches, and increasing patient awareness. Including quality of life assessments may provide relevant information on how cancer and its treatment affects the subjective well-being of patients.

description:
National biobank to facilitate clinically relevant multi-omics research in patients with IBD. 

Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IBD) are diseases characterized by inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract, including Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Its prevalence is rising, affecting approximately 100.000 persons in the Netherland alone. Its cause is multifactorial, involving a complex interplay between host genetics, environmental factors including the diet and dysregulated immune responses towards the gut microbiome 

Our aims
-	To further knowledge of the complex etiology of development and course of IBD 
-	To search for predictors of treatment response 
-	To use multi-omics data research of large groups of patients and translate its findings to personalized treatment of individual patients

name: The identification of phenotypes in patients with severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (PULMOLINES - Severe COPD Cohort)
description: The UMCG is an expertise center for servere COPD and has established the Groningen Severe COPD Cohort (GSCC) under the PULMOLINES banner. The main aim of the GSCC cohort is to identify clinical phenotypes and endotypes in patients with severe COPD and to investigate the contribution of (epi)genomics. A total of 1030 patients are included in the GSCC, 121 of which also underwent a bronchoscopy with collection of lung biopsies, lung brushes and nosh brush samples. Future findings of this cohort may lead to earlier identification of subjects at risk for severe COPD, better clinical characterisation of established COPD, and a more tailored treatment of this subgroup.

name: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey (TRAILS)
description: TRAILS (Tracking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey) is an ongoing, multidisciplinary research on the psychological, social and physical development of adolescents and young adults. More than 2700 participants have participated since they were about eleven years old. For over 20 years, these participants have been examined every 2 to 3 years, through questionnaires, interviews, tests and/or physical measurements. Not only the participants provide us with information, but also their family members, teachers and partners. The more recently launched TRAILS Next research focuses on the children of the participants.

name: UMCG-SSc serumbank
description: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune disease that involves vasculopathy, inflammation and fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Its clinical characteristics are heterogenous and feature vascular signs such as Raynaud’s phenomenon, fingertip lesions, telangiectasia, abnormal nail fold capillaries, skin abnormalities such as sclerodactyly and calcinosis cutis, and potentially life-threatening internal organ manifestations such as interstitial lung disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, gastrointestinal tract manifestations, scleroderma renal crisis and cardiopathy. Limited cutaneous (lcSSc), diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc) and sine forms of SSc can progress to severe disease modes with increased morbidity and mortality, but also present as stable conditions. Although advances have been made in biomarker discovery for SSc, it is still difficult to predict which patients are going to progress to severe fibrotic disease for which no disease-modifying treatment is currently available. Interstitial lung disease, a result of inflammatory and fibrosing processes, is the leading cause of mortality (30%) in SSc patients (11) (12). name: UMCG_SSC Systemic Sclerosis Cohort Groningen (SScUMCG)
description: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune disease that involves vasculopathy, inflammation and fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Its clinical characteristics are heterogenous and feature vascular signs such as Raynaud’s phenomenon, fingertip lesions, telangiectasia, abnormal nail fold capillaries, skin abnormalities such as sclerodactyly and calcinosis cutis, and potentially life-threatening internal organ manifestations such as interstitial lung disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, gastrointestinal tract manifestations, scleroderma renal crisis and cardiopathy. Limited cutaneous (lcSSc), diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc) and sine forms of SSc can progress to severe disease modes with increased morbidity and mortality, but also present as stable conditions. Although advances have been made in biomarker discovery for SSc, it is still difficult to predict which patients are going to progress to severe fibrotic disease for which no disease-modifying treatment is currently available. Interstitial lung disease, a result of inflammatory and fibrosing processes, is the leading cause of mortality (30%) in SSc patients (11) (12). Therefore. new treatment strategies are urgently needed to attenuate progression and potentially modify the course of this disease.

name: The Norwegian Childhood Cancer Biobank
description:
Pediatric cancer is the dominant cause of disease-related death in children over one year of age in Western countries. New treatment strategies are warranted, and rapid advancements in molecular and genetic sequencing technologies are realizing the potential for improving care through precision medicine. In pediatric oncology, this encompasses the identification of unique cancer predispositions, somatic tumor mutations, personalized surveillance, and targeted treatment.
The clinical benefits of these scientific advancements rely on the development of translational bioinformatic expertise, clinical pipelines for extended testing and services, and ethically sound information and decision systems for families and healthcare professionals within pediatric oncology.
The Norwegian Childhood Cancer Biobank was established in 2017 as a national initiative to support research and improve outcomes for children with cancer. The biobank collects and provides a broad range of high-quality biological samples, including plasma, serum, buffy coat, bone marrow, cerebrospinal fluid, urine, biopsy, feces, extracted tumor DNA and RNA, extracted genomic DNA (gDNA), and mononuclear cells (MNC) from leukemia patients.
Our goal is to use the generated knowledge toward the establishment of a general translational platform that integrates different molecular modalities, where novel molecular and genetic information is systematically translated into clinical application.
The biobank has also established an advisory board to guide its development and ensure its alignment with clinical and research needs.
